description: A shop located in the promenade at Springfield Heights, $50 Marmalade is featured in the episode "The Girl on the Bus."

A gym in Springfield, it is where Homer attempts to get fit despite not understanding what a gym is. The All Night Gym is frequented by Rainier Wolfcastle and offers a view of the nearby mountains, including the Murderhorn.

The Alkali Flats, also known as the Springfield Badlands, is a desert region in Springfield. It features a building used by Krusty to broadcast his show during a television outage caused by Sideshow Bob.

location_type: Pet store inside the Springfield Mall
description: A pet store located inside the Springfield Mall, it features a sign that reads "You pet it, you bought it." Homer often argues with a bird there, and Lisa purchased a hamster, possibly named Nibbles, which demonstrated its intelligence over Bart. The fate of the store and its animals remains unknown after the mall became abandoned.
A retail shop in Springfield specializes in selling Christmas trees, presumably priced at $75 each. Homer visits this store after losing his bonus to find an affordable tree for Christmas.

A steel mill in Springfield, it employs many openly gay workers and also functions as a nightclub called The Anvil. The Ajax Steel Mill is known for its vibrant atmosphere, where workers celebrate after hours with music and dancing.

An office where Al Simmons and Mike work, it is featured in the episode "Homer's Night Out." In this location, Mike faxes a photo of Homer Simpson and Princess Kashmir to Al, who then calls to thank him.

This large, modern mansion serves as the summer residence for Alec Baldwin and Kim Basinger, hidden in the forest to avoid fans. Homer Simpson discovered the house after an accident and briefly worked as their agent, but he revealed its location to Springfield residents, leading to his dismissal and a restraining order against him.

An education facility in Springfield offers various adult education classes, including one taught by Homer Simpson on the secrets of a successful marriage. Other classes cover topics such as eating oranges, chewing tobacco, and funk dancing for self-defense.
Located at Springfield International Airport, this bar is accessible to all travelers. Barney Gumble has been seen drinking there.

A bus stop is located near the runway of Springfield Airport, known as Airport Refueling Way. Lisa once passed this stop while on a bus ride, realizing she was on the wrong route and ended up far from home.
The aerobic studio is where Marge goes to exercise. In one episode, she discovers a photo of Homer belly dancing with a caption mocking his appearance, which angers her.

A major airline headquartered in Springfield, it operates primarily from Springfield International Airport and is known for its large fleet of Airbus A340 aircraft. The airline has a poor safety record, with pilots reportedly selected from bars and lacking proper identification to access the cockpit.
A perfumery store in Springfield, Abercrombie & Fish sells fragrances made from a unique ingredient called bluella.
Aced Shoe is a shoe shop in Springfield, situated next to a pawn shop.
A clothing shop in Springfield features two skeletons in the windows, likely serving as mannequins. Marge drives by this costume shop on her way to Fiesta Terraces.
Located at the Springfield Heights Promenade, this store is a parody of Abercrombie & Fitch and is likely a clothing retailer. The Simpsons do not visit it during their Christmas shopping.
A shop located in the Springfield Mall, Cookie Colossus specializes in selling cookies. Homer once walked past it and was offered a free sample of macadamia nut cookies by a saleswoman.
A clothing store located on Fifth Avenue in Springfield's Little Ukraine district, it is a pun on Saks Fifth Avenue and references the Cossacks, a group of East Slavic people.

A comic book store in Springfield, Coolsville Comics & Toys is owned by Milo and is located across the street from the Android's Dungeon. It quickly gained popularity among kids for its larger selection and Milo's friendly customer service, contrasting with the indifferent attitude of Comic Book Guy.
A diner in Springfield owned by Cora, it employs mostly ex-convicts and is a popular hangout for the Springfield police force.

A copying and printing center, The Copy Jalopy has the slogan "We tried to make copying fun." Lisa and Homer visited to print fliers revealing the true history of Jebediah Springfield, while Comic Book Guy was there making a copy of his screenplay.

A high-end department store located in downtown Springfield, Costington's is known for its slogan "over a century without a slogan." Owned by Mr. Costington, it has employed various Springfield residents, including Homer Simpson, who worked as a parade Santa and mattress salesman. The store sponsors the annual Thanksgiving Day parade and has been criticized by Lisa Simpson for its revealing fashion in the children's section.
A convenience store in Springfield, Convenience Plus is featured in episodes such as "Homer vs. the Eighteenth Amendment."

A computer repair facility in Springfield, it is humorously referred to as a "hospital" for computers. The location is featured in the episode "Holidays of Future Passed," where a mix-up leads to a character mistakenly going there during a critical moment.

location_type: Regional office serving the embassy in the capital.
description: A consulate building in Springfield, it serves as the regional office for the Swedish embassy. The Simpson family visited the consulate when Homer was convicted of copyright infringement.

A business specializing in brainwashing, Conformco Brain Deprogrammers is a subsidiary of Mrs. Fields' Cookies. Homer and Marge seek its services after Bart leaves home, leading to a mix-up where an employee accidentally kidnaps Hans Moleman, causing him to believe he is Bart.

location_name: Condos at Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne
description: Lenny lives in the condos located at Towne Centre in Springfield. This residential area features various shops and amenities nearby.

A traveling carnival owned by a wealthy Texan, it features attractions like a yard work simulator, the roller coaster "Tooth Chipper," and a rigged ring toss. Bart Simpson once worked there to pay off a debt after accidentally destroying a historical car on display.
A coffeehouse located in the Towne Centre of Springfield, it serves as a local spot for residents to enjoy coffee and snacks.

A mansion where Colonel Burns resides, it features a stall behind it that was once home to Virgil Simpson, who lived there when he was Burns' servant. The manor has hosted events, including a ball attended by Eliza Simpson.

A private school in Springfield, Cloisters Academy offers a quiet campus with amenities like a swimming pool, observatory, and imaginatorium. Lisa Simpson briefly attended the academy, which features a unique setup where each student has their own teacher, but she left after discovering her mother was washing the students' uniforms.

Cold Stone Screamery is depicted as a torture center in the kingdom of Springfieldia, where characters like Hans Moleman have been shown enduring torment. It parodies the American ice cream chain Cold Stone Creamery.

location_name: Coffee Shop (New Kids on the Blecch)
description: A coffee shop is located at Springfield Squidport. It serves various coffee beverages to the residents of Springfield.
This café in Springfield specializes in serving coffee and tea.
Located in the Springfield Mall's food court, this café offers a variety of coffee and snacks for shoppers. It is one of many dining options available in the bustling mall environment.

An antique shop located in the Springfield Mall, Cockamamie's is owned by John. Marge once attempted to sell her grandmother's Civil War doll there, but John revealed it was actually a liquor bottle from the early 1970s.
A coffee shop located in Springfield Heights, it is where Marge had coffee with Patty and Selma before learning that Homer was acting as a wingman.
A store located at Springfield Squidport, it specializes in selling clay jars.

A recording studio in Springfield, Classified Records is where the Party Posse recorded their hit single, "Drop Da Bomb." It has also appeared as a premium building in the mobile game, The Simpsons: Tapped Out.
A nightclub located on East Oak Street, it features performances by dancers, including Nelson's mom in "The Food Wife." Nelson is seen standing outside the establishment in the episode.
A cheap, cut-price supermarket offers low-priced products. Homer once shopped there for Christmas gifts, purchasing items like pantyhose for Marge and a chew toy for Maggie.

A former restaurant located in the Springfield Forest, Clam-Elot Sea-Food was abandoned and became a secret hideout for Kearney, Jimbo, and Dolph. Lisa Simpson and Juliet Hobbes once ran away to this location.
Chupo's Candy Store is a candy store in Springfield owned by Mr. Chupo. It was once robbed by the candy store bandit.

An ear-piercing clinic located inside Springfield Mall, it becomes a Starbucks shortly after Bart visits to get his ears pierced, inspired by Milhouse's popularity. The sarcastic clerk, Raphael, urges Bart to hurry, as the transformation is imminent.

A morgue in Springfield, it is operated by Dr. Julius Hibbert. The single-story red brick building is typically reserved for the recently deceased, although senior citizens sometimes seek refuge there during heatwaves.
The Immigration and Naturalization Service office in Springfield handles immigration laws, including deportation and citizenship tests. Apu became a United States citizen at this location.
A specialist movie theater in Springfield, the IMAX Theater features large-format films. Edna Krabappel and Bart visit to watch the documentary "Nature's Biggest Holes."
An ice cream parlor located in the Towne Centre, it offers a variety of frozen treats to the residents of Springfield.
A tree imagined by Maggie while Marge sang "Rock-a-Bye Baby," where she envisioned herself falling like the baby in the song. This location is part of a non-canonical segment in the series.
A stock exchange located inside the Springfield Mall, I.P.O. Friday's is where Homer once went to buy stock in Animotion.

location_name: I Can't Believe It's A Law Firm!
description: A storefront at Springfield Mall, this law firm is owned by Lionel Hutz and serves as his main office. Hutz has employed a secretary named Della and often offers quirky incentives to attract clients, such as faux pearl necklaces and smoking monkey figures.
A store in Springfield sells returned wedding cakes at a discount. Homer once visited to buy a cake, selecting one with blue rosettes.
A clothing store located in Springfieldia, Hyborian Apparel is featured in the episode "The Serfsons." It is part of a scene where several characters participate in a public stoning.

A house located in the Rat's Nest neighborhood, it is situated next to the rendering plant, resulting in a strong smell of hog fat. Marge and Homer Simpson were shown the house by a realtor, but they ultimately did not purchase it, despite Homer's interest.

A music festival held in Springfield, Hullabalooza features various acts, including Homer Simpson, who became part of the freak show after it was discovered he could withstand cannonball blasts. He eventually had to leave the festival due to health concerns regarding his belly.

A German-cuisine restaurant in East Springfield, The Hungry Hun is known for having the best bratwurst in the area. It is also the location where Hans and Fritz negotiated the purchase of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant from Mr. Burns.
A stall at Springfield Squidport, it sells hot dogs that are often described as cold and droopy. Due to a local law, the seller must shout truthful information about the quality of the hot dogs.

A flower shop in Springfield, Howard's Flowers is known for its expensive roses, prompting Homer to buy just one for Marge. The shop was originally owned by Howard, who passed away in 1999 and was succeeded by his son.
A chain restaurant, Hooters has a location in Springfield where Mrs. Muntz worked. The restaurant is referenced in various episodes, including one where Bart wears a Hooters t-shirt.

A shop that sells a wide variety of house products, including bathtubs, which Homer Simpson once purchased for brewing bootleg alcohol during Prohibition. The store's motto is "Your super super-store store!"

A pharmaceuticals factory, Hotenhoffer Pharmaceuticals is known for its attempt to replicate a drug discovered by Homer Simpson. The company halted production after the drug caused severe side effects, including users' eyes popping out of their sockets.
The hotel is located near Moe's Tavern and next to King Toot's. It frequently appears in establishing shots of Moe's and in scenes set outside the bar.
Horatio McCallister's houseboat is a vessel that he tried to sell to Homer and Marge Simpson, but they declined the offer after discovering the presence of a giant squid in the area.

An ice-skating rink located in Springfield's Little Ukraine district, it is the site where Homer was kidnapped by Viktor and held under the ice. Wayne Slater rescued him by melting the ice and defeating Viktor and his henchmen.

A honey store owned by Captain McCallister, it allowed customers to harvest their own honey, but it was unpopular and ultimately closed due to lack of business. Homer later opened a salon called "Are We Hair Yet?" in the same location.

A computer store in Springfield, it is known for its dishonest sales tactics and overpriced products. Customers are often misled into purchasing expensive machines while being pressured to make quick decisions.

A hunting club operated by Homer, it was established to allow him to serve drinks in his garage. The club features a bar where Marge serves as the barkeep, and it has hosted a performance by the band R.E.M. Although it has only gone hunting once, Homer attempted various strategies to catch a turkey, including using a plate as bait.

Homer and Mindy's Mansion is a non-canon residence where Homer envisions a future with Mindy after being knocked out. In this vision, he sees himself happily living with Mindy, complete with a butler named Jeeves and playing tennis.

An imaginary theme park envisioned by Homer, Homerland features areas like Trampoline World, Muckville USA, and Fort Adventure. Although Homer earns money charging for trampoline access, Marge ultimately makes him stop due to the injuries it causes.
Located at Springfield Squidport, this restaurant features an explorer theme and is inspired by old banana republic stores, complete with a jeep in the front window.

A natural landmark in the Springfield National Forest, Holding Hands Point is a popular spot for couples to sit on stones and hold hands. It is known for a memorable incident involving Lisa spying on Milhouse and Taffy, leading to a series of romantic misunderstandings.

An older version of Springfield Mall, this location features various shops and restaurants. It was the site of a misunderstanding involving Homer, who mistakenly believed a demolitions expert was a terrorist planning to blow it up.

location_name: Homer and Bart's Surveillance Camera Blind Spot
description: A blind spot in the Simpsons' backyard allows townspeople to escape surveillance cameras and have fun. It was notably mentioned when Marge discussed it, leading to Ned Flanders trying to keep his sons Rod and Todd safe from bullies.

An old quarry features a pipe leading to the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Homer and his friends used to swim there, and after discovering a clog in the pipe, Homer accidentally released water that revealed a dead body, later identified as Waylon Smithers, Sr., discarded by Mr. Burns.

A temporary town formed when half of Springfield's citizens seceded due to a dispute over a change in area code, Olde Springfield was home to the wealthier residents. It was separated from New Springfield by a wall of trash and featured notable locations such as Burns Manor, the Kwik-E-Mart, and Channel 6 News.

The Old Springfield Library is the main branch of the public library, featuring a collection of older books. It has undergone a color change from grey to brick red, and is known for its unique offerings, including a variety of literature and even adult content.
An old abandoned warehouse serves as the location where Fat Tony kidnaps Selma, leading to an unexpected romance between them.

An abandoned subway system once operated in Springfield, known for causing earthquakes and having multiple stations, including Elm Street and Springfield Harbor. The fare was five cents when it was active, and it had a total of 15 stops throughout the city.

An elderly Jewish man resides in this house, which is featured when Homer delivers meals on wheels. Although he is typically seen at the Springfield Retirement Castle, it is suggested that he also owns this house.

A seasonal store in Springfield owned by Apu, it specializes in Halloween items. The store faced issues when Apu's seasonal workers began stealing, leading to their dismissal after Homer reported them.

Located outside the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, the old fishin' hole is a polluted river where Bart caught Blinky, a three-eyed fish. The contamination from the power plant has caused mutations in local wildlife.
A pharmacy sells prescription drugs and is where Homer goes to fill his narcolepsy medication. The pharmacist, Candace, asks him out on a date during his visit.

An oil refinery located in West Springfield, it is known for being a dangerous workplace where employees often suffer severe injuries. Homer and Lenny once worked there, leading to a chaotic incident involving a fire and a rescue attempt by Marge and Artie Ziff.

A lake located near the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, it receives waste water from the plant, leading to mutations in local wildlife, including the three-eyed fish named Blinky. The lake is connected to the old fishing hole and Lake Springfield.

A cathedral located in Springfield, it features prominently in a dream sequence where Homer, in a grotesque form, is pushed off the tower by Marge. The location serves as a backdrop for themes of sanctuary and transformation.
A fast food restaurant located in the Springfield Mall food court, Odd Ones offers a variety of quick meal options.
A shop located in the promenade at Springfield Heights, Oceanscapes offers various ocean-themed merchandise.
The Nuclear Power Plant is a key location in Springfield, where Homer Simpson works as a safety technician. It is known for its safety violations and the presence of Mr. Burns, the plant's owner.
Apu briefly replaced the Kwik-E-Mart with the Nude-E-Mart, a unique establishment that combines elements of a convenience store and a strip club, featuring a clothing-optional policy.

A video game arcade located in downtown Springfield, Noise Land Video Arcade is a popular hangout for local youth, particularly Bart and Milhouse. The arcade features a variety of games, including classics and some less favorable titles, and has a VIP section for select customers.

A government plan to convert Springfield's crater into a New Grand Canyon was thwarted by Homer and Bart Simpson, who destroyed the dome intended for the explosion. This event occurred after the Simpson family had escaped to Alaska.

A town formed when half of Springfield's citizens seceded, New Springfield was established due to a dispute over an area code change. Homer Simpson became its first and only mayor, but it eventually became a ghost town after he cut off the water supply, leading to its merger back with Olde Springfield.

The next exit is located 34 miles from Ye Olde Off-Ramp Inn and the Sapphire Lounge, serving as the only alternative route to these establishments. Homer and Marge miss the first exit and take this one instead.

location_name: New Bedlam Rest Home for the Emotionally Interesting
description: A mental institution in Springfield, the New Bedlam Rest Home for the Emotionally Interesting is where Homer was sent after being declared insane for wearing a pink shirt to work. It is referenced in various episodes, including "Stark Raving Dad," and is known for its association with other mental health facilities in the area, such as Calmwood Mental Hospital.
A diner in Springfield, Nighthawk Diner is where Rex Banner celebrated his birthday with Eddie and Lou. It is inspired by Edward Hopper's painting "Nighthawks."
A homeless man living under a bridge in Springfield, he is known as the inventor of New Coke, a product that led to his firing from the Coca-Cola Company due to its unpopularity.

An asylum for children, New Beginnings offers help for those suspected of sociopathic behavior. Bart Simpson is briefly sent there after his parents misinterpret his test results, but he is released when the staff realizes he is a normal child.
A bowling shop located in Springfield, one of its two locations is inside the Springfield Mall. Marge once had to visit both shops due to poor service.
A store located at the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, Neiman Mark-Up is a parody of Neiman Marcus, known for its high-end merchandise.

A middle-class subdivision in Springfield, Pressboard Estates features family houses and streets like Evergreen Terrace, home to the Simpson and Flanders families, and Pikeland Avenue, where the Van Houten family resides. This neighborhood is depicted in various episodes and media, as it includes the iconic 742 Evergreen Terrace.
A video game store in Springfield, Sequel Stop is where Bart Simpson tries to buy a game called "Grand Theft Scratchy." The purchase is interrupted when Marge catches him with the game.

A roadside zoo located in Springfield, the Springfield City Zoo has had incidents of animals escaping. The zoo is featured in various episodes of The Simpsons, including a Treehouse of Horror segment where Bart ends up in a cage with mutated peacocks.

A building that hosts various entertainment events, the Springfield Civic Center has been the venue for award ceremonies, including the Montgomery Burns Award for Outstanding Achievement and the Cartoon Awards, where Abraham Simpson won for outstanding writing.

A prison located in Springfield, it is known for housing inmates like Snake Jailbird. Chief Wiggum once released prisoners to attend a peewee hockey game, despite their refusal to promise good behavior.

Springfield Cemetery is where the residents of Springfield are buried, located next to the Springfield Pet Cemetery and in front of Springfield General Hospital. Notable individuals buried here include Frank Grimes, Maude Flanders, and Bleeding Gums Murphy.
A medical facility in Springfield, the Burn Ward specializes in treating burn victims. It gained attention when Homer Simpson flooded the town, providing relief to the residents.

Springfield Cemetery is the burial site featured in the short "The Funeral," where Hubert Simpson's funeral takes place. It has appeared in several episodes, including "Simpson and Delilah," "Old Money," and "Mother Simpson."

A Christian school in Springfield, it is known for its strict adherence to fundamentalist teachings. Bart Simpson was briefly enrolled there after being expelled from Springfield Elementary, but he was quickly expelled again for singing an inappropriate song during his first day.

The bus station in Springfield serves as a hub for intercity transportation, connecting the town to other locations. Its interior is somewhat run-down, featuring stained seats and litter, along with coin-operated tel-a-chairs for waiting passengers.

Originally a children's hospital, it has been transformed into the Springfield Cosmetic Surgery Clinic. Mayor Joe Quimby oversaw the conversion, and the facility is known for its focus on cosmetic procedures rather than pediatric care.

The Springfield Memorial Bridge is the only road access out of Springfield, often covered in graffiti and frequented by the city's homeless population. It was destroyed by a missile during a failed attempt to stop a comet but was reconstructed shortly after.

A box factory located across from Krusty Lou Studios, it manufactures boxes primarily for shipping nails, although full assembly occurs in Flint, Michigan. The factory is known for its tours, which were once popular among students from Springfield Elementary.
A temple dedicated to meditation and worship, it is where Lisa Simpson explores Buddhism. Inside, she finds Lenny and Carl meditating, and Richard Gere raking sand in a zen garden.

A group dedicated to observing and protecting birds meets at the Springfield Municipal Building, where they have an office space. The society is led by Seymour Skinner and includes members such as Edna Krabappel, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, and Moe Szyslak.

A beach along Springfield's coastline, Springfield Beach is popular for family trips and weddings. Notable events include Kirk and Luann Van Houten's second wedding and Lisa's efforts to care for a stranded whale named Bluella.

A car dealership specializing in Bentley luxury vehicles, it once offered free tickets to a health spa in exchange for test drives, prompting Homer Simpson to pretend to be wealthy for a chance to drive one of the cars.

An amphitheater located inside Jebediah Springfield Park, Springfield Bowl is where Mr. Burns attempted to host a variety show after the town was destroyed by the Lard Lad statue. The design is inspired by the Hollywood Bowl, and it has historical significance for Burns, who had a traumatic experience there as a child.

A building used for holding auctions, the Springfield Auction House is where Bart Simpson famously bought a painting for 23 million dollars before fleeing the scene. The auctioneer also ran off laughing, revealing that no serious bids had been made.

Springfield's American football team is the Springfield Atoms, known for their intense rivalry with the Shelbyville Sharks. The team was controversially relocated from Portland and features standout player Stan Taylor.

An area open to the public, the Springfield Botanical Gardens features rare and exotic plants. It has hosted events such as the McClure-Bouvier wedding and has experienced incidents like a stampede of Springfield residents.

Students at Springfield Barber College train in hair cutting and styling, though their skills are often questionable. Bart receives a free haircut there as part of the family's financial sacrifices for their dog, Santa's Little Helper.
An apartment complex in Springfield, the Springfield Bachelor Apartments was briefly home to Apu after he was kicked out by Manjula for infidelity. Kirk Van Houten also lived across the hall.

An apartment complex in Springfield, Springfield Arms is the residence of Comic Book Guy. The police once raided the building to arrest him for possession of illegal videos, and the Simpson family temporarily stayed there while their home was being fumigated.

A luxury stadium hosts the Springfield Atoms, featuring amenities like a sushi bar, a 60-screen cinema, a museum of tolerance, a day spa, and a zoo with NFL team mascots. It has a retractable roof and a large jumbotron, and is believed to have replaced the Springfield Estadio de Toros.

An arts education center in Springfield, it was mentioned in the news as having burned down in a fire, along with several other local establishments. Its current status after the incident remains unknown.

The Springfield Animal Shelter cares for sick and abandoned animals, often run by a grumpy woman who has a tendency to euthanize them. Marge has taken Lisa there on two occasions to adopt pets, including after the death of Snowball II.

A municipal arboretum in Springfield, it features water lilies that provide a peaceful escape for Martin Prince from bullying at school. The arboretum also contains various trees, which were quickly stripped of their leaves by Stampy.

An aqua-car factory existed in Springfield during the 1950s, known as Springfield Aqua-Cars. It was the state's first factory dedicated to producing amphibious vehicles that could operate both on land and in water, resembling the real-life Amphicar.
An antique shop located in Springfield, it is known for a fight between Homer Simpson and Tom that resulted in the destruction of its sign.

An armory located in Springfield, it is known for being the launch site of a rocket built by Professor Frink to destroy a comet threatening the town, although it ultimately missed and struck Springfield Bridge instead.

An animal refuge designed to provide better lives for animals held in captivity, it features open fields resembling their natural habitats. The Simpson family donated Stampy, the elephant, to this refuge.

Jebediah Springfield, originally named Hans Sprungfeld, is the legendary founder of Springfield, known for his supposed heroic deeds, including killing a bear with his bare hands. A statue of him stands in the town square, depicting him triumphantly with his foot on a bear's head, although historical accounts of his life reveal a more controversial and dubious past as a pirate and enemy of George Washington.

The main post office in Springfield is known for its high volume of undelivered mail, with workers sometimes searching through letters for money. It is also a common field trip destination for Springfield Elementary School.
A street in Springfield, Sycamore Avenue is mentioned in an episode where Lisa listens to various bus stop names. It is also noted for its treehouses.
A factory in Springfield during the early twentieth century, it was owned by Montgomery Burns and featured an atom smashing building where employees worked.

A healthy convenience store in Springfield, Swapper Jack's became popular after opening, attracting customers away from the Kwik-E-Mart. Apu, feeling betrayed, confronted Homer and later attempted to rob the store, but was dissuaded by Snake Jailbird, who worked there. After a brief closure due to a scandal involving monkey meat, the store reopened with a live performance by Krusty the Clown.

An exclusive hotel in Springfield, Swell-Air Hotel was the intended venue for Marge and Homer's third wedding, which was disrupted by Homer's mysterious disappearance. The hotel is linked to a keychain with the initials S.B., initially leading Bart and Lisa to suspect Sideshow Bob, but the keys actually belong to Selma Bouvier.
A shop located in the Springfield Mall, it is where Mr. Burns searched for a gift for the Simpsons. The name references the famous Lynyrd Skynyrd song "Sweet Home Alabama."
A bartending university in Springfield, Swigmore University is where Moe obtained his degree in bartending before opening Moe's Tavern.

A bridge in Springfield, known as Suicide Bridge, is where Homer contemplates suicide after mistakenly believing Marge is cheating on him. The bridge is dedicated to Chester L. Suicide and features in the episode "Eternal Moonshine of the Simpson Mind."

A construction company in Springfield, Surly Joe's Foundation Repair specializes in repairing building foundations and is the only one of its kind in town. Owned by Surly Joe, the company is known for its high prices, as seen when it charged the Simpson family $8,500 to fix the sinking west side of their home.

A music and poster shop specializing in alternative music, it is known for its indifferent and sarcastic teenage employees. Homer visited while searching for a Bread album and was surprised to find a Styx record in the oldies bin, highlighting the staff's lack of knowledge about classic bands.

A record shop in Springfield, Styx and Stones Records features customers listening to Homer's song "Everybody Hates Ned Flanders." The store's name references the rock bands Styx and The Rolling Stones, as well as the nursery rhyme "sticks and stones may break my bones."
A store located in the Springfield Mall, Stuff-N-Hug allows customers to create and customize their own stuffed animals.
A dangerous and underdeveloped road off Rural Route 9, Suicidal Moron Pass features hills, a forest, animals, and a cliff. Homer and Marge have both taken this shortcut home.
A coffee shop in Springfield, Stuckey's is where Marge, Ned, and Timothy Lovejoy discussed Bart's and Homer's conversion to Catholicism.

A '70s-style disco club, it is likely owned by Disco Stu and features a windowless brick exterior with a large neon sign. Inside, the club has a purple gridded floor, dark green walls, and serves drinks like shot glasses and margaritas, while playing looped instrumental disco music.

A kitchenware store in Springfield, Stoner's Pot Palace is known for misleading customers with its name, leading some, like Otto, to expect a head shop. Marge has purchased items such as a juice bowl from the store.

A storage locker in Springfield, Stor-U-Stuff is where Seymour Skinner kept some of his personal belongings after being exposed as a fraud. The real Seymour Skinner later retrieved his items from the locker before leaving for Capital City.

A restaurant in Springfield, Streami's caters to podcasters and features walls adorned with pictures of notable figures in the podcasting world. Kent Brockman has been seen socializing there with various podcast personalities.

A children's theme park for ages 1 to 7, Storytown Village featured animatronic storybook characters, a petting zoo, and a ferris wheel. It closed after a tragic incident and was later converted into a Christian theme park called Praiseland, which also eventually shut down due to a gas leak.
A Strategic Air Command base is located in Springfield, known as the Springfield Station. It plays a role in the episode "Gone Boy."
The Stonecutters Lodge serves as the headquarters for the Stonecutters, a secret society comprised mainly of male citizens of Springfield. Members gather at this lodge for their meetings.

A daycare center owned by the Stonecutters was established after Homer became the chosen one, as a way for the organization to give back to the community. Some members of the Stonecutters have worked there.

Located in Springfield Town Square, the statue depicts Jebediah Springfield, the town's founder, standing over a bear he allegedly killed. The statue has been the center of various incidents, including Bart Simpson stealing its head, which led to public outrage.
A steel mill factory in Springfield is responsible for producing steel and has contributed to environmental issues, such as acid rain, affecting the area.
A plastic surgery office visited by Marge Simpson, it parodies the Staples Center in Los Angeles.
A motel in Springfield, the Starlight Motel is often frequented by Mayor Quimby and his girlfriend.

A restaurant in Springfield, Taj Mah-All-You-Can-Eat is where Homer once indulged in a massive amount of food while being secretly filmed for a television show. The establishment's name is a play on the Taj Mahal.

A restaurant and gas station, the Seething Sisters is where Ruth Powers and Marge Simpson stop to eat and use the phone while evading the police. The establishment is known for its patrons' mantra, "friends stick together," which influences Marge's decision to continue running from the law with Ruth.

A software company formerly owned by Artie Ziff, Ziffcorp produced products like the Snore Converter and a device that turns computer noise into music. The company ultimately failed due to Ziff's extravagant spending, leading to his legal troubles and a loss of ownership to Homer Simpson in a poker game.

A pizza restaurant and arcade in Springfield, it features various games, including a skateboarding game. Principal Skinner once arranged for Bart to take Melody there while he spent time with Calliope Juniper.
A restaurant in Springfield, Zesty's serves pizza and subs and is known for having the world's first crustless pizza. It is one of the many establishments located in the town square.
Zip Boys is a shop featuring mascots of the same name. It is known for its involvement in a chaotic scene where the mascots come to life and become aggressive.

A mansion owned by Artie Ziff, it was the setting for a senior prom that Artie organized to show Marge what her life could have been like with him. The mansion later appears when Artie's possessions are repossessed, highlighting his fall from grace.
Zechariah Springfield is the son of Jebediah Springfield and the older brother of Obadiah Springfield. He was born in the Shelbyville hospital.
A photo kiosk located in the Springfield Heights Promenade, it features a picture of Moe Szyslak, who had his portrait done there. The Simpson family visited this kiosk while Christmas shopping.
A Thai restaurant in Springfield, You Thai Now is owned by Mr. Thai, who once hired Bart to distribute menus around town to help fund his daughters' education.
One of Mayor Quimby's many mistresses, she was seen with him at the Who's to Know Motel, where he offered to name a street after her.

An inn located in Springfield, Ye Olde Off-Ramp Inn hosted the Little Miss Springfield pageant and served as temporary accommodation for the Simpson family after their house was infested with termites. It has appeared in various episodes of the series and in video games, including The Simpsons: Hit & Run.
Located inside Springfield Mall, this yogurt store is situated next to a law firm. Yogurt Nook participated in the Taste of Springfield outdoor food festival.
A gift shop in Springfield that sells inexpensive items, You Forgot-Me-Nots is where Bart went to find a present for Lisa. The shop is staffed by a character named Wiseguy.
A joke shop in Springfield, it specializes in novelty and prank products, including itching powder and x-ray specs. The name parodies Buckingham Palace.

A tavern located in Bloodbath Gulch, this saloon features animatronic robots that represent old west characters. Homer is dismayed to find that it does not serve alcohol, and after he punches one of the robots, chaos ensues as the machines begin to malfunction and attack.
A historic candle shop located in Olde Springfield Towne, it was briefly worked at by Homer Simpson in 1980, who was fired for making a disfigured candle that offended tourists.
A butcher shop in Springfield, Ye Old Butcher Shoppe is where a steak was once put out for Santa's Little Helper and She's the Fastest during a walk.
A Christmas tree lot sells mutant Christmas trees. Homer passes by it while searching for a tree.
A yarn shop located in Springfield, the Yarn Barn is notable for an incident where a Duff racer crashed into the building after a cat from the Crazy Cat Lady distracted the driver.

An internet café in Springfield, it attracts many nerds, including characters like Database and Report Card. However, insect-like individuals such as the Human Fly and Bumblebee Man dislike it due to the computer network resembling a spider web that entangles them.
A store that specializes in selling harpsichords, it is notable for the sounds produced by the instruments during a hurricane that struck Springfield.

A specialist maritime store in Springfield features anchors in its front display window. It is known for its appearance during the Springfield monorail incident, where Captain McCallister criticized Homer's makeshift anchor.
A rundown hotel in Springfield, the Worst Western features rented sheets and cardboard box furniture. It serves as a residence for Roger Meyers Jr. after the bankruptcy of Itchy & Scratchy Studios.
A hotel in Springfield, the Woosterfield Hotel is owned by the affluent Woosterfield family and is located at 35 City London Road. Lenny once hosted a party there after winning the lottery.

A program designed to help victims of crime relocate and assume new identities, the witness relocation program moved the Simpson family to Terror Lake after Bart received threats from Sideshow Bob. Homer had difficulty adjusting to his new identity and inadvertently revealed his association with the program.

The shack serves as the home of Groundskeeper Willie, located on the playground of Springfield Elementary School. It has been destroyed multiple times, often due to Bart's pranks, and at one point, Willie had a girlfriend named Inga who lived there.
A hat shop in Springfield, The Wooly Bully is where Jimbo purchases his purple toboggans.

Chief Clancy Wiggum is the head of the Springfield Police Department, characterized as a lazy and incompetent officer with a fondness for donuts. He often flaunts his authority despite being uninformed about the law and is known for his corrupt practices, including accepting bribes. Wiggum is frequently assisted by his more competent officers, Eddie and Lou.

Ralph Wiggum is a major character in The Simpsons, known as the son of Chief Wiggum and Sarah Wiggum, and a student at Springfield Elementary School. He is portrayed as a well-meaning boy with learning and social disabilities, often exhibiting quirky behavior and a surprising potential for performance.

A shop that sells wind chimes is located near Springfield Beach. The owner experienced a breakdown due to the constant chiming, and Marge accidentally burned it down while rushing home after receiving an invitation to Costa Rica.
West Oak Street is located in the Springfield Heights area and features businesses such as El Chemistri, The Fifth Helping, Vulgari, and Monoclecrafters. It runs parallel to East Oak Street.

The second highest mountain in Springfield, Widow's Peak has an elevation of 13,613 feet and is known for heavy snowfall, making it prone to avalanches. Homer once rescued Barney from an avalanche on the mountain after a prank call led Barney to a fake plowing job there.
Located inside Springfield Mall, Wicked Excess is a store that offers a variety of upscale and trendy electronics, appliances, furniture, and novelty items.

An elementary school located in West Springfield, it shares the same floor plan as Springfield Elementary School. Notably, it offers French classes, which Lisa Simpson discovers after mistakenly attending the school.
The western region of Springfield is known as West Springfield.
A motel in Springfield, it is featured in the episode "Separate Vocations," where Mayor Quimby attempts to gain votes by asking a young woman if she wants a street named after her.

A supermarket in Springfield, Wellness Foods specializes in organic products that spoil quickly. It promotes the use of reusable grocery bags and features a selection of magazines focused on health and sustainability.
Located on Fast Food Boulevard, this restaurant features restrooms and is known for its brief appearance in "E. Pluribus Wiggum" and "The Simpsons Movie."

An island off the coast of Springfield, Weasel Island is known for its round shape and is home to a population of weasels, a historic Civil War prison, and a dilapidated amusement park. Access to the island is only possible via the Island Queen ferry.
A bridal shop in Springfield, Wed Lobster is where Marge purchased a dress for her and Homer's third wedding. The name is a pun on the seafood restaurant Red Lobster.

A cannabis store in Springfield, Well & Good offered a variety of cannabis products, including lollipops, candles, and sodas. The store was affected by the re-criminalization of marijuana in the state following an incident involving Homer.

An upper-class district of Springfield, Waverly Hills features an upscale elementary school that Bart and Lisa attended. While most residents are relatively well-off, some, like those living in the Royal Waverly Apartments, are exceptions.

Springfield's waterfront is a boardwalk area that features various businesses and was once the center of a squid-gutting industry. It was revitalized with the construction of the South Street Squidport and is known for Mr. Burns' casino, which briefly operated there.
A clothing store located in the Springfield Mall, Wee Madame specializes in girls' clothing.
A jewelry store chain with locations in Springfield, Vulgari is a parody of the luxury brand Bulgari. It is situated on West Oak Street and in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne.

A storage and shipping facility in Springfield, the warehouse appears disheveled and unkempt on the outside, leading Homer Simpson and Larry Burns to mistakenly believe it is abandoned. However, it is fully functional on the inside.
Waylon Smithers resides in a house located in the Springfield Heights district.

A family entertainment restaurant in downtown Springfield, Wall E. Weasel's offers food and activities geared towards children, including arcade games, skee ball, a basketball game, a ball pit, and a whac-a-mole-style game called Whack-a-Weasel. The venue features poorly-maintained animatronic puppets, including Wal E. Weasel and Signor Beaverotti, who perform for birthday parties.
Located in the Springfield Mall, this clothing store parodies The Gap and is named Wage Gap.
A theater in Springfield, the Walter R. Bridgetunnel Theatre is featured in episodes such as "Lisa with an S" and "Springfield Splendor."

A video dating service operates in Springfield, where Homer once created a videotape of Ned Flanders to help him find dates, though the results were disappointing. Comic Book Guy is a frequent visitor, often checking out videos of women.
A parlor that operated in Springfield during the 1940s or 1950s, the Vinegar Parlor likely closed as the town's economic conditions worsened.
A video shop in Springfield, Video Village is where an employee once put out a steak for Santa's Little Helper and a greyhound during their walk.

A clothing store frequented by Homer, who visited to change his outfit while living with Julio and Grady. He struggled with his belly size, ultimately resorting to wearing a belt to keep his shirt in place.

An apartment block located in a gay neighborhood, it is home to Julio and Grady. Homer briefly lived there as a roommate after a conflict with Marge, where he learned about gay culture before ultimately leaving after an awkward encounter with Grady.

A building in Springfield where war veterans gather to share their experiences, the Veterans of Popular Wars Hall has hosted various veterans, including Abraham Simpson II and Jasper Beardly. Bart Simpson once reported on a flag-making event there, which frustrated his sister Lisa.
A clothing store that parodies Victoria's Secret, Victarion's Secret offers women's apparel in Springfield.

A men's clothing store located at the Springfield Heights Promenade, Victor's Secret features a memorable scene where Marge has two salesmen try on oversized underwear for Homer during her Christmas shopping. The salesmen fold the underwear like a flag and place it in a small box, cautioning Marge to be careful when opening it.

A video store in Springfield, VHS Village was formerly known as the Beta Barn. It offers a variety of titles, including sports, foreign films, and action thrillers, and carries at least one McBain movie.
A house was targeted by Ms. Lucille Botzcowski, known as the Babysitter Bandit, who stole all their valuables. It was featured in the episode "Some Enchanted Evening."

A building in Springfield where war veterans gather to share their experiences, the Veterans of Unpopular Wars Hall features a tavern called The Voum. Notable discussions have included stories from veterans of various conflicts, including humorous and contentious anecdotes about their service.

A fast-food restaurant located on Fast-Food Boulevard, Vesuvius Pizza featured a volcano on its roof that erupted tomato sauce. It was destroyed by a gas explosion, resulting in pizza batter being sprayed over the crowd, except for Hans Moleman, who was crushed by falling debris while trying to get free food.
A park in Springfield, it honors veterans and is featured in the episode "Bart's Girlfriend."

A clothing store located in the Springfield Mall, it specializes in apparel for obese men, offering items like ponchos, muumuus, and jumpsuits. Homer once visited the store to find comfortable clothing after gaining weight to work from home, ultimately choosing a muumuu for its loose fit.

The Van Houten House, located at 316 Pikeland Avenue, is a pink residential home where Kirk, Luann, and their son Milhouse live, along with Milhouse's Shih Tzu and Taquito. It is situated down the street from the Simpson's house and next to Elizabeth Hoover's house.

A storage room located in the school, Utility Basement B was used by Principal Skinner to trap Bart and his friends under the pretense of giving them mountain bikes during a school inspection. They remained locked inside for an extended period before eventually escaping.

A recycling center in Springfield, Uriah's Heap Recycling Center is where students from Springfield Elementary take their recyclables. Despite collecting six bags, they received only $0.75, which was insufficient to cover the costs of their planned field trip.

An advertising company, Van Brunt & Churchill specializes in creating giant figures for advertisements. These figures can come to life and caused chaos in Springfield when Homer Simpson stole Lard Lad's donut, but the town managed to stop them by ignoring their antics.
An outhouse store located in Springfield, Urban Outhouses is a parody of Urban Outfitters. It appears in the episode "The Serfsons."

A buffet restaurant shaped like an airplane, it offers a unique dining experience that simulates eating during a flight. Located near the Gilded Truffle, it features turbulence effects and keeps silverware in luggage compartments. Homer and Marge visited the restaurant on their wedding anniversary after a babysitting mix-up.

This district in Springfield is where Marge grew up and includes notable locations such as the Bouvier house, a 7-Eleven, a McDonald's, and a food bank that was formerly a bank. The area reflects Marge's past, including her academic achievements as revealed when the Simpson family visited her old home.
An alleyway in Springfield connects Evergreen Terrace to the street ahead. It appears in the episode "Marge Be Not Proud" as a dirty alley, contrasting with its cleaner depiction in the show's intro.

The University of Minnesota Spankalogical Protocol is a controversial treatment involving eight months of continuous spanking sessions, which Ned Flanders underwent as a child to control his behavior. This method ultimately backfired, leading to repressed anger that manifested in irrational outbursts later in life, prompting Ned to seek help at Calmwood Mental Hospital, where he learned healthier ways to express his emotions.

The unincorporated part of Springfield connects Evergreen Terrace with Springshire. It features a forested area where Marge and Bart ride a tandem bike, encountering various characters like Reverend Lovejoy and Cletus during their journey.

A family restaurant that Moe Szyslak transformed from his tavern, Uncle Moe's Family Feedbag initially attracted customers with promotions like million dollar birthday fries and a guarantee of free food if he wasn't smiling at the check. However, after a negative incident with a young customer, the restaurant reverted back to Moe's Tavern.

A daycare center was established by Homer Simpson in his home after he injured his leg and was unable to work. Initially successful and popular with neighborhood children, it ultimately closed down after a disastrous incident at an awards ceremony where Homer embarrassed himself in front of the audience.
A beauty parlor in Springfield, it is where Marge took Lisa to try out various hairstyles for the Little Miss Springfield beauty pageant. The name is a pun on the phrase "turn your head and cough."
A store that sells turbans, Turban Outfitters is located at Springfield Squidport. The name is a pun on Urban Outfitters.
A truck rental service where Bart once rented a truck, U Tote is a parody of U-Haul.

The U.S. Air Force Base in Springfield serves as a military installation for the Air Force, featuring a nuclear warhead storage facility, hangars, and a command office led by Colonel Leslie Hapablap. It is known for hosting air shows and has been the site of various incidents, including Sideshow Bob's failed attempt to use an outdated atomic bomb to threaten the town.
A dry-cleaning service located across the street from Moe's Tavern.

A coffee shop located in Springfield's Little Ukraine, Tsarbucks is a parody of Starbucks. It is mentioned in the episode "The Falcon and the D'ohman," where Wayne Slater passes by while on a mission to rescue Homer.

A private all-girls school in Springfield, Tuition Academy is known for being a scholarship-free environment. It is first seen when Lisa waits for her friend Juliet Hobbes, who is a known student there.

Trappuccino refers to a crisis in Springfield when a dome was placed over the city by Russ Cargill and the EPA due to Homer Simpson contaminating Lake Springfield. The event lasted 100 days and was dubbed "Trappuccino" by Channel 6 News, ultimately ending when Homer and Bart thwarted Cargill's plan to destroy the town.
A grocery store specializing in organic food, Trader Earth's is where the Springfield Democrats held a meeting. It is a parody of Trader Joe's.

A fish farm in Springfield, the trout hatchery is where trout are bred. It is featured in the episode "The Last Temptation of Homer," where Homer crashes into the facility while distracted by his thoughts.
A retail shop sells Christmas trees priced at $60 and above. Homer drives past it while heading to cut down a tree from the forest.

A toy store in Springfield, based on the real-life Toys 'R' Us chain, was closed after Moe changed the sign. The store is referenced in the episode "D'oh Canada," where the Simpsons pass by the closed location.
A toy store located in the Springfield Mall, it serves as a parody of Toys "R" Us, which has gone out of business.
A toy store located in Springfield's Chinatown, it parodies the Toys "R" Us chain.

A shop located in the Springfield Mall, it sells toys and is situated between the Popcorn Shack and Dr. Zitsofsky's Dermatology Clinic. Marge, Lisa, and Maggie have visited this store while Christmas shopping, but they only looked without making any purchases.
A narrow-gauge rail vehicle transports people around the Towne Centre. It should not be confused with the Li'l Lisa mini-train, which also operated in the area.
A toy factory located in Springfield, Toy Town is seen during a school trip taken by Edna Krabappel's students.

A new outdoor shopping mall in Springfield features a variety of parody stores and a trolley for easier navigation. It includes dining areas, dancing waters, and shops like Cinnabun, Cookie Mart, and the Leftorium Express.

Toys 'N' Stuff is a toy store located near Springfield Town Square. It appears in the video game "The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants," where it serves as a location for Bart to purchase items needed for gameplay.

A group of Springfield citizens is responsible for upholding the legacy of the town's founder, Jebediah Springfield, by organizing events like the bicentennial parade and appointing the town crier. Key members include Mayor Quimby, Police Chief Wiggum, Reverend Lovejoy, Principal Skinner, and Dr. Hibbert, although some members do not take their roles seriously.
A store located near Springfield Town Square, Top It Off is featured in several episodes of The Simpsons, including "Marge in Chains" and "Homer vs. the Eighteenth Amendment."
Tony's is a restaurant located near Springfield Town Square. It is featured in the episode "Homer vs. the Eighteenth Amendment."

A tool shop located near Springfield Town Square, Tool World is featured in the video game "The Simpsons: Bart vs. the Space Mutants." It is one of the storefronts where Bart can purchase items, including a key and a wrench, to complete tasks in the game.
A thrift shop in Springfield sells cheap and used items.
A toupee shop in Springfield, it is where Homer goes to get a wig identical to his old hair after Mr. Burns and the Rich Texan pluck out his hair for a scavenger hunt.
A district of Springfield located next to Chinatown, Tibet Town is a locked alley surrounded by barbed wire. Residents report constant harassment from the neighboring Chinatown.
A camping goods store located in the Springfield Mall, Tommy Hillclimber is a pun on the clothing brand Tommy Hilfiger.

A commercial rose garden is located near Evergreen Terrace, where Homer Simpson was once forced through the bushes. This incident led to him accidentally delivering roses to Marge, ultimately saving their marriage.
Located at the Springfield Heights Promenade, this store sells a variety of unnecessary and overpriced merchandise. Homer once purchased an astrolabe from there.

A store located in Springfield Mall, it serves as a parody of Foot Locker and features bullies as employees. Bart and Milhouse once encountered the bullies there, leading to a confrontation that resulted in the bullies getting revenge on them.

location_name: The Webs at Giant Spider Acres
description: A retirement forest located in Springfieldia, it is known as a place where residents like Abraham Simpson II and Jacqueline Bouvier have lived. The Serfson family visited to pick up Jacqueline from this location.
A motel in Springfield, the Starlight Motel is notable for its bright sign that once interrupted Lisa's stargazing. It has been featured in the episode "'Scuse Me While I Miss the Sky."

The Springfield Shopper Building, located at 314 Dutch Elm Street, serves as the headquarters for the Springfield Shopper, the town's most popular newspaper. Homer Simpson once became a food critic for the paper after attending a retirement party, leading to various comedic misadventures involving his family and the newspaper's staff.
A shop that specializes in selling harmonicas, it gained attention when a hurricane caused the instruments to produce sound due to the strong winds.
A tabloid magazine in Springfield, the Springfield Inquisitor is known for sensational stories and gossip. The Simpsons once sold a photo of Duffman and Booberella to the magazine to pay off a bill.
A group of three teenage girls practices witchcraft in the forest. They are known as the Wiccans.

location_name: The Sea Cap'n's Bait 'n' Baron B'n
description: A shop located at Springfield's docks, it is run by the Sea Captain and sells bait along with various aquatic items, such as ships in bottles. Handsome Pete is known to perform there.

A party hall frequented by celebrities, it is located across the road from Moe's Tavern. The Snub Club serves as a venue for celebrations, where characters like Rainier Wolfcastle and Krusty have been seen, and it plays a role in various events involving Homer and the celebrity community.

A bus service catering to the elderly, the Seniorville Trolley is likely associated with the Springfield Retirement Castle. It is featured in the episode "Lady Bouvier's Lover," where Jacqueline Bouvier and Abraham Simpson II board the bus after an aborted wedding.

A secret location within Springfield Elementary School, this refuge is used by nerds to escape bullies. Bart Simpson is welcomed here by Martin Prince and other members, where they engage in activities that often attract the attention of bullies.

Located in Springfield Heights, this sub-district features various shops, including a cultural artifacts store and a pet costume shop. Lisa visits her friend Sam Monroe here, and the area offers free parking for the first hour.

A fine dining restaurant in Springfield, The Pimento Grove is popular among local and visiting celebrities, with framed photos of them adorning the walls. The restaurant features a posh interior with dark red carpeting and a dark olive green exterior, and it was established in the 1990s.

location_name: The Rolling Stones Rock N' Roll Fantasy Camp
description: A rock camp run by the Rolling Stones, where Homer and other Springfield citizens learn music from famous artists like Mick Jagger and Tom Petty. Participants are taught various rock skills, including guitar techniques and stage presence.
A pharmaceutical and medical research laboratory in Springfield, the Pharm Team develops the behavior modification drug Focusyn, which is prescribed to Bart.

An unincorporated region beyond Springfield, the Outlands is inhabited by society rejects who value anarchy and freedom from government oversight. The Simpsons initially settled there after being expelled from Springfield, but the community eventually transformed into a replica of their former home as many Springfield residents moved in.
A vegan fast food restaurant located in the Springfield Mall food court, The Picky Vegan offers plant-based options for diners.

A hair salon located inside the Springfield Mall, the Perm Bank is where Marge Simpson occasionally gets her hair done. Homer once attempted to cut her hair there, but his efforts only resulted in Marge's anger.
A future version of Springfield Elementary has been converted into residential lofts, with Elder Skinner as the landlord. Mooch Bart is one of the residents, living in what was once room 203.

A small bar located at Springfield International Airport, it is exclusively for pilots and those who have played pilot-themed games on TV. Homer visits after being banned from Moe's and pretends to be a pilot, ultimately being chosen to fly when the airport needs one.
A sewing store in Springfield, it has the motto "We mean sewing." Marge and Sherri and Terri's mother visit to sew, while Lisa arrives late due to a date.

A store in the Springfield Mall, the Leftorium specializes in products for left-handed people and is owned by Ned Flanders. Initially struggling, the store faced competition from larger retailers and eventually went out of business due to the rise of online shopping, leading Flanders to become a fourth-grade teacher at Springfield Elementary.
A fine dining restaurant in downtown Springfield, The Loin King features a name that is a pun on The Lion King. Homer once met with the mayor there while he was working as an accountant.
An apartment building in Springfield, The Lonely Arms is home to Lenny Leonard. Homer once visited Lenny there while searching for an old ballot box from high school.
The headquarters for Springfield's branch of the United States Navy serves as a recruitment center where potential recruits fill out questionnaires to be considered for naval positions.

location_name: The League of Extra Horny Gentlemen
description: A gay bar located opposite Moe's Tavern, this establishment is known as the League of Extra Horny Gentlemen. It features prominently in various episodes of The Simpsons and is a nod to the movie The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen.

An internet café located in Springfield, the Java Server first appeared in "Thirty Minutes Over Tokyo." It was the site of a robbery by Snake, who stole money from Homer's bank account, and is featured in the video game "The Simpsons: Hit & Run" where players race to reach it first.
An Afghan-themed restaurant in Springfield, The Kabuli Palow is visited by Marge, Bart, and Lisa Simpson when they explore food blogging.
A shop located in the promenade at Springfield Heights, the Jogging Stroller-y specializes in selling jogging strollers.
A strip club located in Springfield, The Horny Toad is situated near other adult establishments like Nudes at Eleven and Adam & Adam.

A shelter for homeless individuals in Springfield, it is run by Ned Flanders and was founded by Father James Helter. Homer once volunteered there, leading to a memorable moment when he served soup at an impressive speed, which was captured in a newspaper photo.

A motel in Springfield, the Happy Earwig Motel is where Homer and Marge hire a worker to brainwash Bart into returning home, but the treatment mistakenly affects Hans Moleman instead. It is suggested that this location is one of the many places Mayor Joe Quimby uses for his affairs.

An apartment building in Springfield, The Happy Gypsy was where Mr. Bergstrom lived during his time in the city. Lisa met a young woman here who informed her that Mr. Bergstrom had moved to Capital City.
A sports bar located in downtown Springfield, The Gridiron is situated across the street from P.F. Wang's, a gay bar.
A prominent attraction in Springfield, the Great Tire Fire is known for its constant smell of burning tires. It serves as a notable landmark in the town.
A pony farm and stables located on Route 401, it is owned by Millicent, who offers lessons on riding and grooming. Homer buys Lisa a pony from here for $5,000, with a monthly stable fee of $530.
A luxury hotel that parodies the Ritz-Carlton, it is featured in the episode "Top Goon," where Fat Tony and the Springfield mafia hold Toot hostage in a backroom.
A golfing shop is situated in the promenade on the Grove at Springfield Heights.
A sex shop located in Springfield, The Elegant Scoundrel is where Homer purchases various sex merchandise in an attempt to win back Marge's affection.
A jeweler located inside the Springfield Mall, The Family Jewels is where Homer purchases Marge's wedding ring and Seymour Skinner buys Patty's engagement ring.

location_name: The Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers
description: An exclusive club formed by former stonecutters, the Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers is located in an abandoned store. The club prohibits members named Homer, leading to a humorous encounter when Homer Simpson attempts to join.

A cannabis-based spa founded by Drederick Tatum was destroyed by a fire after Homer mistakenly tried to smoke pot there. The firefighters who responded appeared high due to the spa's cannabis content.

location_name: The Brushes are Coming, The Brushes are Coming
description: A shop located in the Springfield Mall, it specializes in selling brushes and brooms. Mr. Burns and Smithers visited this store while searching for a gift for Homer.

A restaurant in Springfield, The Cloth Napkin is where Edna and Moe dined during their dating period. It is notable for a confrontation between Moe and Homer, Lenny, Carl, and Barney, who were upset about Moe closing his tavern.
A prank store located at the Towne Centre in Springfield, it offers a variety of slingshots and novelty items. Lisa once considered buying a gift for Bart from this store while Christmas shopping.
A large building in Springfield shaped like the letter "T" was considered by residents as a potential hiding place for hidden money mentioned by Molloy, but it was ultimately not the location.
A Thai restaurant in Springfield, Thai Palace was introduced to Homer Simpson by Trent Steele, who treated the entire Simpson family to dinner there.
A large cliff face located next to Springfield National Forest, Tenderfoot Gorge is where the Simpsons accidentally drove their RV off the edge.

Located in Little Bangkok, the Thai Food Factory was formerly a Petco and is known for its peanut shrimp. Bart and Principal Skinner once battled on a catwalk there, which collapsed, causing them to fall into the vat and trigger their allergies.
A gas station chain located on the edge of Springfield, Texxon features a giveaway event called "Texxon presents... happy little elves!" The name is a pun on Texaco and Exxon.
An arcade and sports arena in downtown Springfield, it features a batting cage and a large arcade filled with prizes. The Squeaky-Voiced Teen works at the ticket counter.
A facility in Springfield dedicated to producing possums. It is known as Tetanus Terminal.

A facility exists where suspended teachers must report until their cases are heard by the school board, while still receiving their pay. It is located approximately 500 feet from a school and is described as quite plain, with teachers allowed to leave during certain hours each day.
Located at Springfield Squidport, this cannery presumably processes tentacles for various products. It is featured in the episode "My Sister, My Sitter."

Located in Itchy & Scratchy Land, this restaurant features a menu with violent-themed food items, such as the "Brain Burger" and "Eyeball Stew." The unusual names initially disturb Marge, but Bart explains the gimmick, which also includes dishes like "Baby Guts" veal.
The local synagogue in Springfield is Temple Beth Springfield, located in the lower east side. Rabbi Hyman Krustofsky, Krusty the Clown's father, served as the rabbi here until his death.
A hobby shop located in downtown Springfield, it is where Lisa and Homer go to buy a telescope. The name is a reference to the song "Baba O'Riley" by The Who.
The Taylor House is the residence of Allison Taylor and her father, Mr. Taylor. Allison's room is decorated with numerous trophies and awards, which Lisa becomes envious of during her visit.

Spud is a carny and the son of Cooder. During a carnival visit, Homer and Bart get involved with the carnies, leading to chaos that forces the Simpsons to temporarily live in Bart's treehouse before reclaiming their home through a rigged ring toss game.
A tattoo parlor located on D Street, it is featured in the episode "Moaning Lisa."
A health spa located in Springfield, Stagnant Springs Health Spa is known for attracting notable visitors, including Tom Brokaw.

A clothing store for orphans located in the Springfield Mall, Tatters offers a variety of apparel for children in need. Bart and Milhouse have been seen passing by this store during their visits to the mall.

A popular coffee shop chain, Starbucks has multiple locations within the Springfield Mall. In one instance, Bart Simpson noticed that several shops were being converted into Starbucks, highlighting the chain's rapid expansion.

location_name: Squeaky Farms Brand Genuine Animal Milk
description: A rat milking company owned by Fat Tony sold rat milk to Springfield Elementary School under the guise of providing dog milk or better. The operation was shut down after Homer exposed the scheme, leading to Fat Tony's arrest and the release of the milking rats into Springfield.
The house is owned by Stacy Lovell, who is known for her connection to the Malibu Stacy doll. Lisa visits her to discuss the doll's significance.
The Spuckler home is a rural farm belonging to Cletus and Brandine Spuckler, along with their children, located on Rural Route 9. It is situated near the Movementarianism location.

A Roman Catholic school, St. Jerome's Catholic School is where Bart Simpson attended after being expelled from Springfield Elementary. Father Sean is a staff member, and one of the students is named Kevin.

Cletus Spuckler, also known as Cletus the Slack-Jawed Yokel, is a thin, good-natured redneck who lives on Rural Route 9 in Springfield with his wife Brandine and their children. Their relationship is often portrayed as incestuous, with implications of them being related.

A museum in Springfield, the Springsonian houses a variety of exhibits on art, history, culture, and architecture. It features notable displays such as the Egyptian Treasures of Isis exhibit and has been the site of various art and sculpture exhibitions.

A train that was once considered the most beautiful and expensive ever built, the Spruce Caboose crashed due to its size and was converted into a restaurant. The dining car remains in its original location, serving as a unique dining experience in Springfield.

Springshire is a neighborhood in Springfield characterized by its old, colonial British architecture and renaissance-style shops, including the Leaf Garret. It is known for its quaint atmosphere, reminiscent of a bygone era.
A magical version of Springfield Elementary School, Springwarts School of Magicry features students practicing magic. It serves as a parody of Hogwarts from the Harry Potter series.
The Springshire Wind Power Plant is a British counterpart to the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, owned by Mr. Bumble and his assistant Mr. Smithers.

The Springfieldia Human Power Plant is a medieval-style energy source owned by Lord Montgomery, where Homer and others work as manual laborers. The plant operates a power generator that is ultimately revealed to be non-functional, leading to the workers' despair.

A community watch and law enforcement agency, SpringShield was established by Homer Simpson, Lenny Leonard, and Carl Carson. It was more effective at fighting crime than the Springfield Police Department, leading to Chief Wiggum's dismissal, but was disbanded shortly after its formation.

Jebediah Springfield IV is the great-grandson of Jebediah Springfield, the founder of Springfield. He was in need of a kidney and was on a heart transplant list in the episode "Homer's Paternity Coot."

Springfield is located in an unspecified and possibly fictional U.S. state, often humorously suggested to be in any state but yours. The state was founded by circus freaks and is characterized by its diverse geography, including counties like Springfield County and Swartzwelder County, as well as cities such as Capital City and Ogdenville. The state has a mix of agricultural land and industrial areas, with notable landmarks like the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and a variety of wildlife. The exact location of Springfield remains a running gag in the series, with conflicting hints about its geographical position and neighboring states.
The oldest tree in Springfield was damaged when Homer Simpson used an anchor to stop the monorail, causing it to fall onto the birthplace of Jebediah Springfield.

The oldest and tallest redwood tree in Springfield was purchased by the Rich Texan for $100,000 at a secret auction. Lisa Simpson climbed the tree to protect it from being cut down, but after a lightning strike damaged it, the Rich Texan planned to build an amusement park called "Lisa Land" in her memory, prompting Lisa to protest against the development.
An adult movie theater in Springfield, it shows pornographic films and is open 24 hours. Regular visitors include Krusty the Clown and Chief Wiggum, and the movies often parody real-life titles.

location_name: Springfield's Best And Seattle's Worst Coffee
description: A coffee shop in Springfield, it humorously parodies Seattle's Best Coffee and features a logo reminiscent of Starbucks. The establishment is known for selling coffee to the local community.

An extremely obese resident of Springfield, he appeared in an episode of "Eye on Springfield" where he met Springfield's oldest man. Homer Simpson remarked that he did not consider him particularly fat.

A sports center for children, the Springfield Youth Center offers various youth sports programs, including volleyball and basketball. Lisa attempts to join teams here to improve her gym performance but faces challenges during tryouts.

The third season of The Simpsons premiered on September 19, 1991, and concluded on August 27, 1992. It featured 24 episodes, including the notable guest appearance of Michael Jackson, who voiced a character in "Stark Raving Dad."
A wetland located in Springfield, it was affected when Mayor Quimby drained a pond, causing the surrounding trees and plants to be swept away.

The Springfield Wall of Fame features plaques honoring the town's most famous and infamous residents, including cartoon characters and animals. Each plaque displays the individual's image, name, and claim to fame, except for El Barto, who has a question mark instead of an image. Ceremonies are held to unveil new plaques, with the most recent addition being for Vance Connor, a former class president of Springfield High School.

This facility is a prison for women, where Marge Simpson was sentenced twice: first for shoplifting and later for unsupervised parenting. During her time there, she gained the respect of fellow inmates and found a break from her homemaker life, ultimately escaping during a prison break.

A center for health and fitness, the Springfield YMCA features recreational activities and classes taught by Lugash. Homer once injured his leg during a basketball game here, and Rainier Wolfcastle planned to convert the building into a nature preserve.

A train station in Springfield, it has been destroyed and presumably rebuilt. Notable events include Lisa running there to stop Mr. Bergstrom from leaving, and a chaotic incident involving a forgotten bag of plutonium that led to an explosion, damaging the station. Lady Gaga also performed her first concert in Springfield at this location.
A college located in Springfield, Springfield University is an educational institution that features various programs and has a diverse student body.

A public wax museum features wax models of famous people and celebrities in Springfield. Notably, after Lisa becomes Little Miss Springfield, she receives a wax figure of herself, while poor climate control during a heatwave causes many figures to melt.

At the center of downtown Springfield, the town square features a grassy area with trees and is home to the county courthouse and a statue of Jebediah Springfield. It hosts events like the Springfield Fringe Festival and is surrounded by various businesses, including the Aztec Theater and the Android's Dungeon.

A toxic waste dump is located in Springfield, visible from the school bus on its way to the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. It represents one of the few responsible approaches to managing the city's radioactive waste.

A baseball stadium in Springfield, it serves as the home field for the Springfield Isotopes, a AA minor league team. The stadium hosts unique promotional events like Tomato Day and Dart Day, where fans throw tomatoes and darts at a communist recruiter.
A map of Springfield provides a visual representation of the town and its various locations, including notable spots like the Simpson family home, Moe's Tavern, and the Kwik-E-Mart.

A travel agency that sells plane tickets, vacation packages, and other tourism-related services. It is owned by Wally Kogen and has been used by various characters, including Moe Szyslak and Homer Simpson, for travel arrangements, often with humorous outcomes.
A skyscraper in Springfield, the Springfield Trade Center contains financial office space and features the exclusive fine dining establishment, the Millionaires Club, on one of its uppermost floors.

A lot where tires are disposed of, the Springfield Tire Yard is infamous for its persistent tire fire, which has become a local landmark and can be smelled in multiple states. The fire was accidentally started by Krusty the Clown and has been extinguished and re-ignited several times throughout the series.

Located at 2001 Windsor Avenue, Springfield Town Hall is where town meetings are held to discuss local issues, including taxes and community improvements. It is also the site where the Simpsons were voted out of Springfield in the episode "At Long Last Leave."

A natural landmark near Springfield, the Tide Pools are a rich ecosystem that Bart's class visited during a school trip. The visit turned dangerous when high tide arrived, leading to a dramatic rescue by Nelson.

An abandoned underground railway network runs beneath Springfield, with functional trains that are no longer in use due to damage caused to buildings by tremors. The subway passes under Springfield Elementary School, which suffered structural damage when Bart and Milhouse operated one of the trains.

The Springfield Telephone Directory serves as the standard phone directory for the city, allowing residents like Bart to contact various people and places. It has appeared in multiple episodes of the series.
