A district in Springfield hosts Broadway-style performances, including movies and plays. The Simpsons attended an Itchy and Scratchy musical titled "Stab-a-Lot" there.
Springfield State Prison is an active correctional facility in Springfield. It has housed notable inmates such as Sideshow Bob and Snake Jailbird.

A natural landmark in Springfield, the tar pits are located near the Springfield Natural History Museum and consist of malodorous, gas-emitting tar. Visitors could enjoy a free bucket of tar with admission, although certain professions were excluded from this offer. The tar pits were recognized as a top picnic site before Mayor Joe Quimby had them drained to make way for a new highway.
A subatomic supercollider was built in Springfield instead of a new baseball stadium, thanks to Lisa's lobbying. It is known for having created a black hole.
Springfield Symphony Hall is a venue for musical performances that was mentioned as being destroyed by Kent Brockman.

The Springfield Streetcar System is a trolley system that runs along the Springfield waterfront, utilizing single-unit streetcars that resemble those from the American Historical Presidents Conference Committee.
A train station in Springfield, it serves as a departure point for destinations like Rancho Relaxo.

A district and waterfront area in Springfield, Squidport serves as the city's main harbor and features a food court with a variety of cuisines, albeit mostly all-purpose meat. It is located near Barney's Bowlarama and the Aztec Theater, and includes attractions like Moe's Tavern, Duff Brewery, and Mr. Burns' casino.
One of Springfield's football stadiums, it is also used for concerts. The stadium has appeared in several episodes of The Simpsons.
A museum dedicated to stamps is located in Springfield, next door to Lenny's house.
A skating rink in Springfield, it is occasionally used for pee-wee hockey games and was heavily damaged during a riot caused by a tie in one of these matches.

A large sign on a hill overlooks Springfield, built by nuns and featuring the largest ring in the town. The sign can be rearranged to say either "Lisa is the jewel" or "Maggie is the jewel," and it was partially damaged when the Cargill Dome collapsed on it.

The Springfield Shopper is the most popular local newspaper in Springfield, founded in 1883 by Johnny Newspaperseed. It covers a wide range of topics, including local and world news, sports, and lifestyle, often featuring sensational headlines and tabloid-style content.

A sports arena in Springfield hosted the mixed martial arts Ultimate Punch, Kick and Choke Championship. Marge intervened to stop the event, challenging the championship's president, Chet Englebrick, to a match in the septagon, where she ultimately triumphed.

A racetrack located in Springfield's bird sanctuary, the Springfield Speedway has hosted events such as monster truck rallies. Notably, Maude Flanders was killed there when a t-shirt cannon knocked her off a grandstand.

A recreation center in Springfield, it features various classes such as kung-fu and art. Homer once took Bart and Lisa there, where Bart attended a kung-fu class taught by Comic Book Guy, and Lisa participated in an art class that ended with her and another student being asked to leave by their teacher.
A financial assistance office located in Springfield, Springfield Savings is situated near Slot Car Heaven.

Located at 2001 Creaking Oak Drive, this nursing home serves as Springfield's retirement facility for the elderly. Notable residents have included Abraham "Grampa" Simpson and Jasper Beardly, and the home is known for its strict rules and indifferent staff.

A small, one-story library in Springfield, it is frequented by Lisa Simpson, who is well-known by the staff and regular visitors. The library has faced issues with bats nesting in its card catalog cabinet.

A vehicle used to transport prisoners to and from Springfield State Prison, the Springfield Prison Bus was temporarily driven by Otto Mann to pick up students from Springfield Elementary when the school bus broke down, further depressing Bart Simpson about attending school.
A school for the hearing impaired is located in Springfield, where Grampa once played music so loudly that a deaf student shouted at him to turn it down.

A body of water in Springfield, the Springfield River is less popular than Lake Springfield, possibly due to its inconvenient location surrounded by thick forests. It was the site of an attempted emergency baptism by Ned Flanders for Bart, Lisa, and Maggie Simpson, which was interrupted by Homer and Marge.

The public pool in Springfield is a recreational facility where families can swim and relax. It has been featured in various episodes, highlighting moments such as Marge advising Lisa on how to handle a situation involving Maggie.

A theater in Springfield, the Springfield Playhouse has hosted various performances, including Duffman portraying Mark Twain and auditions for a passion play. Notable events include Homer landing the role of Jesus Christ, while Milhouse failed his audition.

The Springfield Police Station serves as the headquarters for the Springfield Police Department, featuring several prison cells, a front desk, a small museum of crime, and the chief's office. It is located near Barney's apartment and across the street from a travel agency and a newsstand.

A building in Springfield, the Springfield Primate Institute is where scientists, including Marvin Monroe and Fraumaker, debate the classification of Bigfoot as either a low-rate human or a brilliant beast.

A private school in Springfield, Springfield Preparatory School is known for its higher academic standards compared to Springfield Elementary. The headmaster is St. John Van Hookstratten, and notable students include Greta Wolfcastle and Brittany Brockman.
A club for journalists and reporters, the Springfield Press Club is frequented by members like Chloe Talbot and Kent Brockman. Lisa once dined there with Chloe Talbot.

A police academy located in Springfield, it is where Clancy Wiggum trained to become a police officer. The academy is known for its unconventional training methods, including an incident where Wiggum accidentally shot a cameraman during a shooting test.

A blood bank where residents can donate plasma, the Springfield Plasma Center is notable for an incident involving Bart and Santa's Little Helper, where Bart fainted after donating blood. He was later rescued by two men who took him and his dog to eat.

An apartment complex in Springfield, it is home to many young residents, including Homer and Marge Simpson, who lived there after graduating from Springfield High School. Other notable former residents include Kirk and Luann Van Houten, Selma Bouvier, Moe Szyslak, and Disco Stu.

A pet shop in Springfield, it is known for its motto, "All our pets are flushable." The Simpson family once took Santa's Little Helper there, where the owner claimed to use psychic powers to determine the dog's needs.
A theater in Springfield, the planetarium is often frequented by Professor Frink. It serves as a location where Bart and the Superfriends sought information about a comet heading for the town.
A pet cemetery in Springfield where residents bury their deceased pets, it is located next to the Springfield Cemetery. Lisa Simpson buried her cat, Snowball I, there.
A duckpond-filled park popular with senior citizens, Springfield Park is a natural area that has appeared in several episodes of The Simpsons. It is distinct from Springfield National Park.
An opera house in Springfield, it is owned by Mr. Burns and features performances by Boris Csupowski. The building closely resembles the Sydney Opera House.
An art museum in Springfield, it is home to Marge Simpson's nude painting of Mr. Burns and once housed Michelangelo's David.

A hotel located in downtown Springfield, the Springfield Palace Hotel offers amenities such as free food, a swimming pool, and HBO. Homer once stayed there while jurors were sequestered during a trial, and he infamously took several items from his room as souvenirs.

An orphanage in Springfield, it is staffed by Lindsey Naegle and has been depicted as destitute, often suffering from neglect due to the nearby Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. Notable events include Selma's consideration of adoption and the story of an orphan named Charlie, who briefly became Bart's younger brother before being returned.

A theater in Springfield, the Springfield Performing Arts Center hosted Krusty the Clown's performance as Franklin D. Roosevelt in the play "Sunrise at Campobello," where he humorously forgot his character's disability.

A public facility, the Springfield Office of Unemployment manages benefits and services for the unemployed. Marge Simpson received unemployment payments there after losing her job at a real estate agency.

The Springfield Observatory gained notoriety when it detected a comet named after Bart, which threatened the town. After the crisis was averted, the townspeople, led by Moe, attempted to destroy the observatory, but it later came under the care of Professor Frink, who feared losing it to other scientists.
A factory in Springfield that produces oatmeal, it became notable when Homer Simpson flooded the town, causing the building to overflow with oatmeal.

The Springfield Nuclear Power Plant is a two-unit pressurized water reactor facility owned by Charles Montgomery Burns, serving as the main power source for Springfield. Homer Simpson works in Sector 7G of the plant.

A wildlife refuge and camping area, Springfield National Forest features a waterfall and a cave inhabited by bears. It was once threatened by logging but was saved after a corrupt congressman was arrested, and it has been a site for various adventures involving the Simpson family.

A retail shop located inside the Springfield Mall, the Springfield Nutrition Center sells various health and nutrition products, including dietary and fitness supplements. One notable item is a massive weight gain powder, which the clerk admits does not actually work.

A national park located in Springfield, it features forests, mountains, and a lake with a small island. Pumas inhabit the area, and Bart and Lisa once visited, where they encountered Martin while he was excavating for arrowheads.
The Springfield Mountains are a range of mountains located near the city of Springfield. They serve as a backdrop for various outdoor activities and adventures.

The Springfield Museum of Natural History is the city's second museum of natural history, built after the original burned down. It features various exhibits, including dinosaur bones, marine life, and Egyptian artifacts, and has interactive displays like a plasma globe and a large telescope.
A natural preserve located in Springfield, it serves as a habitat for various wildlife and offers a serene environment for visitors.

A reserve of desert land used for rock climbing, this park is where Homer Simpson fulfilled his deceased mother's last wish by scattering her ashes at the peak. The location is also secretly used by Mr. Burns to manufacture missiles filled with nuclear waste.

Springfield Memorial Stadium is the home of the Springfield Isotopes, a fictional baseball team featured in the Simpsons comics. It serves as an alternative venue for the team, distinct from the more commonly seen Duff Stadium.

A maximum security prison located in Springfield, it has housed notorious inmates like Sideshow Bob and Snake Jailbird. Sideshow Bob once agreed to be a test subject in exchange for a reduced sentence, which led to his transformation and subsequent escape.
A karate dojo located at the Springfield Mall, it is run by Akira. Bart joins the classes but skips them, leading to his defeat when he tries to protect Lisa from bullies.

The local mall in Springfield features hundreds of shops, restaurants, and services, with Mr. Costington as its CEO. Notable stores include the Leftorium and Lionel Hutz's law office, but the mall has fallen into disrepair, with many stores closed and its interior now serving as a shelter for the homeless.

An annual marathon takes place in Springfield, inviting both residents and international visitors to participate for charity. The event commemorates town founder Jebediah Springfield's legendary run across six states to evade creditors, and notable moments include Bart winning by cheating while disguised as an Italian.

A historic landmark in Springfield, the lemon tree was planted over 100 years ago and is associated with the town's founding. It was once stolen by kids from Shelbyville but was returned after a daring rescue led by Bart Simpson. Tourists are not allowed to pick fruit from the tree, as all fruits in Springfield emit a barely audible radioactive hum.

A local publication, Springfield Magazine covers current events in the town, including community activities like a historic manuscript open house and an azalea festival. Edna Krabappel and Marge Simpson are known to read this magazine.

A school for gifted and troublesome students, Springfield Magnet School is where Lisa Simpson was sent to stop a student strike. It features a large library and is known for its diverse student body, including a handsome French boy Lisa met there.

A young offenders prison, the Springfield Juvenile Correctional Facility is likely operated by the Springfield police. Bart Simpson was incarcerated there after faking a wedding, and Homer Simpson worked as a security guard to protect him. The facility hosted a dance where inmates were handcuffed together, during which Bart and Gina Vendetti escaped.

A highly interactive museum in Springfield features unusual exhibits such as a giant book, a Mars section used as a skate park, a DNA-shaped slide, and an earthquake simulator. The museum also includes a sex education pavilion with an arcade game, and Professor Frink demonstrates a computer-themed exhibit that malfunctions after being tampered with.

An Italian-American organized crime syndicate operates in Springfield, known as the Springfield Mafia or Springfield Mob. The group is involved in various illegal activities and has notable members, including Fat Tony.
A lumber shop located on the outskirts of Springfield, Springfield Lumber is seen when Bart and Homer pass by in "Old Yeller-Belly."
This location resembles a fire station and is home to various lawyers, including the blue-haired lawyer. It was involved in the Movementarian cult's attempt to recruit Homer Simpson.

A jewelry shop located in downtown Springfield, it was once robbed by Waylon Smithers, who accidentally caused a diamond to become lodged in Maggie Simpson's mouth. This incident led to Smithers attempting to abduct Maggie for the jewel.

A children's baseball team in Springfield, the Isotots was once managed by Ned Flanders before Lisa Simpson took over. Using sabermetrics to strategize, the team initially won every match, but Bart's rebellion against her strict tactics ultimately led to a more enjoyable game for the players.

The primary airport serving Springfield features frequent direct flights to major international destinations, despite the city's small size. It is home to airlines such as Air Springfield and Crazy Clown Airlines, and includes amenities like a private bar for pilots and a lounge at gate 45.

Springfield's main public high school is where Homer Simpson and Marge Bouvier first met. The school's mascot is the Springfield High Jebediahs, and its facade is inspired by Grant High School in Portland, Oregon.

A hunting supplies store located inside the Springfield Mall, it is frequented by Homer Simpson, Barney Gumble, and Moe Szyslak. The store offers various hunting gear and was featured in the mobile game "The Simpsons: Tapped Out."

The Springfield Isotopes are the town's only minor league baseball team, known for their financial struggles and a record 26-game losing streak. The team has been owned by various entities, including the mafia and the Duff Corporation, and plays its home games at a stadium referred to as Springfield Stadium, Duff Stadium, or Isotope Stadium. Homer Simpson briefly served as the team's mascot, and there have been plans to relocate the team to Albuquerque, which were ultimately thwarted by Homer's activism.
A shop in Springfield that sells various craft supplies for hobbies. In the episode "MoneyBart," Bart encounters an employee trying to sell him a model ship, but he declines.

A wealthy district in Springfield, Springfield Heights is home to Burns Manor, a shopping promenade, and the Springfield Heights Institute of Technology. Notable residents include Charles Montgomery Burns, Rainier Wolfcastle, and Krusty the Clown.

A museum dedicated to Springfield's history, it features exhibits on the town's founder, Jebediah Springfield, including his bagpipe, chamber pot, and prosthetic silver tongue. The curator of the museum is Hollis Hurlbut.

A hardware store located near the Simpsons' house, it is where Bart purchases paint cans for his graffiti. The store is also featured when Homer tries to retrieve a letter from a mailbox next to it and during a price gouging incident related to the production of the Radioactive Man movie.
A movie theater located in Springfield Heights, it serves as a venue for various films.

A learning institution in Springfield, the Springfield Heights Institute of Technology (S.H.I.T.) is where Apu earned his PhD before working at the Kwik-E-Mart to pay off his student debt. Lisa once took Bender there to meet Professor Frink during a time travel adventure.
A mall located in Springfield Heights, it features several upscale stores popular with the wealthy elite of Springfield, including Abercrombie Rich and Victor's Secret.

A country club for Springfield's upper class, it features a front gate that promotes itself as the proud home of the "tippling gadabout." Groundskeeper Willie works there as the greenskeeper on weekends and during the summer.
The Springfield Hall of Records stores all of the town's official records, including election results. It was notably blown away in 1978.

The main hospital in Springfield, also known as Marvin Monroe Memorial Hospital, is staffed by Dr. Hibbert and Dr. Nick Riviera. It features a children's ward for injuries related to imitating TV shows and a Homer Simpson ward, named after a donation made by Homer, although it was actually funded by Mr. Burns.
A grocery store located near Moe's Tavern, Springfield Grocers serves the local community.

A natural tourist attraction, Springfield Gorge is known as the third most beautiful gorge in the state. It has been the site of various daredevil stunts, including Bart's skateboard jump and Homer's motorcycle leap, both of which highlight the dangers of such activities.

The city utility provides natural gas service to residential and commercial customers in Springfield, operating a network of pipelines, meters, and stations. A notable incident involved a worker repairing a gas line leak at the Simpson residence, which cost the family $900.

A multiplex movie theater located in downtown Springfield, it features at least 28 screens and has plans for future expansion. The Springfield Googolplex showcases a variety of films, including popular titles and parodies.

A rapidly melting glacier near Springfield has significantly diminished, now resembling a lake. During a school trip, Lisa attributes the melting to global warming, while a park ranger disputes this claim.

The Springfield Fire Department is the town's fire station, where firefighters respond to emergencies and operate firefighting equipment. Notable employees have included Homer Simpson, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, and Seymour Skinner, and the department is equipped with a standard fire engine and a ladder truck.

A funeral parlor in Springfield, it hosted Mona Simpson's funeral, attended by Homer, Grampa, and a few friends. The Springfield Funeral Home was also the site where Sideshow Bob's coffin was sent after he faked his death, and it features the Garden of Talking Statues.
A folk art museum is located in Springfield, where Lisa once visited with her friend Juliet Hobbes to explore special exhibits.

A wildlife refuge and nature reserve, Springfield Forest was created by Theodore Roosevelt. It is notable for being the childhood home of Homer Simpson and his family, and it has been the site of various adventures, including a search for lost spectacles and a family reunion over a box of recipes.
A gas station located across from Edna's Edibles, Springfield Gas is where Bart once wished for a flame vision and accidentally burned a gas pump.

An outdoor market in Springfield, it primarily sells crops and was established after a significant influx of hipsters from Portland. The market replaced the Springfield Tire Yard at the same location.
A luxury hotel in Springfield, the Four Seasons is where Selma and Fat Tony got married.

location_name: Springfield Estadio de Toros (initially the Duff Beer Krusty Burger Buzz Cola Costington's Department Store Kwik-E-Mart Stupid Flanders Park)
description: A sports stadium designed by Homer Simpson, it was originally built for the Springfield Meltdowns football team. After the team was canceled, it was repurposed for bullfighting and renamed Springfield Estadio de Toros, owned by Montgomery Burns.
The Springfield Fairgrounds host various events and festivities, including the Hullabalooza music festival, where Homer once participated.

Springfield's only professional basketball team, formerly known as the Austin Celtics and Springfield Celtics, is called the Springfield Excitement. Owned by Montgomery Burns, the team plays at the Burns Arena, which was once invaded by bees after the roof was opened, turning it into a massive beehive.

The Springfield Extension School is where Homer Simpson attended a class to learn how to satisfy Marge, which ultimately led him to become the boss at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant. He initially took a lesson on how to strip for his wife, taught by Julius Hibbert, but ended up in a successmanship class led by Stark Richdale.

The former Springfield Elementary School was converted into a prison, with classrooms featuring prison cells to help manage troublesome students. Principal Skinner and Edna Krabappel rented out cloakrooms to the Springfield prison, and notable inmate Snake Jailbird had a cell located behind Bart's desk.
An Episcopal Christian church is located in Springfield, situated across the street from the First Church of Springfield.

A mall owned by Richard Texan was built around the Simpson family's house, which they discovered when they woke up to find it encased within the mall. The mall was later transferred to Lenny Leonard after it was revealed to be constructed on Woopakanomie Native American land, and Lenny ultimately destroyed it to create a casino.
A dry cleaning business located in downtown Springfield, it is staffed by Raphael and offers chemical cleaning services for clothes. Comic Book Guy has been seen getting his clothes dry-cleaned here.

A drive-in movie theater located in Springfield, it is visible from the rooftop garden of the Kwik-E-Mart. The Springfield Drive-In has been the setting for various events, including a date between Abe and Zelda, and a marriage proposal by Troy McClure to Selma Bouvier during a screening of his film.

A facility for drag racing, Springfield Dragway hosted an event where Mr. Burns invited employees of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant to watch a race. He ordered the cars to race slowly for better comprehension, and Waylon Smithers, Jr. briefly worked as an announcer there.

Springfield's main landfill site is known as the Springfield Dump. It has been the location where Homer and Bart illegally supplied the town with beer during Prohibition and where they discovered the Mr. Sparkle box. After losing his shack, Groundskeeper Willie lived in the dump and once attempted to harm Bart in a fit of rage.

An elementary school attended by Bart, Lisa, and other Springfield children, it is managed by Principal Seymour Skinner and overseen by Superintendent Gary Chalmers. The school's mascot is a purple puma, and its address is 19 Plympton Street.
A dry cleaner is located across the street from the Android's Dungeon in Springfield.

A popular gambling destination, Springfield Downs is a dog and horse racing track where Homer and Bart once bet on a dog named Santa's Little Helper, who later became a member of the Simpson family. The track features a mechanized rabbit named Swifty and offers low-stakes wagering options for patrons.

A hydroelectric dam located in Springfield, it was constructed by Cecil Terwilliger, who embezzled funds and attempted to destroy it with Bart and Lisa trapped inside. Although the dam was later deemed too weak and destroyed, a giant wave from the incident caused no damage.
A donut shop in Springfield, Springfield Donuts was notably affected by a city riot.

A live entertainment venue, the Springfield Dinner Theater offers meals alongside stage plays, musicals, and cabaret shows. Notable events include an assassination attempt on Mayor Quimby during a production of "Guys and Dolls" and a negative review from Homer while he was a food critic for the Springfield Shopper.
A dog park located in Springfield, it provides a space for residents to bring their dogs to play and socialize.
The Springfield Dam is a large dam located near the city, often referenced in various episodes. It plays a significant role in the local environment and is a notable landmark in Springfield.

A cryogenic freezing facility is located in Springfield, where Abe Simpson was placed due to an incurable illness before 2041. The entrance is disguised as a gravestone, and the facility utilizes advanced technology to preserve individuals, including notable residents like Agnes Skinner and Gil Gunderson.
A facility that sells dogs as pets, the Springfield Dog Pound is where Santa's Little Helper was taken after running away from home before being adopted by Mr. Burns.

A visual and performing arts elementary school, this academy is located near Springfield Elementary School and is visible from Principal Skinner's office. The building is made of modeling clay and is reshaped daily, suggesting it is a private institution.

The Springfield County Court House serves as the main building for local judicial matters and the seat of government for Springfield County. It features the motto "Liberty and Justice for Most" inscribed at its grand entrance, located next to the public square with the statue of Jebediah Springfield.

A major events venue in Springfield, the Convention Center hosts large conventions, trade shows, and conferences. It was officially opened by Mayor Joe Quimby and has been the site of various events, including a notable fire during a science fiction convention.

A cosmetic surgery clinic in Springfield, it was formerly the Springfield Children's Hospital before being repurposed by Mayor Joe Quimby. The clinic is known for its controversial focus on cosmetic procedures rather than traditional medical care.

The Springfield County Fair is an annual event where various competitions take place, including a place setting competition and a 4-H cow contest. Notably, Homer once participated as a judge and, while disguised as the superhero Pie Man, humiliated the Rich Texan for ruining Lisa's entry, while Bart's cow Lou won a blue ribbon but faced the grim fate of being slaughtered.
A costume shop in Springfield, it is where Homer and Larry Burns hid after a kidnapping incident. The shop features various costumes and has been seen in multiple episodes of the series.

A concert hall designed by Frank Gehry was built in Springfield after Marge requested it in a letter. Due to a lack of interest in classical music, it was eventually converted into the Montgomery Burns State Prison.

A community college located in Springfield, it offers various courses and has been attended by several characters, including Marge, Apu, and Principal Skinner. The college is known for its slogan, "where old dogs learn new tricks."

A large indoor arena in Springfield, the Coliseum hosts concerts and various events for thousands of attendees. Advertisements for local brands such as Duff Beer, Buzz Cola, and Krusty Burger can be seen around the venue.

A community facility in Springfield, it features a stage and seating for various recreational, arts, and civic events. The Springfield Community Center has been the site of numerous significant events in the town, including auditions for plays and civic gatherings.
A theater in Springfield, it is where Bart auditioned for a summer stock play and famously shouted "sit on it, Springfield" during a performance of Grease 2, earning applause from the audience.
A commercial airline, Springfield Airways operates out of Springfield Airport and offers flights to cities including Los Angeles, Las Vegas, New York, Houston, and Chicago.
A live entertainment venue in Springfield, the amphitheater hosts various events, including comedy festivals and performances by magicians like Penn and Teller.
Springfield's main pet-treating facility is the Animal Hospital, where pets receive medical care. The Simpsons have taken their dog, Santa's Little Helper, there for treatment on multiple occasions.

Springfield features a diverse range of accents among its residents, including a general American accent commonly spoken by children and many adults. Some characters, like Homer Simpson, exhibit traits of northern and western U.S. accents, while others, such as Marge Simpson and Barney Gumble, display New York metropolitan accents. Additionally, characters like Ned Flanders show traces of a southern accent, and Mayor Joe Quimby has a non-rhotic Boston accent. This variety may reflect the town's socioeconomic diversity and its status as a linguistic melting pot.

One of Springfield's universities, Springfield A&M is known for its rivalry with Springfield University and is often referred to as a "cow college." Its mascot is a pig named Sir Oinks-a-Lot, and the school hosts an annual football game against Springfield University.
A theater in Springfield, the Clamphitheater hosted a performance by Cheech and Chong, where Homer stepped in for Chong after he walked out.

A hotel located next to Springfield Airport, the Springfield Airport Motor Lodge is notable for its proximity to the runway, where landing planes can hit the hotel sign. It features amenities like free HBO and has hosted events such as a seminar on love secrets attended by Moe.

A small city in Springfield County, Springfield is home to the Simpson family and has a population of approximately 60,000. The city features a nuclear power plant, several elementary schools, a minor league baseball stadium, and various districts including Little Italy and Chinatown, while also being known for its rivalry with neighboring Shelbyville.

An apartment building in Springfield, Spinster City Apartments is home to Marge Simpson's twin sisters, Patty and Selma, along with Selma's adopted daughter, Ling Bouvier, and her iguana, Jub-Jub. The building has caught fire three times due to Patty and Selma's smoking habits.

An airfield in Springfield where airplanes take off, it is the site from which Homer Simpson, Mr. Burns, and Waylon Smithers stole a plane to flee to Cuba while evading the FBI. It serves as a smaller alternative to Springfield International Airport.
A sporting goods store in Springfield, Sportacus is where Marge took Bart and Milhouse when they joined the Springfield Pee Wee football team.
A spirograph factory in Springfield is run by a man referred to as Mr. S by Bart. It appears as a background building in the "Shadow of the Colossal Donut" level of The Simpsons Game.
A venue for the Spellympic Games, it features the Spellympic Stadium where various competitions take place. Lisa competes here in the episode "I'm Spelling as Fast as I Can."

A store selling left-handed merchandise, Southpaw Superstore is located at Towne Centre in Springfield. Its success led Ned Flanders to close the Leftorium and open a smaller kiosk called Leftorium Express.

A cracker factory in Springfield, Southern Cracker was once the leading cracker brand in town, owned by Luann Van Houten's father. After managerial duties were passed to Luann's husband, Kirk, the brand's popularity declined significantly, leading to his eventual firing following their divorce.

A quirky restaurant known as the Spaghetti Laboratory, or "Spaglab," serves unusual Italian dishes inspired by science fiction, such as Pene from Planet X and Manicottimal. It is a remnant of the 1980s fun-restaurant trend.
A sock store located in Springfield Mall, Sox appears briefly in the episode "Simpson and Delilah." Its name is a parody of the Fox broadcasting network, which airs The Simpsons.

A renovated pedestrian mall located on the waterfront, South Street Squidport was once the site of a squid-gutting industry. It has been transformed into an upscale shopping promenade featuring various businesses, including the Itchy & Scratchy Store and the Karachi Hibachi.
A bed and breakfast where Homer and Marge stayed to rekindle their romance after their 11th anniversary. Snuggler's Cove features charming accommodations, including rooms with elegant decor.
This office handles government benefits for groups like the elderly and disabled. Abe Simpson and Jasper Beardly sought assistance from the Social Security Office due to their age.

A cat park in Springfield, it was formerly known as the Springfield Dog Park before being renamed by Mayor Quimby after Snowball II saved Homer. The park is exclusively for cats and is sponsored by Buzz Cola with lemon.
A resort located in West Springfield, Smooches On The Beach offers a getaway destination for relaxation and leisure.
A shop located within Springfield International Airport, Snacks offers a variety of snack foods for travelers.
A mattress store located near the Android's Dungeon, Snooze at 11 offers a variety of bedding options for customers in Springfield.
A smoke factory in Springfield contributes to pollution, with smoke from it, along with the steel mill and a day-care center, causing acid rain to fall over the town.
A smoothie parlor in Springfield, Snooty Smoothies is known for its upscale atmosphere. Helen Lovejoy has been seen leaving the establishment, where she encounters Marge, Bart, and Lisa.

The Slide Factory is a fun center in Springfield where schools typically take field trips, except for Springfield Elementary, which Principal Skinner chose to send to the Springfield Box Factory instead. Buses from Shelbyville Elementary and Spittle County Elementary were seen nearby.
A slaughterhouse in Springfield processes cows into meat products using automated machinery. It is located on Rural Route 9 next to Abattoir Costello LLC.
A business where customers can control and race model slot cars, popular among characters like Otto and Comic Book Guy.

A rundown motel in Springfield, the Sleep-Eazy Motel features deteriorating facilities and coin-operated amenities in the rooms, including the television and vibrating beds. It has a reputation for unsavory activities, with a history of strange occurrences, such as a body floating in the pool and surveillance cameras in the rooms.

A money loaning office chain in Springfield, Sleazy Sam's Payday Loans has 50 locations throughout the town. The establishment is known for its questionable practices, highlighted by an incident where Homer, dressed as Jesus, promoted the opening of the 50th building and was struck by lightning.

A barn-themed steakhouse in Springfield, the Slaughterhouse features an interior decorated with hanging steer carcasses and a blood fountain. Customers can choose a cow for their steak, and the menu includes a massive 72 oz. New York-style sirloin steak, with a special 16 lb. tenderloin steak available upon request. The restaurant is known for its controversial pro-meat stance and has faced protests from vegetarians, including Lisa Simpson.

A poor district in Springfield, Skid Row is known for its high population of derelicts and junkies, often referred to as Bumtown or Junkyville. It is separated from the nicer parts of town by railroad tracks and is located near Crackton and the Badlands.

An abandoned amusement park, Six Flags Over Krusty features Krustyland, which was shut down after the events of "The Food Wife." Following its closure, it became known as Bully Summit, a gathering place for bullies.

A rotating restaurant located atop a large tower, it can be accessed by an elevator in the center. Homer once reviewed it positively as a food critic, although he became nauseated after seeing his sisters-in-law exercising in revealing outfits.

The home of Principal Seymour Skinner and his mother Agnes is located at 330 Pikeland Avenue, next door to Martin Prince. The house is often vandalized by students from Springfield Elementary and has been the site of various comedic incidents, including a disastrous lunch with Superintendent Chalmers.
A ski chalet is a Swiss-style house featured in Springfield, often associated with winter sports and vacationing.

A diner located on the town square next to the Android's Dungeon, Skip's Diner has primarily appeared in the background of various scenes. The interior was first shown in "A Springfield Summer Christmas for Christmas," where Mary Tannenbaum meets Seymour Skinner.

A restaurant in downtown Springfield, known for its singing waiters, serves steaks cooked to various degrees of "sung." The Simpson family celebrated Marge's birthday and Bart's academic achievement there, but after Homer's credit card was rejected, they attempted to leave without paying and ended up having to perform a song to settle their bill.
A detailed map of Springfield was created by Lerma Terry Hogan, showcasing various locations within the town.
A clinic located on Psychiatry Row, Sit 'n' Weep is where Marge and Homer sought psychiatric help for Lisa.
An ice rink located in Springfield, it hosts a curling club on Saturdays and features a "clockwise night" every Thursday.

Two sinkholes have appeared in Springfield: one at the Simpson family's house featured in The Simpsons Movie, and another caused by a leaking force in the episode "Adventures in Baby-Getting," which created a massive hole in the center of the town.
A donut shop located in the kingdom of Springfieldia, it is a parody of Dunkin' Donuts. Homer and Lisa pass by it while trying to earn gold pieces for the amulet of Warmfyre.

A laser tag warehouse in Springfield, it is owned by Abe Simpson II. Homer worked there to help pay for Marge's college tuition, and it is suggested that the business may have been sold or closed after he began working at the nuclear power plant.

location_name: Sir Putt-A-Lot's Merrie Olde Fun Centre
description: A miniature golf course and recreation complex in Springfield, it features over a dozen holes, go-karts, a batting cage, skee ball, and video games. Sir Putt-A-Lot's hosts an annual miniature golf tournament and is notable for being the place where Homer and Marge conceived Bart.

Marge Simpson is one of the five main characters in The Simpsons, serving as the homemaker and moral compass of the family. She is married to Homer and is the mother of Bart, Lisa, and Maggie, often trying to maintain order amidst their chaotic lives.

A furniture shop in Springfield Heights, Shøp is known for its unique and unusual designs. Its mascot is an anthropomorphic Allen wrench, and it features a canteen with Lego-made forks, which Homer Simpson enjoys.

A bike customizing store run by Bart Simpson, it was originally co-owned by Abe Simpson II before his death. The shop features murals created by Bart, including one celebrating his life and another honoring Lisa, which made her happy as she believed Bart disliked her.

A country bar located near Springfield, Shotkickers features country-western music, line dancing, and a mechanical bull, along with a variety of drinks. Marge Simpson and Ruth Powers visited during a girls' night out, where Marge participated in line dancing, and Groundskeeper Willie was seen riding the mechanical bull.

A wedding chapel located just over the state line, it is where Homer and Marge got married. Known for its inexpensive, cookie-cutter weddings, it offers a punch card system for repeat customers and is associated with a nearby gambling house, providing complimentary casino chips as gifts.

A shoe store located inside the Springfield Mall, Simply Shoes sells high-end running shoes, including a pair called "Assassins" that Homer purchased for $125. The store features a window display with the brand's tagline, "Join the conspiracy."
A strip club located on Silicon Alley, it is known for its adult entertainment. Barney Gumble once worked there.
A shoe store located in Springfield, Shoe City is briefly seen in "Homer's Night Out" when Homer drives home from the Kwik-E-Mart.

A coffee shop and diner in Springfield, Shorty's has been the setting for various character interactions, including a brunch between Marge and Jacques, and a blind date between Edna Krabappel and Jasper.
A retail store located in the Springfield Mall, it specializes in selling children's shoes. It is situated opposite Lionel Hutz's law firm.
A Jewish store, Shlomo's Judaica is where Marge once stopped to shop during a trip to visit Dwight Diddlehopper in prison.

A lesbian bar located in the lower east side of Springfield, the She-She Lounge is known for its pride, sisterhood, and excellent margaritas. It has a friendly, laid-back atmosphere and is considered one of the finest watering holes in town, though Homer Simpson once left after expressing concern about its lack of a fire exit.

A fast-food fried chicken restaurant chain, Shakespeare's Fried Chicken is named after the famous writer William Shakespeare. It is known for its buckets of fried chicken, which the Simpson family has been seen enjoying in various episodes.

A fitness center chain opened by Marge Simpson, Shapes provides a positive workout environment specifically for ordinary women. It quickly gained popularity in Springfield, leading to the establishment of a second location and Marge's rise to fame. The gym enforces four rules: no men, no cell phones, no mirrors, and no shame, with the slogan "I am woman, hear me sweat."

An atomic bomb-themed diner in Springfield, the Sha-Boom Ka-Boom! Cafe features a menu with items named after the bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Its design includes googie architecture resembling a mushroom cloud and displays framed images of WWII planes and veterans.
A store where Lisa once went to get a key copied for $1.80, and plastic rings are available for 7 cents.
A shell shop located at Springfield Squidport, it has a sign that humorously reads "Hell Ha K" due to missing letters.

A restaurant in Springfield, Shake 'n' Bake likely sells ice cream shakes and baked goods. Homer Simpson once placed a coupon for this establishment in the collection plate at the First Church of Springfield.
The house belongs to Sherri and Terri, the twin daughters of Mrs. Krabappel. It is featured in various episodes of The Simpsons, including "Bart of Darkness" and "Marge's Son Poisoning."

A shop that specializes in a wide variety of musical doorbells, it is owned by Señor Ding-Dong, originally a marketing gimmick. The shop is notable for its colorful selection and has been visited by characters like Marge, Lisa, and Bart, who were impressed by the offerings during an adventure.

A fat camp, Serenity Ranch features a sign that reads, "When diet, exercise, and surgery aren't enough." Bart is sent there after a heart attack due to junk food consumption, where he trains under the demeaning supervision of Tab Spangler alongside other attendees like Apu and Rainier Wolfcastle.

This dentist, featured in the season 1 opening sequence, is located above Howard's Flowers. It is known as "Semi-Painless Dentistry" and later replaced by "Candy Most Dandy" in the opening sequence from season 2 to early season 20. In the episode "Last Exit to Springfield," Lisa has a check-up at a similar establishment called "Painless Dentistry."
A scrapyard featured in the episode "Cue Detective," where Nelson escapes from Bart and Lisa while being pursued by Tyler over a stolen grill.

location_name: Secret Nuclear Defense Plan U.S. Govt. Film
description: Springfield has been designated as a nuclear calibration target for allied nations, meaning it would be bombed first in the event of a nuclear war. This information is revealed in a leaked government film intended for the U.S. president, which features a map resembling Springfield, Massachusetts.

A Christmas-themed amusement park in Springfield, Santa's Village is open year-round and features real-life reindeer as its main attraction, although they often struggle in the local environment. The park is ironically closed on Christmas, and it has been the setting for various misadventures involving the Simpson family and other characters.

A medical and scientific research lab in Springfield, the Screaming Monkey Medical Research Center is known for creating a mutant parrot called an octoparrot. Homer Simpson visited as a test subject, where doctors discovered a crayon lodged in his brain, which, when removed, reportedly increased his IQ by 50 points.

A desert in Springfield, known as Satan's Anvil, features a rock formation that resembles a blacksmith's anvil. It is inhabited by an elderly couple, a roadrunner, a coyote, and scorpions, and contains a mine where settlers left behind explicit drawings discovered by Bart Simpson.
A school in Springfield teaches individuals how to be mall Santas, where Homer and Barney enrolled. The school features a hypnotist as a teacher and is led by the head of Santa School.
A clothing store for girls located in the Springfield Mall, Saks Fifth Grade offers a limited selection of sizes, which leads Lisa to struggle with body image issues during her visit.
Sanjay's house is the residence of Apu's brother, Sanjay.
A shoe store specializing in sandals, it is located at Springfield Squidport.
A sandy beach is a location where the Simpson family has vacationed. Homer once swam with a fake shark fin, scaring beachgoers, while Bart joined in the fun with his own fin.
A pirate-themed restaurant, The Rusty Barnacle is known for its nautical decor and seafood offerings.

A district in Springfield, the Russian District has a significant population of Russians, Chechens, and other Eastern Europeans, resembling a typical Eastern European city. Homer visits this area while searching for Lisa.

The cafeteria at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant is owned by Mr. Burns and is located adjacent to the plant. It serves meals to the plant's employees, including Homer Simpson, who has been seen sneaking in for a quick bite.

location_name: Saint Sebastian's School for Wicked Girls
description: A Catholic school for girls with behavioral issues, Saint Sebastian's School for Wicked Girls is run by nuns from a French-Canadian order. Samantha Stankey, Milhouse's former girlfriend, was sent there after being caught kissing Bart.

location_name: Rubber Baby Buggy Bumpers Babysitting Service
description: A babysitting service in Springfield, Rubber Baby Buggy Bumpers employs a receptionist and several babysitters, including Lucille Botzcowski. The Simpsons children are blacklisted due to past misbehavior, and Homer once deceived the service into sending a babysitter by claiming to be part of the Samson family.

location_type: Site of the Heavenly Hills Mall
description: An undeveloped area of Springfield, Sabertooth Meadow was the site of an archaeological dig by Springfield Elementary students, where Lisa discovered an angel fossil that was later revealed to be a hoax. The land was subsequently developed into the Heavenly Hills Mall, which features the faux angel fossil as part of its exterior decoration.
A trailer park located in Spittle County, it features a sign that tracks the number of days since the last tornado. Lurleen Lumpkin, a country singer, resides there.

location_name: Royal Majesty for the Obese or Gangly Gentleman
description: A tailor shop in Springfield, this establishment specializes in clothing for obese, tall, and exceptionally large men. It is known for its custom creations, including a purple crushed-velvet tuxedo and a traditional African dashiki, and has a slogan that emphasizes the importance of not damaging its merchandise: "You rip it, you buy it."

A military boarding school named after General Erwin Rommel, Rommelwood Military School is where Bart and Lisa Simpson attended. The school offers traditional academics alongside military training, including weapons training and drill, and features a challenging obstacle known as the eliminator, which was later deemed too dangerous and removed.

A business in Springfield that functioned as both a flea market and a drive-in movie theater, it was known for its poorly maintained marquee and was eventually demolished. The location featured a showing of Troy McClure's film "The Muppets Go Medieval" shortly before its closure.

Dr. Nick Riviera is a quack physician known for his dubious medical practices and catchphrase, "Hi, everybody!" He operates a walk-in clinic in Springfield and has performed questionable medical procedures on the Simpson family, often with disastrous results.

A clothing store located in Springfield, Rural Outfitters is featured in "The Serfsons," where Homer and Lisa pass by while seeking gold pieces for the amulet of Warmfyre. The store is a parody of Urban Outfitters.
A store located in Springfield Mall, it specializes in selling meat and is presumably founded by someone named Ron.

A book shop located in the Springfield Mall, Rock Bottom Remainders is where Homer and Marge purchase the Time-Life Carpenter's Library box set. The store features a variety of books, including titles related to woodworking and carpentry.

The Springfield Republican Party headquarters is a sinister-looking castle situated at the edge of a tall cliff. Access to the building is provided through a secret tunnel located at a Lard Lad statue, which has stairs leading inside.

A green grassy field marked with a warning sign to keep off the grass, it is featured in "The Telltale Head." Jimbo, Kearney, and Dolph are seen lying on it while Bart visits with the head of the Jebediah statue in his backpack.

A re-education facility used during Ned Flanders' rule, the Re-Neducation Center forced dissenters to smile, wear outfits resembling Flanders' clothing, and undergo lobotomies to erase their personalities, while allowing them to keep the removed sections of their brains.

A clothing store located in the kingdom of Springfieldia, Restoration Bard Wear was featured when Homer and others participated in a stoning event. It parodies the home-furnishing retailer Restoration Hardware.
An animal waste processing plant is located in the Rat's Nest neighborhood, where Homer Simpson enjoys the smell of hog fat it produces.

A real estate agency run by Lionel Hutz, Red Blazer Realty has at least two offices in Springfield. All staff members wear red blazers, and notable employees have included Gil Gunderson and Cookie Kwan.

A two-star health spa located in the Springfield mountains, Rancho Relaxo offers amenities such as a tennis court, jacuzzis, and mud baths. Guests can enjoy activities like bungee jumping, kayaking, and hula dancing, and the spa features its own train station for access from Springfield.

A snake sanctuary is located in Springfield, known as the Rattlesnake Sanctuary. It is featured in the episode "Fraudcast News," where Homer ends up there after an incident involving Mr. Burns' henchmen.

A poor, crime-ridden district in Springfield, Rat's Nest is located on the New Springfield side of the Springfield Bridge. The area is characterized by unpaved roads and is close to the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, which has contributed to environmental hazards.
A delivery truck transports rat traps in Springfield. It is featured in the episode "The Boy Who Knew Too Much."

Joe Quimby, also known as Mayor Quimby, is the slick and corrupt mayor of Springfield, often prioritizing his own interests over those of the citizens. He is known for his womanizing ways, frequent acceptance of bribes, and a catchphrase, "Vote Quimby," which he uses inappropriately even in compromising situations.

A district in Springfield, the Rat's Nest Neighborhood is a hillbilly community populated by farmers and descendants of the town's founders. It is located near the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, which has contaminated the area with radioactive waste and poorly maintained roads.
A large brick mansion with a ring driveway, it is the residence of Rainier Wolfcastle, his wife, and their daughter Greta. The mansion features an indoor swimming pool.

A motel in Springfield, Quantity Inn parodies the Quality Inn hotel chain. It is where Marge, Ned, Helen, Reverend Lovejoy, Sideshow Mel, and Agnes stayed after a successful card counting session at La Belle Frottage Casino.
A mansion in Springfield, Quimbebunkport Estates is the residence of Mayor Quimby and features a swimming pool with a volleyball court.

A muffin store located on the same block as Edna's Edibles, R. Crumb's Keep on Muffin' features a sign modeled after characters from Robert Crumb's "Keep on Truckin'" comic. It is one of several muffin-themed shops in the area.
A psychiatrist office located on Psychiatry Row, it resembles an older-style Jack in the Box restaurant and serves as a parody of the fast-food chain.

A restaurant in Springfield, Pudding on the Ritz is where Homer was caught cheating on his diet by Marge, who was filming a segment for a show. The establishment is known for its pudding, which Homer ordered during the incident.
A shop parodying Pottery Barn, Puttering Barn is located at the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, next to Banana Dictatorship.
A golf store located near the Springfield Glen Country Club, the Pro Shop is designed as a large pyramid with numerous steps leading to its entrance.
A store located in the Springfield Mall, it sells potions, hexes, and a fax machine. Selma visits Princess Opal in hopes of finding a man.

A bus stop located in Pressboard Estates serves bus routes 22A and 22. Lisa once visited this stop while trying to take a bus to the museum, where she encountered a crowd that pushed her aside as she attempted to board.
A district featuring various psychiatric facilities, Psychiatry Row includes establishments like Quack in the Box, 99 Shrink, and Sit 'n' Weep, as well as a child psychiatrist.
A preschool located on Elm Street, it is situated across from the Kwik-E-Mart and may be referenced by Springfield Elementary School.

A Protestant youth festival in Springfield features activities aimed at engaging young attendees in their faith. Bart attended with Marge, Ned, and Timothy Lovejoy, where he initially resisted the event but ultimately helped resolve a conflict between different Christian groups.
The Prince family resides in a house located on Evergreen Terrace.

A prank store located at the Towne Centre in Springfield, it sells joke items like chattering teeth and novelty vomit. Lisa once considered buying a gift for Bart from this store while Christmas shopping.

A theme park owned by Ned Flanders, Praiseland was created in memory of his late wife, Maude. It was built on the site of the old Storytime Village and featured a statue of Maude that caused hallucinations due to a gas leak, leading to its eventual shutdown after a scandal involving orphans.
A skyscraper made of popsicle sticks, it was located near a 50-foot magnifying glass and was ultimately burned down.
A bookstore located in the Springfield Mall, Popular Books specializes in trendy and popular titles. It is one of the many retail options available in the mall.
A store located in the Springfield Mall, Poverty Barn is a parody of Pottery Barn, offering a variety of home goods and decor.
A barn used for storing horses and polo equipment is located at the Polo Field House. It serves as a facility for polo-related activities in Springfield.
An employee at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, the power plant guard is stationed at the entrance and is often seen watching television, eating a sandwich, and drinking soda.
A stall at Springfield Squidport, it sells popcorn and is visited by Homer, Bart, and Lisa during their walk.

A pool shop in Springfield offers various swimming pool options, including unique models like the hick tub and the lightning magnet. The Simpson family visits this location after a demonstration from the Springfield pool mobile.

A member of Springfield's police force, this officer worked at the Springfield State Prison and was involved in a fight with Snake Jailbird, which ended in reconciliation after hearing Lurleen Lumpkin's song "Your Wife Don't Understand You."
A plumbing supplies store in Springfield is where Lupe Velez purchased the toilet she drowned in, which Marge photographed during a family ride. This location appears in the episode "Homer's Phobia."

A casino owned by Plato, it is where Abe Simpson goes after inheriting money from his late girlfriend, Beatrice Simmons. The casino appears in various episodes, including "Old Money" and "I Married Marge."

A store located in Springfield Mall, the Popcorn Shack is situated next to the Happy Sailor Tattoo Parlor. It is a place where characters like Marge, Bart, Lisa, and Maggie pass by on their way to Dr. Zitsofsky's dermatology clinic.

A factory in Springfield produces playdough, which is transported via flatbed trucks using an overgrown play-doh fun factory shape slider. The playdough is noted to be non-toxic, although it is unclear if this factory is the source of that product.

The Plant Operations Center is part of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, where Homer once attempted to release spoiled milk and utility-grade chicken into the air-conditioning system. The operation was thwarted by FBI agent Annie Crawford, and it was later revealed that the air conditioning was non-functional.
A child in Springfield suffered a plumbing accident that resulted in a faucet becoming lodged in his head, leading to his hospitalization at Springfield General Hospital.

An amusement park in Springfield features a giant plaster mountain as its main attraction. It offers various rides and attractions, including a toilet sponsored by Fodex, souvenir shops, and traditional amusement park stands.
A fast food pizza takeout stand located in the Springfield Mall food court, Pizzeria Cheapo offers quick pizza options for customers on the go.

This dog school trains attack dogs and addresses their behavioral issues for the safety of the public. It also prepares dogs for competitions like Crufts, offering owners diplomas and special events for members.

This plastic surgery clinic has the motto "correcting God's mistakes." Selma underwent surgery here, funded by Fat Tony, and Homer visited to get stomach staples and other procedures to improve his appearance for Marge.
A yogurt shop in Springfield, it features a pink bearded pirate as its mascot and has a building designed to resemble a ship. It is located next to the Frying Dutchman.
The Pie Cave is a basement hideout used by Homer when he adopts the persona of the Pie Man. It is located in the Simpson home.

A hotel located in the Springfield Heights district, Pillowmint Hotel was visited by Homer and Bart to persuade the band The Who to perform in their area, New Springfield. They humorously warned the band about the restrictions they would face in Old Springfield.

A photography studio in Springfield showcases Christmas cards featuring family photos during the holiday season. In the episode "Changing of the Guardian," Homer and Marge discover a photo of their children with their new guardians, Mav and Portia, prompting them to reclaim their kids.
A gated neighborhood in Springfield, Pine Hills features Raphael as the security guard. It is known for hosting a Halloween block party called "Spine Chills."

location_name: Phineas Q. Butterfat's 5600 Flavors Ice Cream Parlor
description: An ice cream parlor in Springfield, Phineas Q. Butterfat's 5600 Flavors features a mascot resembling Marge Simpson. It has appeared in several episodes, including one where Homer faints into a giant sundae, and it is located inside the Springfield Mall.

A pharmaceutical manufacturing company, Pharm-Er John's Pharmaceuticals is where Lisa and Marge sought answers about high prescription drug costs after Mr. Burns eliminated the employee drug program. They encountered an unhelpful employee who resorted to showing them a video before leaving.

A pet shop in Springfield sells various animals, including parrots and hamsters. In one incident, Bart's prank with megaphones causes the parrots to repeat "testing!" and leads to a confrontation with henchmen while the Simpson family pursues Mr. Burns' assistant, Smithers.
A parking garage is located in Springfield, where Bart and Lisa were summoned by Smithers during Sideshow Bob's mayoral campaign to discuss his voting strategy.
The Peanut Street Hotel is located on Peanut Street, situated next to King Toot's and Moe's Tavern. It is featured in several episodes of The Simpsons.
A pet costume store located in the Promenade on the Grove at Springfield Heights.
Peanut Street is the location of Moe's Tavern and King Toot's music shop. It often intersects with Evergreen Terrace and has appeared in various episodes of The Simpsons.
Pepi's House is located in the poorer part of Springfield, where Pepi resides.

A peanut processing factory produces peanuts for consumption and is known for its eccentric boss, who requires employees to prepare for the unlikely event of an elephant breaking in. This bizarre precaution becomes a reality when an elephant attacks the boss while he is distracted.
A house that belonged to Mr. Burns' cousin and former lover, Lyla. It is notable for being one of the locations Bart passed by in a floating basket.

A pier with old carnival rides was once located in Springfield, but it was later rebuilt into condos. The Simpson family visited Paradise Pier before it was torn down, leading to a series of chaotic events involving Homer.

An expensive accommodation in Springfield, this resort is where Homer and Marge vacationed while Marge attended a meeting with fellow businesswomen. The name is a blend of Palm Springs and Springfield.

A pawn shop in Springfield, typically located next to the Aztec Theater, features the traditional three-ball sign for pawnbrokers. Homer once pawned the family's television to afford therapy, later retrieving it after receiving double their money back.

A dental office where the Simpsons have sought dental care, Painless Dentistry was previously known as Painful Dentistry. Dr. Wolfe is the assumed owner, and Lisa received braces there during the episode "Last Exit to Springfield."
A pharmacy located in Springfield's town square, Page's Pharmacy is situated next to Zesty's.
A gay bar located in downtown Springfield, P.F. Wangs is situated across the street from the Gridiron. Its name is a play on the real-life restaurant P.F. Chang's.

A cell phone company in Springfield, Omnitouch sponsors exhibits at the local museum, which frustrates Lisa Simpson. After Homer destroys the Bill of Rights, their technology is used to convert 742 Evergreen Terrace into a cellular tower, enhancing roaming coverage in the area.
A diner in Springfield, it offers a burger and squalor for under a dollar. Homer, Bart, and Mona Simpson visit the Overpass Diner after a reunion at the Four Street Overpass.
An all-you-can-eat cafeteria in downtown Springfield, this restaurant specializes in pork and is popular among local seniors. Patrons are limited to an eight-hour dining period.
A store located in Springfield Mall, Origami Designs specializes in selling various origami creations. It has appeared in multiple episodes of The Simpsons, showcasing its unique offerings.
A night club in Springfield, One Night Stan's is a popular venue for nightlife and entertainment.

A private all-boys Christian elementary school in Springfield, this academy follows a curriculum that excludes evolution and traditional astronomy. The school mascot is the Sluggin' Thessalonian, and Todd and Rod Flanders attended until they were withdrawn by their stepmother, Edna Krabappel.
A stadium in Springfield currently without a name, it has hosted performances by Coldplay and features a design reminiscent of the FTX Arena in Miami.

A testing center located in Proctorville, it is where Springfield Elementary's standardized tests are sent to be processed by a robot named Emma. The center's motto is "Controlling your destiny since 1925."

A construction company owned by the Rich Texan, Omni-Pave has a red brick headquarters featuring numerous windows and a large garage-style door. The building is marked by a prominent sign depicting a smiling steamroller chasing a frightened flower.
A service store in Springfield, Neat & Tidy Piano Movers is located next to Candy Most Dandy and Heinrich's Monocle Shop.

A historical district in Springfield, Olde Springfield Towne showcases colonial-era attractions and preserved sites, including the historical Fort Sensible. It serves as a destination for heritage tourism, offering tours and experiences related to Springfield's history.

A bank located in Springfield, it has been the site of various robberies, including one where Buck McCoy disarmed robbers with a lasso. The building was also famously dropped on Homer and Marge during a tornado, trapping them inside until they were rescued.
A tattoo studio located at Springfield Squidport, My First Tattoo features a character named White Weasel showing his tattoo to other children outside the establishment.

A museum dedicated to television and its celebrities once existed in Springfield, where Bart's class visited and Milhouse accidentally destroyed some figurines. The museum was later liquidated, with its assets sold off, including the Batmobile to Comic Book Guy.

A store briefly run by Marge Simpson, Murmur sold crystals that she believed helped improve children's grades. It was located in a mall and faced competition from a rival named Piper, but Marge eventually closed the store after it was revealed that the crystals were ineffective.

The highest mountain in Springfield, the Murderhorn stands over 20,000 feet tall and is known for its treacherous climbing conditions. Homer Simpson famously climbed it to promote the Powersauce bar, ultimately destroying the last peak to make the second to last peak the summit.

A house in Springfield known as the Murder House is infamous for a series of murders that took place there, with Mrs. Astor being the sole survivor. Marge attempts to sell the house to the Flanders but struggles due to its dark history, and after it is destroyed by Homer, Chief Wiggum, and Snake, she loses her job at Red Blazer Realty.

Nelson's father, Edward "Eddie" Muntz, is known for his motorbike and was once his son's soccer coach. He abandoned the family after taking his wife’s gold tooth and claiming he was going to buy cigarettes, later being found at a circus where he suffered an allergic reaction that left him disfigured and unable to speak.

An aquatic museum located on the waterfront, it features a prominent swordfish display. The museum has a reputation for causing trouble, as noted by Marge after a near-disaster involving a parade float.

Located inside the New Springfield Atoms Stadium, the Museum of Tolerance aims to promote understanding among fans of rival football teams. It features a scene where a Green Bay Packers fan and a Minnesota Vikings fan embrace after visiting the museum.
A district in Springfield known for its high crime rate, Murder Town is monitored by CCTV cameras, including those watched by Ned Flanders.

A house in the Rat's Nest neighborhood was the site of a murder, where the killer ominously wrote a warning in the victim's blood. A realtor unsuccessfully tried to sell the house to Marge and Homer Simpson.

An operating cider mill and tourist attraction on the outskirts of Springfield, it offers guided tours led by Randy, who explains cider production and the mill's history. Visitors can enjoy tastings, purchase apple-related products, and learn about the mill's quirky past, including its rat population.

An island located near Springfield, Mulberry Island is where Lisa and Nick attempted to share their first kiss under a mulberry tree. The trip was interrupted by police, and ultimately, Nick left Lisa before they could kiss, leading to a heartfelt moment between Lisa and Marge.
A food stand selling muffins, Much Ado About Muffins! features the slogan "To eat or not to eat?" and is located at Springfield Squidport, which was refurbished to accommodate new businesses.
A restaurant in Springfield, the Municipal House of Pancakes specializes in pancakes but is known for its popular syrup bottles. The Springfield Investorettes once held a meeting there.

A mountain located outside of Springfield, Mt. Useful features two cabins, a ranger's station, and a visitor's center that provides information about the mountain's ecology. The area is known for a team race organized by Mr. Burns for the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant staff, but it suffers from budget cuts that limit activities and have left its chairlifts outdated and potentially dangerous.

A water park in Springfield, Mt. Splashmore features thrilling attractions like the Devil's Gullet, which drops riders from 300 feet into a series of twisting tubes, and H2Whoa!, known for its intense water challenges. The park is staffed by teenage lifeguards and includes a kiddy pool called the Rock-a-Bye-Riptide, as well as a roller coaster named the Wave Walker.
A muffin store is under construction and will sell muffins. It is located on the same block as Edna Krabappel's store, Edna's Edibles, and other nearby muffin shops.

A mud wrestling-themed strip joint in Springfield, it is known for performances by various entertainers, including April Flowers. Grampa Simpson frequents the venue while trying to enjoy his inheritance, and it is also referred to as Club Mud.

A popular downhill skiing area in Springfield, Mt. Embolism is where the Simpson family goes to ski, although Marge stays in the lodge due to her fear of skiing. In the episode "Little Big Mom," she suffers an injury when a clock falls on her leg.

A gifted nursery school for infants and toddlers, it is where Lisa attempted to enroll Maggie after Apu and Dr. Hibbert's children attended. Initially rejected for not speaking, Maggie was later accepted when her high IQ was discovered, although she was eventually dismissed for cheating on an intelligence test.

Opened by Mr. Burns after Springfield legalized gambling, the casino featured him as a merman mascot and was located on the waterfront. It became notable for Homer Simpson's blackjack dealing, where his poor skills led to gamblers winning frequently, but was later demolished in an explosion to make way for a casino-themed family hotel.

Located on a spooky hill, this house was once home to Myrna Bellamy and her husband. It serves as a social gathering place for Myrna and her friends, and is the site of her murder and the theft of her jewel necklace.

A summer mansion owned by Mr. Burns, it was temporarily occupied by the Simpson family while filming a movie. The mansion features a medicine cabinet filled with old man ointments, which puzzled Marge when questioned about it.

A biological germ warfare laboratory operated by Charles Montgomery Burns was located on the campus of Springfield University. It faced protests from students and activists, including Mona Simpson, who infiltrated the lab to destroy its germ stockpile, leading to a long-standing conflict between Burns and the Simpson family.

A volcanic mountain located just outside of Springfield, Mt. Springfield is known for its past eruptions and incidents, including a fire caused by a discarded camera light bulb. Bart and Lisa were once trapped on the mountain until Homer and Barney rescued them, with Homer hanging upside down from a helicopter.

A large basketball stadium designed by Mr. Burns features architecture reminiscent of a beehive. It was built after he destroyed Lisa's bee sanctuary, which led to the stadium being overrun by Africanized bees, effectively turning it into a giant hive.

A funeral parlor in Springfield, Mourning Glory Funeral Home hosted Larry's funeral after his death at Moe's Tavern. Bart and Lisa also attended other funerals there, including those of Pauline McAllister and Eunice Quimby.

A Springfield-based company, Motherloving Sugar Corp. produces various unhealthy sugar products and is owned by Garth Motherloving. It supplies all the sugary items at the Kwik-E-Mart and was involved in a plot to include sugar in all food products in Springfield, eventually closing after a court ruling declared sugar products illegal, but later reopening with the help of Homer, Mr. Burns, Apu, and Garth.
A lodge located in the mountains, it serves as a getaway spot for Springfield residents.

A sandwich franchise chain restaurant, Marge opens Mother Hubbard's Sandwich Cupboard and hires Gil Gunderson, a squeaky-voiced teen, and Shauna Chalmers to work there. The franchise's logo features a sandwich designed to resemble an elderly woman, inspired by the nursery rhyme "Old Mother Hubbard."
A private prison owned by Mr. Burns, Montgomery Burns State Prison houses various inmates and is known for its harsh conditions.
A mountain in West Springfield features a carving of Carl Carson's face. Lenny reminisces about a summer spent creating the sculpture, although he and Carl have never discussed it.

A once-abandoned prison in Springfield, Morningwood Penitentiary was reopened by Mayor Quimby to use its electric chair as a deterrent against crime. Before its reopening, it was patrolled by an elderly guard, and Bart Simpson and Ralph Wiggum once trespassed there, playing with the electric chair the night before it was set to reopen.

A delicatessen in Springfield, Mort's Deli was once famous for housing the world's largest pickle until its theft in 1995. Despite the loss of prestige, Mort serves the best kugel in town and offers fatty pastrami sandwiches.

A motel is where the Simpson family stayed overnight while traveling to Itchy & Scratchy Land. During their stay, they witnessed a car crash outside their window, relieved it wasn't their own vehicle.

A Montessori school is located across the street from Springfield Elementary School. It is known for its alternative educational approach, which emphasizes hands-on learning and student-led activities.
A miniature version of Moe's Tavern, Moe's Express is a bar located in the food court, staffed by the Squeaky-Voiced Teen.

location_name: Montgomery Burns Institute For Soul Extraction
description: A facility located next to Springfield General Hospital, the Montgomery Burns Institute for Soul Extraction is where Mr. Burns is seen leading the devil into the building. It is featured in the episode "Holidays of Future Passed."
A motel located opposite Moe's Tavern, Moeview Motel is where Snake Jailbird once stayed after discovering gold coins. During his stay, Moe sneaked into Snake's room and stole the coins.

Moe's Brewing Co. is an alternate name for Moe's Tavern, which is known for its dive bar atmosphere. Visitors enter through a long tunnel that leads directly to the tavern, where Moe Szyslak serves drinks to patrons.

location_name: Miss Tillingham's School for Snotty Girls and Mama's Boys
description: A prestigious private preschool, Miss Tillingham's School for Snotty Girls and Mama's Boys was considered by Marge and Homer Simpson for enrolling Lisa, but the $6,000 tuition was unaffordable for the family, and scholarships were only available to minority groups.
A hardware store in Springfield, it is owned by a couple known as Mom and Pop, who are the store's employees. Homer Simpson once purchased a barbecue pit from this shop.
Moe's Apartment is located at 242 in downtown Springfield, serving as the residence of Moe Szyslak.

The local bar in Springfield is owned by Moe Szyslak and is known as Moe's Tavern. It is the only tavern in town and is located near King Toot's Music Store, with a reputation for being kept in business through bribes to Mayor Quimby.
A residential home where Mike and his son Freddy live, it appears in the episode "Homer's Night Out" when Mike punishes Freddy for looking at a photo of Homer Simpson and Princess Kashmir.

A homeless man living under a bridge in Springfield, he was formerly the owner of the Mickey Mouse massage parlor, which was shut down by the Walt Disney Company for copyright infringement. He is now unemployed and struggling to survive.

This spa features a sauna and a steam room. Homer Simpson once pretended to be wealthy to win free tickets, leading him and Marge to visit the steam room, where they encountered Don Vittorio DiMaggio.

An institute owned by Professor Frink, it specializes in helping individuals recover their memories, often serving residents from the Springfield Retirement Castle. Homer visited the institute to regain memories of a lost day.
A life insurance agency, Merry Widow Insurance Co. is featured in episodes such as "Homer's Triple Bypass" and "Lisa the Tree Hugger."

A mental institution in Springfield is where the Simpson family took Homer when they wanted him out of their lives. Homer was initially confused about the destination, fearing it could be a mental institution, a slaughterhouse, or Santa's village before realizing they were headed to a rock n' roll fantasy camp.
A chain of mattress stores, Mattress King was originally run by Morty Szyslak, Moe's father. Moe was once tasked with sabotaging competitors, leading to a mishap that ruined his family's business.

A freeway connects downtown Springfield to other regions, including Evergreen Terrace. It was renamed the Matlock Expressway by Mayor Quimby to appeal to the elderly, as the show "Matlock" is popular among them. The freeway remains incomplete due to construction issues and a gap caused by 742 Evergreen Terrace.
A restaurant located in Springfield Heights, Medieval Times features a medieval-themed dining experience. Marge once asked Homer to meet her there, but he did not show up.

A ski house owned by Mav and Portia serves as a temporary home for Bart, Lisa, and Maggie when Mav and Portia become their guardians. The children ultimately choose to return to their parents, Homer and Marge, after realizing they prefer to be with their natural family.

A novelty shop located near Springfield Town Square, Mel's Novelty Shop is featured in the video game "Bart vs. the Space Mutants." It sells items like cherry bombs and rockets, which Bart uses to complete various tasks in the game.

Mayor Quimby's mansion is the residence of Joe Quimby and his wife, Martha, featuring a large garden. The mansion hosts events like the annual Easter egg hunt, where the Simpson children have participated, and it has been depicted with Quimby's questionable modifications to his office, reflecting his womanizing tendencies.
