A house owned by Mav and Portia, located near Springfield Beach, where the Simpson family met the couple while looking for new guardians for their children. After a dinner invitation, Mav and Portia agreed to become the children's guardians during Christmas.

A fourth-grade student at Springfield Elementary School, Martin Prince is a friend and classmate of Bart Simpson, known for his academic brilliance and being a teacher's pet. He is often bullied by Nelson Muntz and is portrayed as a stereotypical nerd.
A shop briefly seen in "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire," it is located opposite the Circus of Values and the Springfield Mall. Its specific purpose is not detailed in the series.

A retail chain owned by Mapple, the Mapple Store sells various products including mypods, myphones, and the Mapple Void computer. The Springfield Mall location features a cube-shaped design with blue walls made of video projection screens and includes a Brainiac Bar for technical support.
A food market is located in downtown Springfield on a one-way road. The surrounding area changes in its appearances throughout the series.
A former department store, Marvyn's was one of the many shops where Marge had a voucher, but it has since closed down. It serves as a parody of Mervyn's.
An aquarium and marine mammal park in Springfield, Marine World features daily dolphin shows in a large amphitheater. A sign at its entrance indicates that the attraction is no longer educational.

A street in Springfield Heights, Mammon Street is home to Burns Manor and connects to Croseus Street. Bart and Santa's Little Helper walked down this street after Bart was sent to his room on Thanksgiving.
Business dealings related to Malibu Stacy take place at this headquarters. It serves as the central hub for the iconic fashion doll's operations.

Main Street is a prominent road in Springfield that features in the opening sequence of the show, where Bart often skateboards past citizens and bus stops. It hosts various parades and is home to several notable locations, including Moe's Tavern and King Toot's Music Store.

A restaurant in Springfield, Magic Palace features performances by magicians, including Diablo and a mentalist named Questo, who served drinks to the Simpson family. The venue has hosted events like the World Magic Championship and Lisa's magic show.

A workshop that allows residents to craft various items, it initially served as a special event location in the game "The Simpsons: Tapped Out" before becoming a regular income-producing building. Its name is likely inspired by the real-life Build-A-Bear Workshop chain.

A business run by Homer Simpson, Magic Craphole Waste Removal allowed residents to dispose of their trash into a black hole that Lisa brought into their home. The black hole eventually grew large enough to consume most of Springfield.

A massage parlor in Springfield, it is where Homer took Marge to distract her while the kids disposed of unwanted peaches. During a massage, Homer revealed his plan to her, but the relaxing experience helped her forget about the peaches.

A waffle house in Springfield, Luftwaffles is designed to resemble a World War I pickelhaube, complete with a giant waffle around the spike. The restaurant is mentioned when the Simpson family considers dining options after church.

A modern nightclub created by Moe after attending bartending school, M is an upscale version of Moe's Tavern that serves no Duff products. It fails to attract customers due to their snobbish behavior, leading Moe to return to his original bar, Moe's Tavern.

An Italian fine dining restaurant and pizzeria located in Springfield's Little Italy, it is owned and managed by Luigi Risotto. The Simpsons frequently order take-out pizza from here, and it is a popular hangout for Fat Tony and the Springfield mafia, known for its preferential customer service and fresh lobster selection.
A gymnastic facility owned by Lugash, where characters like Carrie, Tina, and Lisa practice gymnastics.

location_name: Luck o' the Irish Wishing Well
description: A wishing well in Springfield, owned by a leprechaun, allows people to toss in coins and make wishes. Homer and Bart once hid inside to collect the coins, leading to a confrontation with the leprechaun.
A bus stop in the Springfield transit system is located on the Lower East Side.
Lower Springfield Lake is a body of water located in Springfield, often associated with outdoor activities and local events. It serves as a recreational area for the residents of Springfield.

A district in Springfield with a large Jewish community, it features businesses such as Tannen's Fatty Meats, Izzy's Deli, and Temple Beth Springfield. Krusty the Clown grew up here, and it includes a Jewish Walk of Fame.
Louie Jr. is the son of Louie, a member of the Springfield Mafia, and works under Michael D'Amico and Fat Tony. He is part of the junior mafia associated with the criminal activities in Springfield.
This district in Springfield is mentioned as a bus stop name. It is named Little Newark, likely referencing the real-life city of Newark in New Jersey.

A recycling plant owned by Lisa and Mr. Burns was created to help him recover his lost fortune. Made entirely from recycled materials, it produced a controversial product called "Little Lisa Slurry," which was made from sea life and sold as pig food before being sold to a fish stick company for $120 million.
A shop in Springfield that sells lottery tickets and alcohol, Lotto 'N' Liquor is located across the street from Sleazy Sam's Payday Loans and next to Bail Bonds and Beyond.

A district in Springfield, Little Seattle features a smaller version of Seattle's Space Needle, numerous coffee shops, and a vibrant grunge music scene. It is known for its cultural similarities to Seattle and was the venue for Homer Simpson's grunge band, Sadgasm.
A district in Springfield, Little Bangkok is located next to Tibet Town and Chinatown, and is home to a Thai food factory.

A neighborhood in Springfield, Little Ukraine is home to the Ukrainian community and features various Ukrainian shops and buildings. Notable businesses include Cossacks Fifth Avenue, Insane in the Ukraine, Tsarbucks, and Trotsky's Ice-Skating Rink.

An ethnic enclave in Springfield, Little Italy is home to Luigi's Italian Restaurant and the Springfield Mafia's clubhouse. Milhouse once visited this district with Lisa, where he helped translate for Luigi, who spoke with a strong Italian accent.

location_name: Lisa Simpson Home for Abandoned Animals
description: A home for abandoned animals was established by Bart to help Lisa care for the animals she adopted from a pound. After a mishap with a tiger, the animals were at risk of being euthanized, prompting Bart to organize a benefit concert to fund the creation of this sanctuary.

location_name: Lil' Vicki Valentine's School of Dance
description: A dance school in Springfield, it is run by Vicki Valentine, a former child star. Lisa once asked Marge to enroll her there to learn how to dance, and the walls are decorated with posters of Vicki's movies.

A planned theme park in Springfield National Forest, Lisa Land was conceived by the Rich Texan as a tribute to Lisa Simpson, whom he mistakenly believed had died. After Lisa protested against the park, a log resembling her head, which was part of the park's design, caused widespread destruction as it rolled through Springfield and beyond.

In the future, Lisa Simpson resides in a modern house made primarily of metal, featuring a recycle sign that suggests it is constructed from recycled materials. She lives there with Milhouse Van Houten and her daughter, Zia Simpson, who is often preoccupied with the ultranet.
A music school in Springfield, Li'l Ludwig's Music School is where Lisa once impressed her teacher with her saxophone skills, despite being told she inherited stubby fingers from her father.
A liquor store supplied alcoholic beverages in Springfield but went out of business after Fort Springfield was closed. It is unclear if it reopened after the military base resumed operations.

A deserted movie theater in Springfield, the Limited Appeal Theatre is largely forgotten by the community. Its lobby features outdated movie posters and possibly stale food, while the screening rooms are in poor condition, with skinny chairs and rotten wallpaper, making for an unpleasant viewing experience.
A former home textile shop, Linens-N-Such was one of the many stores where Marge had a voucher before it closed down. It parodies the real-life store Linens 'n Things.

A member of the Springfield Mafia, Legs is known for his catchphrase "Shut up-a your face!" and often serves as muscle alongside Fat Tony and Louie. He is characterized by his threatening demeanor and loyalty to his boss, Fat Tony.

A kiosk located in the Towne Centre, Leftorium Express is run by Ned Flanders, who downsized from a larger store due to competition from the nearby Southpaw Superstore. The kiosk shares space with a makeup store.

The Li'l Chapel is a garage at 742 Evergreen Terrace that Homer converted into a place for conducting weddings, initially for homosexual couples. Notable ceremonies include those of Patty Bouvier and Veronica, Julio and Thad, and Cletus and Brandine Spuckler.

Lenny Leonard's house is a standard single-story home located in the Pressboard Estates district, possibly on Evergreen Terrace, across from the Springfield Stamp Museum. Lenny lived here before moving into his apartment.

A theme park based on LEGO bricks features models of famous buildings constructed from the toy. In Springfield, Mr. Burns dumped nuclear waste beneath the park, causing the LEGO models to come to life, leading to chaotic events such as the United States Capitol chasing children.
A superstore specializing in left-handed goods, it competes with the Leftorium. The store is a parody of Walmart.

location_type: Springfield Mafia hangout / money launder front
description: A hidden underground location, the Legitimate Businessman's Social Club serves as a hangout and money laundering front for the Springfield Mafia. Bart Simpson briefly worked there as a bartender, and the club is known for its illegal activities, including the storage of firearms, counterfeit cash, and drugs, as well as its involvement in shady dealings with Mayor Quimby.

A bodyguard training school owned by Leavelle, it offers courses that include protecting a watermelon as if it were a celebrity and practicing defensive maneuvers against simulated threats. Homer Simpson attended this academy while training to be a bodyguard for Mayor Quimby.

A tea house in Springshire, The Leaf Garret was closed down by health inspectors due to unsanitary conditions, specifically cakes made from rat droppings. Marge and Bart discovered it while riding a bike built for two.
A restaurant in Springfield, Le Snotterie is where Moe had a date and used a love-testing machine located in the men's room to assist him.

A donut shop in Springfield, Lard Lad Donuts features a giant mascot of a young boy holding a donut. The shop is popular among locals, including Chief Wiggum, and has been depicted in various storylines, including being shut down by a health inspector in The Simpsons Movie.

A hair salon located in Springfield Mall, Le Pamperie is known for its vibrant blue hairstyles. It appears in the episode "Radioactive Man" when Maggie mistakenly thinks a woman's hairstyle belongs to Marge.

A highly polluted lake in Springfield, Lake Springfield is known for its mutated fish and was once a dumping site for waste from the nuclear power plant. Efforts to clean it up have been made, but pollution continues to be a problem, leading to environmental interventions.
A cane shop in Springfield, it advertises its products to residents of the Springfield Retirement Castle.

A dude ranch owned by the Rich Texan, Lazy I Ranch is where the Simpson family once visited. Lisa was initially unhappy due to the ranch's history of Native American lives lost, but her experience changed after meeting Luke Stetson. The ranch features activities like barn dances and is located near Native American land.

A French restaurant in Springfield, Le Petite Appétit is where Lisa and Nick once had a date with other children. During the visit, Lisa imagined she was in France while the waiter served them apple juice.

A burlesque house in Springfield, La Maison Derrière is owned by Belle and features gambling, drinking, and entertainment. Bart Simpson has worked there in various roles, including emcee, while the establishment has attracted a diverse clientele, prompting community controversy and a town meeting led by Marge Simpson to address its existence.

Springfield has a variety of laws, including local regulations and standard U.S. laws. Notable laws include the town charter that allows food dropped on the ground to be claimed by the village idiot, the legalization of gambling to boost the economy, and the legalization of same-sex marriage to attract tourism. Additionally, there are laws regarding illegal immigration, a brief period of marijuana legalization, and various quirky regulations such as banning hatless individuals during daylight hours.

The television studio in Springfield where "The Krusty the Klown Show" is recorded is known as Krustylu Studios. It is located near the Channel 6 studio lot, across the street from the box factory, and was once owned by an unknown chairman before being bought by Channel 6.

A theme park owned by Krusty the Clown, Krustyland features various attractions, including the infamous "Simpsons Ride." The park has a reputation for dangerous rides, which Krusty claims were not responsible for any visitor injuries.

A convenience store in Springfield, the Kwik-E-Mart is managed by Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, with occasional help from Sanjay. The store is known for its outrageous prices and has been depicted in various future scenarios involving Apu's children.

A riverboat casino located in Springfield, La Belle Frottage Casino was where Marge, Ned, Helen, Rev. Lovejoy, Sideshow Mel, and Agnes counted cards to raise money for the rebuilding of the First Church of Springfield.

A college that trains individuals to become clowns, Krusty's Clown College was founded by Krusty's accountant to help alleviate Krusty's financial troubles. The college has been taken over by Fat Tony as part of Krusty's debt repayment and has shifted its focus to training clowns to rob from children after performances.

A fast-food burger restaurant chain founded by Krusty the Clown, Krusty Burger has multiple locations across the United States and even in Paris, France. Known for its unhealthy menu items, the restaurant has faced various controversies, including a disastrous promotion during the 1984 Olympics and a brief period when it was taken over by the IRS.

A daycare center owned by Krusty the Clown, it charged a basic fee of $1,000 per month, with additional costs for diaper changes. Marge considered leaving Maggie there but ultimately decided to start her own daycare due to its high cost and low quality.

Krusty's Mansion is the residence of Krusty the Clown, who once had to auction off his possessions after being arrested for tax fraud. The mansion features a swimming pool where Krusty keeps shrimp, as he does not swim.
A limited-time stadium hosts the show "Krusty's Kristmas On Ice," with admission prices set at $40 for adults and $39 for children.

A fast food restaurant located on an offshore oil rig, Krusty Burger Oil Rig was initially deemed unviable due to its remote location. However, it became a temporary refuge for Homer, Bart, Ned, and Rod when they got lost at sea and discovered the burgers.
Krusty's Apartment is where Krusty the Clown lived, as seen in the first season episode "Krusty Gets Busted." Later episodes depict him residing in a house instead.

A fourth-grade teacher at Springfield Elementary, Edna Krabappel was known for her sharp wit and catchphrases. She had a tumultuous personal life, including a marriage to Ned Flanders after the death of her previous partner, and was characterized as a heavy smoker and occasional drinker. Edna passed away in 2013, following the death of her voice actress, Marcia Wallace.

An adult recreational retreat, Klub Krusty was built on the site of the former Kamp Krusty. It features attractions like a kids' club, a spa, and various adult activities, allowing parents to relax while their children play.
A Korean district located in downtown Springfield, Korea Town features various Korean businesses and cultural elements.

A car dealership in Springfield, Kliff's Kar Chalet is where the Simpson family purchased a car after Bart fabricated a story about a burglar stealing their Christmas gifts, prompting the townspeople to generously support them.

A fast food restaurant in Springfield, Kentucky Fried Panda served panda meat and was destroyed twice: first by the collapse of the Lisa-land log tower and later by a chain reaction caused by Homer throwing away a leaky car battery. The restaurant is a parody of Kentucky Fried Chicken and Panda Express.
A lodge of cabins in Springfield, Kozy Kabins has been visited by Homer and Marge on three occasions, including trips with the Flanders family and their children, Lisa, Bart, and Maggie.

Springfield's premier music store offers a wide variety of instruments and is located next to Moe's Tavern. Lisa has purchased both of her saxophones from King Toot's, and Homer once got a saxophone reed there for her recital.
A lute store located in the kingdom of Springfieldia, King Lute's appears in "The Serfsons" and is situated next to Moe's Tavern. It serves as a parody of King Toot's music store.
A jazz music station in Springfield, KJAZZ has 152 listeners and plays music in memory of Bleeding Gums Murphy, thanks to a saxophone album gifted by Lisa Simpson.

A children's toy store located inside the Springfield Mall, it features a variety of toys including Sergeant Thug's Mountaintop Command Post and Malibu Stacy dolls. The store also stocks the highly-anticipated Lisa Lionheart doll, which faced competition from a reworked Malibu Stacy on its release day.

A summer camp for kids, Kamp Krusty is depicted as having harsh conditions, with nature hikes described as grim and the arts and crafts center likened to a workhouse. Bart and Lisa Simpson express their despair, hoping for rescue from the camp's dismal environment.
Kent Brockman's mansion is a luxurious residence that he purchased after winning the Springfield lottery. It serves as the home of the local news anchor in the Simpsons universe.
A luxurious, modern apartment serves as the residence of Karl, who is seen throughout Springfield in later episodes. His apartment first appears when he calls Homer about an anniversary present.

A karate school in Springfield is led by Akira, who teaches martial arts. Marge and Homer visited the school to learn karate, where Akira demonstrated his skills by defeating Marge and playfully torturing Homer.

A New Age shop offers various treatments and life aids from different cultures, including dream catchers and herbal teas. Lisa Simpson visited in search of stress relief, leading to an experience with sensory deprivation tanks, but the store faced financial difficulties and was at risk of closing.
A store that exclusively sells vinegar appears in the episode "Sex, Pies, and Idiot Scrapes."

A bookstore located within Springfield International Airport, it exclusively sells books by Michael Crichton and Stephen King. An encounter with an employee revealed that it does not carry works by Robert Ludlum.
A store located at Springfield Squidport, it specializes in selling rainsticks.

The daughter of Johnny Tightlips was seen attending a daddy and me class with Homer and Maggie Simpson, as well as Frankie the Squealer and his son. She bears a strong resemblance to Poonam Nahasapeemapetilon.

A junkyard in Springfield is where Cletus collects dead animals, which he intended to use for a wedding feast. Lisa once found herself there after taking the wrong bus and asked Cletus for a ride to the museum, but she ran away when she realized she would have to sit with the dead animals.
A cape shop located in the kingdom of Springfieldia, Just Half-Capes was featured when Homer and others participated in stoning Snake for his ability to read.
A store located in the Springfield Mall, The Jerky Hut specializes in meat products and has been known to advertise sausage sales.
A business that sells teleporters is featured in the future setting of Springfield, as seen on a billboard in downtown.
A restaurant in Springfield, Johnny Fiestas is where Marge first met Tammy and her cheery red tomatoes to gossip about their husbands.
The central park in Springfield features the Springfield Bowl, paddle-boating, and picnic areas. It is known as Jebediah Springfield Park.
A facility in Springfield dedicated to the disposal of jetpacks. It is featured in the episode "Sky Police."
A shop located in the Promenade on the Grove at Springfield Heights, it specializes in handmade jewelry created by Lisa Simpson's sister, Maggie.
Joe's and Moe's are rival pubs located in Shelbyville and Springfield, respectively, known for their competitive atmosphere and local popularity.

A jazz club in Springfield, Jazzy Goodtime's features a children's jazz band performing during brunch. Customers can request the waiter to scat sing the menu, and it is where Bart began his journey to becoming a famous drummer, causing jealousy in Lisa.

A jazz club where musicians perform, the Jazz Hole is known for hosting Bleeding Gums Murphy, who often played there. Lisa once took her family to enjoy his music, and she returned seeking culture when she feared losing her intelligence.
A toy shop in Springfield, J.R.R. Toykin's is visited by Ralph and Bart after they steal Chief Wiggum's key to the town. The name is a pun on the author J.R.R. Tolkien.

An amusement park themed around the Itchy & Scratchy cartoon, Itchy & Scratchy Land is known for its simulated violence and chaotic attractions. The park features various themed areas, including Torture Land and Explosion Land, and offers rides like the Head Basher and Itchy's Mine Field Log Ride. On its opening day, the animatronic characters malfunctioned, leading to a chaotic evacuation, but the Simpsons managed to save themselves using cameras to exploit the robots' sensitivity to flash photography.

A deli located in Springfield's lower east side, Izzy's Deli features sandwiches named after celebrities, including one for Krusty the Clown. The owner, Izzy Kadetz, and his wife Rose are known for their snarky interactions with customers.
Itchy & Scratchy International is the studio where the Itchy & Scratchy Show cartoons are produced. It is modeled after the real-life building where Film Roman creates animated content.
A store located at Springfield Squidport, It’s a Wonderful Knife specializes in selling knives.
A store selling a variety of merchandise and souvenirs from the cartoon "Itchy & Scratchy," including t-shirts, toys, and collectibles, as well as discounted Poochie items.
An air conditioner store located on Walnut Street in downtown Springfield, It Blows was considered by Homer for a new air conditioner before he opted to buy a saxophone for Lisa instead.
A baseball stadium in Springfield, it serves as the home field for the Springfield Isotopes.

The IRS building in Springfield serves as the regional office of the Internal Revenue Service, overseeing taxation and ensuring compliance. Homer Simpson was once brought here after failing to file his taxes properly.

This lovers' lane in Springfield is a popular spot for couples to make out in their vehicles, as well as for teenagers. Notable events include Homer proposing to Marge there, and Artie Ziff making unwanted advances on her after prom.

Located in the southern part of Springfield, this road features the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant and a rendering plant in the Rat's Nest neighborhood. Bart once purchased a factory at 35 Industry Way, which was later destroyed, and bus route 22A services this area.

A student at Springfield Elementary, the Indian Nerd is part of a group of outcasts who gather in a hidden room known as the "refuge of the damned." This location serves as a sanctuary for nerds, where they can escape from bullies.

A store located in Springfield Mall, the International House of Answering Machines specializes in selling answering machines and other communications equipment. Its name is a play on the International House of Pancakes (IHOP).
An old and hidden burial mound is located in Springfield, discovered by Bart and Lisa while cycling. They initially kept it a secret, but Bart later revealed it to Milhouse, which upset Lisa.

Hiram Simpson's house is the residence of Hiram, Mabel, and their daughter Eliza. The family became involved in a plot to help a slave named Virgil escape to Canada, leading to a confrontation with Colonel Burns.

A bird sanctuary located in Springfield, it features a high bird feeder shaped like a diner. Visitors often face aggressive birds seeking birdseed, as highlighted by a scene where Hans Moleman requests a large seed bell.

A medical practice run by Dr. Julius Hibbert, this organization provides various health services, including optometry. It is featured in the episode "The Last Temptation of Homer," where Marge takes Bart for an eye examination.

A mental health hospital located in Springfield's Little Ukraine district, it is referenced in the episode "The Falcon and the D'ohman." The facility is notable for its connection to Wayne Slater, who passed by it while on a mission to rescue Homer.

A clothing store that sold hemp-made apparel, Hemp City was destroyed when Lisa's land log traveled through Springfield. Its destruction upset fans of the store, including members of the band Dirt First.
A shop in Springfield, Heinrich's Monocle Shop was previously located where a now-closed cheap gun store stands. In Season 23, a bus stop is seen in front of it.

A mechanic business specializing in high-pressure tire sales employs questionable practices to deceive customers into spending more money. Homer Simpson was misled into purchasing new tires after being told his were defective, while Wally Kogen was also scammed into buying a useless product.

A district of Springfield, Hickton is known for being the location of one of Snake's hideouts, where he once held Homer and Gloria hostage. Cletus alerted the police to their location, suggesting he may also reside in Hickton.

A shopping mall located in Springfield, Heavenly Hills Mall was built in Sabertooth Meadow, where Lisa Simpson initially protested due to fossil discoveries. The mall's owners staged a hoax involving a fake angel skeleton to promote the mall, claiming it signified the end of high prices.

A medical center in Springfield, Hellman Avenue Medical Plaza is where Marge and Homer took their children for flu shots from Dr. Hibbert. Hans Moleman was also a patient there, waiting for a kidney transplant.

The Halloween Stage is featured at the beginning of several "Treehouse of Horror" episodes, where characters like Marge and Homer introduce the spooky content. Marge often warns viewers about the frightening nature of the episodes, advising parents to tuck their children in before watching.

An underground techno and industrial rave club in downtown Springfield, this nightclub is frequented by goths, punks, and social outcasts. Marge visits the Hate Box with Ruth Powers, where she encounters Otto and Mayor Quimby, who is dancing with body paint and glow sticks.

A Japanese restaurant located on Elm Street, The Happy Sumo offers a variety of sushi, including the potentially deadly fugu, which can only be prepared by the master sushi chef. The restaurant also features karaoke and provides a map to the hospital on its menus for fugu-related emergencies.

Located inside Springfield Mall, this tattoo parlor is where Bart Simpson attempted to get a tattoo of the word "mother." Marge intervened before it was completed, leading to a costly tattoo removal procedure.

This Halloween store changes its theme seasonally and was previously known as the Columbus Day Headquarters. It is located across the street from the official Halloween Headquarters, suggesting a rivalry between the two.
A fast food restaurant in Springfield, Hamburger Heaven serves a variety of burgers.

A barber shop in Springfield, Hairy Shearers is where Homer learns about the salon's financial struggles while trying to help Marge with her hair. Julio works at this location, and there are at least two Hairy Shearers in Springfield.
A liquor store located in Springfield, Hal's Liquor is featured in episodes such as "Poppa's Got a Brand New Badge."

A restaurant located in Little Ethiopia, it serves traditional Ethiopian dishes such as zilzil minchet alicha wot, doro wot, and kifto sandwich. The establishment is visited by Marge, Bart, and Lisa in the episode "The Food Wife."
A hamburger stall located in Springfield National Forest, it sells burgers and was established following sightings of Bigfoot.

An apartment building located in the Cemetery District, it serves as a residence for retirees, including Jacqueline Bouvier and Dorothy. The Hal Roach Apartments are named after the American film and television producer known for the Laurel and Hardy and Our Gang series.

A fast food restaurant in Springfield, Gulp 'n' Blow offers drive-thru service and features items like tacos and onion rings. Homer Simpson worked there when he and Marge were newlyweds, and he later quit to reapply at the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant after Marge reassured him of her love.

A department store located next to Springfield Mall, Hailstone's shares a parking lot and an enclosed walkway with the mall. Its exact relationship with the mall is unclear, as it is sometimes absent in exterior shots of the mall.

The groundskeeper and janitor at Springfield Elementary School is a Scottish character known as Groundskeeper Willie. He supervises the children during recess and is often seen with his distinctive red hair and thick accent, having a complicated relationship with Principal Seymour Skinner.
A guinea pig rescue and adoption center is located in Crystal County, just outside the Springfield city limits. Lisa adopted a guinea pig named Pokey from this center.

A musical instrument store in Springfield, Guitar Central is where Homer and Lisa shop for instruments after King Toot's is closed. An employee named Stig sells Homer various items, including a bass guitar.
A recording studio in Springfield, Groovetone Records is where Homer, Lenny, Carl, and Lou recorded their songs before forming the band Sadgasm.
A retail store located in the Springfield Mall, it specializes in selling various gum products. It is situated next to Lionel Hutz's law firm, "I Can't Believe It's a Law Firm!"

A district in Springfield, Greektown is mentioned by Chief Wiggum when he asks for gyros while pretending to communicate with a dispatcher. Its existence is questionable, as it has never been shown in the series, leading to speculation that it may be nonexistent.
A fast food restaurant located in the Springfield Mall food court, Greek Town offers a variety of Greek cuisine. It is part of a diverse selection of eateries within the mall.

An Orthodox church located on the Springfield town square, it is featured during the Western Catholic Easter celebration, where citizens gather and women wear colorful hats. An Orthodox bishop is seen in front of the church, marking Palm Sunday.

A retail store in Springfield, Grandma's World offers a variety of items catering to older customers, including hard candies, picture frames, doilies, seashell soaps, and potpourri. Abraham Simpson once shopped here for a gift for his girlfriend, Beatrice Simmons.
A grassy hilled area on Elm Street is where Bart and his friends, Jimbo, Kearney, and Dolph, often gather to look at clouds.

A chain of novelty shops owned by Goose Gladwell, Goose's Gags and Gifts is known for its humorous merchandise, including rubber chickens and magic 8-balls. The store gained national attention when Bart's t-shirts, distributed by Goose, became popular and were eventually purchased by the Disney corporation.

A grease recycling plant in Springfield allows residents to recycle used cooking grease. Homer and Bart once took their cans of grease there, where an employee weighed them and paid Homer sixty-three cents.

A 1950s-themed diner, Greaser's Cafe featured car-shaped tables and served classic diner food. The restaurant hosted nightly dance competitions, with a Harley Davidson motorcycle as the prize, which Homer and Marge won shortly before it went out of business.
A store located in the Springfield Mall, Goodbye Kitty is a parody of the popular Hello Kitty brand.
This retirement village features a golf course and is frequented by Harlan Dondelinger. Homer and Bart once visited him here to discuss his election cheating.

A honey production business that keeps bees, Goldsboro's Honey is known for an incident where the bees left the location to gather sugar from a pile outside 742 Evergreen Terrace, the home of Homer Simpson.
A clothing store located in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, Gold Navy parodies the real-life retailer Old Navy.
A workshop where Giuseppe creates fireworks.
Chester Lampwick owns a mansion made of gold, located in the affluent district of Springfield. This opulent residence is known as the Gold House.
A strip joint in Springfield, Girlesque is named as a play on burlesque. Homer and Bart were misled to believe that Princess Kashmir was performing there.
A lingerie store located in the Springfield Mall, Girdles N' Such sells fancy lingerie and was considered by Homer as a potential birthday gift for Marge.

An elegant, upscale restaurant in Springfield, The Gilded Truffle is known for its truffle dishes and is considered the fanciest restaurant in town. It has been featured in various episodes, including moments where Homer and Marge planned to celebrate their anniversary there, and Homer dined with friends while dreaming of historical events.
A shop located in the Promenade on the Grove at Springfield Heights, Gifts for Sisters specializes in items for female siblings.
A gift shop located in Itchy & Scratchy Land, it sells various merchandise including name license plates and toys of characters like the disgruntled goat, Uncle Ant, and Ku Klux Clam.
A clothing store located at the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, Georgio Ourmoney is a parody of Giorgio Armani.
A gift store located at Springfield Squidport offers a variety of items for purchase.

A private gentlemen's club in Springfield, it features a warm buffet, color television, and entertainment. The club operates every evening from 8 PM to 2 AM and hosts a special event called "Tell You Their Real Names Tuesday."

A rock formation resembling a face, Geezer Rock was dedicated as a national park in Springfield. Its collapse occurred when Homer Simpson removed a tree from its eye, leading to chaos and the presumed death of Mr. Burns, who ultimately survived.
A gift store is located at Springfield International Airport, offering various items for travelers.

A general store in Springfield features a design reminiscent of shops from the 1940s. It is notable for being the location where Abe and Jasper were sitting when the air raid siren was activated for the first time in three years due to a comet threat.

location_name: Gee Your Hair Smells Terrific Arena
description: A sports arena in Springfield, it hosts both basketball and hockey games. The Ice-O-Topes are one of the hockey teams that play there, and Lisa once helped a player score a goal during a game.
A waterbed warehouse located in Springfield, it is mentioned in the episode "The Bart of War" as being near the tribal lands of local Native American Jim Proudfoot.

This district features various businesses, including upscale men's clothing stores and bakeries. It is home to residents Julio and Grady, and Homer has lived with them at one point. The area is known for its cable car system and is frequented by Waylon Smithers.
A former toy shop located at the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, GAO Schwarz was one of the many stores where Marge had a voucher before it closed down. It parodies the real-life FAO Schwarz.

A seafood restaurant in Springfield, The Frying Dutchman is owned by Captain Horatio McCallister and features an all-you-can-eat buffet. The menu exclusively offers seafood, and it is known for its poorly-prepared dishes, which led to Homer Simpson's infamous eating spree that nearly bankrupted the establishment.
A firm located in Springfield, G. Bannister & Associates is featured in the episode "Lemon of Troy."

An auction house where Homer and Bart attempted to buy the Kissing Lincolns coin, only to be outbid by Mr. Burns. The Simpson family later visited to sell a painting they purchased from the Van Houtens.
A stall at Springfield Squidport, Fried Dough sells fried dough, which is humorously labeled as America's worst legal food and is said to never leave your body.

A wedding supply store in Springfield, it is Marge's third favorite and specializes in extreme weddings, including triathlons and zero-gravity events. Marge and Lisa once visited to purchase items for Ned and Edna's wedding party, where they faced criticism from Luann, Helen, and Bernice.
The funeral parlor is located near the Springfield Cemetery and serves as the venue for main funeral services, including Uncle Hubert's funeral. It is staffed by a funeral parlor worker.

A pawn shop in Springfield, it is where Homer pawns Bart's trophies and discovers Grampa's watch in a display case. The shop is owned by Dumlee, who initially offers to dispose of the trophies for ten dollars but later engages in a humorous exchange with Homer regarding a trophy for the best pawn shop.

Apu transformed the Kwik-E-Mart into the Freak-E-Mart after Jasper froze himself in the freezer, selling unusual items with Frostillicus as the main attraction. When the freezer failed and Frostillicus thawed, Apu rebranded the store as the Nude-E-Mart, combining retail with a strip club atmosphere.
A stall at Springfield Squidport, Fresh Squeezed Lemonade sells lemonade. Homer, Bart, and Lisa have been seen passing by this stall during their visit to the area.

A peach orchard in Springfield where visitors can pick their own peaches. The Simpson family visited the orchard, where Bart and Lisa met Ewell Freestone, who entertained them with a lengthy song about peaches.
A luxury hotel is located in Springfield, where Chloe Talbot stayed during her visit. Lisa once secretly hid in her car to accompany her before leaving the hotel.
A strip joint in Springfield, Foxy Boxing is mentioned in "Homer's Night Out" where Homer and Bart are misled about a performance by April Flowers.

A large, multistory department store owned by billionaire Arthur Fortune, the Fortune Megastore offers a wide variety of goods across three levels, including electronics, books, and sporting goods. It features a coffee shop and a children's miniature train ride operated by Gil Gunderson.

The main military compound in Springfield is Fort Springfield, where Principal Skinner served as a sergeant during his time in the U.S. Army. Parts of the fort have been preserved as a historical site, which Springfield Elementary School visited for a field trip.

A U.S. Army base located near Springfield, Fort Fragg features areas such as a shower room and a tank hangar. Bart Simpson once infiltrated the base, stole tank keys, and hijacked a tank, causing chaos in Springfield before shooting down a satellite.

A historical building in Olde Springfield Towne, Fort Sensible is named after a captain who was killed by the enemy after being sent out to negotiate. The fort's name reflects the tragic outcome of that decision.
A cookie store located in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, Forgotten Amos Cookies has at least three locations in Springfield, with two situated in the Towne Centre.

A barn at the Movementarian farm is said to house a spaceship that promises to take followers to a planet called Blisstonia. When Homer attempts to reveal the truth, he discovers the spaceship, but it ultimately falls apart, exposing the leader's fraudulent intentions.

An online small business owned by Ned and Maude Flanders, Flancrest Enterprises specializes in selling religious hook-rugs. Homer discovers the business after mistakenly receiving Ned's mail, which inspires him to start his own venture, Compu-Global-Hyper-Mega-Net.
A shoe store located in Springfieldia, Fool Locker is featured in the episode "The Serfsons." It parodies the American footwear and sportswear chain Foot Locker.

A bomb shelter is located in the backyard of the Flanders family's home at 744 Evergreen Terrace. During a comet scare, the Simpson family and other Springfield residents sought refuge there, but the shelter was ultimately destroyed when a weather balloon caused its collapse.

A family restaurant, Flickey's is mentioned during the Simpsons' trip to Itchy & Scratchy Land, where they see multiple signs advertising its distance. Bart expresses a desire to stop there, but Homer declines, and they learn the next Flickey's is 25,000 miles away.

After the death of Fat Tony, his cousin Fit Tony moved from San Diego to Springfield to take over the Springfield mafia. Initially in good shape, he eventually began to overeat due to the pressures of his new role, leading to his transformation into Fat Tony, resembling his late cousin.

A Protestant Christian church in Springfield, it is affiliated with the Western branch of American Reform Presbylutheranism. Reverend Lovejoy serves as the church's pastor, and many residents regularly attend services.

A strip club located in Springfield, Florence of Arabia is situated next to the Ye Olde Off-Ramp Inn. Homer and Bart visit the club in search of Princess Kashmir, only to be directed to April Flowers at the nearby Girlesque.

Located in Springfield Mall, the food court features various dining options including Crouching Tiger Hidden Eggroll, Moe's Express, and The Picky Vegan. It has restrooms nearby and provides access to a hallway leading to an exit.

An apartment complex located off a turn when heading towards the power plant, it is home to Jacques, a man who once pursued Marge Simpson. Their relationship began when they met at the Bowlarama, where Jacques offered her bowling lessons, leading to romantic tension before Marge ultimately chose to stay with Homer.
A field trip destination for Springfield Elementary School, the fireworks testing range is located near the route taken by the school bus on its way to the box factory.

location_name: Fireworks, Candy, and Puppy Dogs Store
description: A store that sells fireworks, candy, and puppies, it features barking puppies in the windows and is located next to the Springfield Retirement Castle.
A church located in Springfield, the First Church of Lard Lad was formerly a Lard Lad Donuts. It is briefly seen in the episode "Holidays of Future Passed."

A major financial institution in Springfield, this bank offers credit, debit, savings accounts, loans, and mortgages. Homer and Marge frequently visit the First Bank of Springfield, where various events, including a robbery and investment mishaps, have occurred.

A predominately African American church in Springfield, this African Methodist Episcopal Church is part of the AME denomination. It is known for its community involvement and has been featured in episodes where characters seek help from Dr. Hibbert.

The federal bureau of investigation building in Springfield focuses significantly on alien invasions. Homer Simpson was taken there by agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder for testing after he believed he saw an alien.
A large mansion located at 5C International Waters Road, Fat Tony's house features numerous expensive statues. It serves as the residence of the mobster Fat Tony.
A collection of fast food restaurants, Fast-Food Boulevard was established in 1972 and was a prominent dining area in Springfield until its destruction in 2008.

An outdoor book fair in Springfield features famous authors like Stephen King and Maya Angelou, who sign books and give talks. The festival also includes appearances by Krusty the Clown, who promotes his children's book, and serves as a backdrop for Lisa's birthday celebration in the episode "Insane Clown Poppy."
A store that specializes in healing crystals, FAO Quartz offers a variety of metaphysical products.
A bacon factory owned by Farmer Billy, it produces Farmer Billy's bacon. Homer once entered a contest to win a trip to the factory by finding a golden ticket.

A luxurious bathroom located in the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, the executive washroom features opulent amenities such as a waterfall and a band of classical musicians. Homer Simpson gained access to this exclusive facility after impressing Mr. Burns, contrasting it with the poor condition of the regular restroom.

A psychological therapy clinic owned by Dr. Marvin Monroe, the Family Therapy Center offers psychological therapy services. The Simpson family once visited for a session that included electric shock therapy, and they received a refund due to their inability to stop fighting.

A gym located in Springfield's gay neighborhood, Fab Abs is where Homer once walked by while searching for Julio and Grady's apartment. He commented on the figurines in the showcase, suggesting that the owners likely never had children.

Evergreen Terrace is the residential street where the Simpson family lives, featuring their iconic house at 742 Evergreen Terrace. It is a central location in the series, often depicted in various episodes.
A performing arts camp that focuses on dance, song, and painting, Expressions was attended by Lisa for a week. Counselors include Kurt Hardwick and Ethan Ballantyne.

A restaurant in Springfield, FaceStuffers serves a unique dish of ground beef, eggs, peppers, mushrooms, and cheese smothered in tomato sauce, all served on wax paper without silverware or plates. It was closed down after a health inspector died.

A small amusement park in Springfield features a video game arcade, batting cages, and a go-kart track. The arcade offers games like skee-ball and various video games, with tokens that can be exchanged for prizes.

Evergreen Terrace is the residential street where the Simpson family lives at 742 Evergreen Terrace, with Ned Flanders residing next door at 744. The street has its own exit off the highway and has been home to notable residents, including former presidents George Bush and Gerald Ford.
A cliff located on Evergreen Terrace, it is known for an incident where Bart Simpson fell while trying to catch a football but survived with minor injuries.
A section in the parking lot of a theme park, the Ethnic Princess is where the Simpsons parked during their visit to Diz-nee Land.

A suburb of Springfield, Ethnictown is known for its immigrant population and vibrant street life. The area features various merchants, including a man selling apples and a gypsy fortuneteller, reflecting the diverse culture and community.

The Entertainment District features various attractions and entertainment venues in Springfield, including arcades and theaters. It is a lively area where residents and visitors can enjoy recreational activities.

location_name: Enriched Learning Center for Gifted Children
description: A school for gifted children, the Enriched Learning Center provides advanced education for prodigious students. Bart Simpson briefly attended this school after cheating on an IQ test but later returned to Springfield Elementary after realizing he didn't fit in.
The last bus stop of route 22A is located in the middle of the desert, where Lisa once found herself after taking the wrong bus. She expressed regret for not getting off in Crackton.

An escalator that leads to nowhere is located near the Springfield monorail, a 50-foot magnifying glass, and the popsicle stick skyscraper. It serves as a notable art structure in the city, appearing in various video games and episodes, including "Marge vs. the Monorail."

Elm Street is a road in Springfield that features the Kwik-E-Mart and the Elm Street Video Arcade. It is also the location of the old Springfield subway stop and is associated with various other establishments, including the Springfield Library and the Springfield Shopper building.
A store located in the Springfield Mall, it specializes in electronics.
The home of Elizabeth Hoover is located next to the Van Houtens on Pikeland Avenue. Apu Nahasapeemapetilon once dropped her off after a date, where she expressed her enjoyment of their time together.
A video arcade located on Elm Street in Springfield. It is featured in the episodes "Bart the General" and "A Star is Torn."
An electronics store located in the Springfield Mall, Electronics, Etc. offers a variety of electronic products.
A car dealership in Springfield, it specializes in selling electric vehicles, including the Elec-Taurus, which Homer famously totaled by driving it into the ocean.

Springfield is located on Earth, the third planet from the sun and the only known astronomical object that supports life. It is often depicted in the series, with characters like Kang and Kodos observing it from space.

The most exclusive restaurant in Springfield is located on West Oak Street, opposite a bad neighborhood. Known for its scientific approach to cooking, it features a laboratory kitchen and requires customers to pay for reservations, with gratuity added for larger parties.
East Oak Street is a rundown area in Springfield, known for its strip clubs, including Classy Girls and Silicon Alley. It has been visited by Homer Simpson and is located opposite West Oak Street.

A gourmet grocery store in Springfield, Eatie Gourmet's offers a variety of products and promotes free samples to customers. The Simpsons frequently enjoy a Sunday brunch there, taking advantage of the free samples, and Homer once bought a live lobster named Pinchy from the store.
East Springfield is a suburb of Springfield and one of its districts, known for having a local softball team. The Muntz family resides in this area.

A natural landmark in Springfield, Echo Canyon is known for its distinctive yellow appearance. The Simpsons visited this location during a family vacation, which was featured in the Tracey Ullman short "Echo Canyon."
An ear piercing business located in the Springfield Mall, it is seen when Homer is searching for a gift for Marge.

An amusement park themed around Duff Beer features attractions like the Little Land of Duff, where guests ride boats on a questionable liquid, and the Duff Beer Hall of Presidents, showcasing animatronic versions of U.S. presidents. Other attractions include the Beeramid, the Beerquarium, and various rides, all designed to provide a humorous and satirical experience.

A shop opened by Edna Krabappel after her dismissal from Springfield Elementary, Edna's Edibles was her dream venture inspired by a self-help book. The store faced financial struggles, and Edna's true passion remained teaching, which she returned to after regaining her job.

The Duff Brewery is where Duff Beer is produced and offers popular tours that often include free beer samples. It was originally located on an island in the river, but closed down when alcohol was outlawed in Springfield.
A dermatology clinic run by Dr. Zitsofsky is located next to the Happy Sailor Tattoo Parlor. Marge brought Bart here to have his tattoo removed.

The stadium where the Springfield Isotopes play baseball was originally known as Duff Stadium before being renamed Isotope Stadium. Homer Simpson famously held hunger strikes here when he learned the Isotopes were moving to Albuquerque, and the team eventually won the pennant despite a history of poor performance.
An arena in Springfield shaped like a beer bottle top, it hosts various events, including a dinosaur show called "Sitting with Dinosaurs." The venue is known as the Duff Center Arena.

location_name: Dr. Julius Hibbert, M.D. Family Practice
description: A medical clinic run by Dr. Julius Hibbert, this family practice serves patients in Springfield. The office is often confused with Springfield General Hospital, as both locations feature identical exam rooms.
A shop located in Springfield Mall, it specializes in karaoke accessories. Marge, Seymour Skinner, and Agnes Skinner visited to find songs for a school karaoke night.
A blood bank operated by Dr. Nick Riviera, it is humorously mistaken for a vampire lair by Groundskeeper Willie. The facility is featured in the episode "Lisa the Vampire."

A clinic owned by Dr. Marvin Monroe, it offered family therapy with unconventional methods, including electroshock therapy. The Simpson family briefly attended but received a refund after failing to resolve their conflicts.

Dr. Nick's Walk-In Clinic is run by Dr. Nick Riviera and is known for its slogan, "We stitch and don't snitch." The clinic is frequented by criminals and those seeking discreet medical attention, and it was notably destroyed in the episode "Trilogy of Error" due to a fireworks accident.

A popular amusement park in Springfield, Diz-Nee Land features numerous family-friendly rides and attractions. However, it is known for its unsettling costumed characters and questionable business practices, including extreme measures against guests who overstay their welcome.

A Civil War site located at Fort Springfield, this historical park was once free to the public but is now operated by a company that charges entry fees. Bart's class visits for a field trip to watch a reenactment, leading to a chaotic escape when Principal Skinner refuses to pay the fee.

The central business district of Springfield features the town square, which is home to the statue of Jebediah Springfield. Notable locations in Downtown Springfield include the Android's Dungeon, Aztec Theater, Springfield Municipal Building, and Moe's Tavern.

Downtown Springfield is a bustling area featuring various shops, businesses, and attractions. It serves as a central hub for the town's activities and is often depicted in various episodes of the series.

A gas station located across from the Springfield City Zoo, Donny's Discount Gas is owned by Donny, who is a close friend of Marge. The station is known for its low gas prices, specifically eight-tenths of a dollar.

A store located in Springfield Mall, Downer's Party Supplies sells various items for parties. Lisa Simpson and her friends intended to shop there for a school dance, but were distracted by Dingo Junction.

A donut shop located in downtown Springfield features a large brown donut resembling the colossal donut from "Treehouse of Horror VI." It is notable for its role in an episode where Homer Simpson uses the donut to stop a runaway monorail.
A district in Springfield, District 9 is home to aliens, referencing the film of the same name. It is mentioned in the episode "Holidays of Future Passed" during Bart's search for his children.

A fast food restaurant in Springfield, Dimwillie's is known for its quirky atmosphere and a mascot resembling Mayor McCheese. Homer once visited with his father to discuss his memory issues, and the family has also used the restaurant as a backdrop for humorous schemes to get free food.

A zoo-like tourist attraction in Springfield, Discount Lion Safari houses retired circus lions and former MGM mascots. It is known for quickly showcasing big cats to tourists, though it previously employed out-of-work actors in costumes until the cowardly lion scandal of 1993 ended that practice.
A district in Springfield, District 10 is an alien residence that is more luxurious than the neighboring District 9. It is featured in the episode "Holidays of Future Passed."

A stylish clothing and fashion store located in Springfield Mall, it features Dash Dingo, a mascot inspired by the video game character Crash Bandicoot. Lisa Simpson and her friends once shopped there for outfits for a school dance.
A cheap clothing store is located in Springfield, known as Discount Fashion.
A picture frame store that offers discounted prices, it is located near Springfield Elementary School. In one episode, Bart Simpson drives a tank through Springfield and targets Discount Frames.

A house on Evergreen Terrace, the Dexter family's residence is located near the Simpson home. They adopted Snowball V, Lisa's cat, who preferred their care and attention, leading to Bart visiting to retrieve his pet turtle.
A music room at Springfield Elementary School, it is used for teaching music by Dewey Largo. The appearance of the room differs from its depiction in the show's opening sequence.

This hotel restaurant in Springfield is known for its deluxe Sunday brunch. Homer once took his family there to celebrate paying their mortgage, but the outing turned chaotic when Bart and Lisa started fighting, drawing the ire of Mayor Quimby at a nearby table.
A car repair shop in Springfield, Dentz is where Raphael works. Homer took his car there for repairs after it was damaged, but found the cost to be too high.
A day-care center in Springfield, it is affected by pollution from nearby industrial facilities, contributing to environmental issues like acid rain.
A merkin shop located in Springfieldia, David's Merkins is featured in the episode "The Serfsons." It is known for selling pubic wigs and is a humorous nod to writer and producer David Mirkin.

A non-industrialized road in Springfield, Dead Weasel Road is notable for an incident where Fat Tony confronted Marge Simpson regarding a debt owed by Homer Simpson related to a pretzel wagon business scheme.

location_type: Motor vehicle registration and driver licensing
description: The Department of Motor Vehicles in Springfield handles motor vehicle registration and driver licensing. Patty and Selma work there, often depicted as bored and unhelpful, while the driving tests take place at the back of the building, where long lines are common.

Located in Springfield Mall, this children's barbershop is where Bart and Lisa once gave themselves terrible haircuts after a mishap. Bart was distracted by a game, leading to a bad cut, and in retaliation, he shaved off part of Lisa's hair, resulting in both siblings trying to hide from their peers.
A clothing shop located at Springfield's waterfront, it specializes in nautical outfits and accessories. Homer Simpson once purchased a sailor outfit from here.

Michael D'Amico is the son of Fat Tony and Anna Maria, and he is a student at Springfield Elementary School. He is characterized by his silence and is described by Sherri and Terri as the "weird kid who never says anything."
D Street is a road in Springfield that connects to Main Street and intersects with 12th Avenue.

A food market located in downtown Springfield, D'Errico's Market has been a part of the town since at least the 1980s. It is situated off the town square and has appeared in several episodes of The Simpsons.
A store located at Springfield Squidport, Crypto Barn specializes in selling codes and has the slogan "A place for codes."

A church in Springfield, the Crystal Cathedral is constructed almost entirely of glass, allowing views of the outside. It is notably featured in the episode "Natural Born Kissers," where Homer famously slides down its glass wall.
Croseus Street is located in Springfield Heights and is connected to Mammon Street. It is known for being a wealthy neighborhood where many affluent residents live.

A car dealership run by Crazy Vaclav, this lot is filled with damaged and low-quality foreign cars. Homer visits the dealership in the episode "Mr. Plow" after wrecking his own and Marge's car, where he discovers that the car he is test driving comes from a country that no longer exists.
A Chinese takeout restaurant located in the Springfield mall food court, it is named as a parody of the film "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon."

A former video rental shop located in the Towne Centre, Cropduster Video was one of the many stores where Marge had a voucher, but it has since closed down. It parodies the well-known Blockbuster video rental chain.
An ice cream parlor located in the Springfield Mall, the Creamatorium sells a variety of ice cream flavors. It is situated next to Lionel Hutz's law firm, "I Can't Believe It's a Law Firm!"

A cellphone shop located in the Springfield Mall, Crazy E.T.'s Phone Home features a name that is a pun on the famous line from the movie E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial. The store offers various mobile devices, including MyPhones at a promotional price of 20 cents.
An indoor water park in Springfield, it was formerly known as the Springfield Museum of Art.

A shady district in Springfield, Crackton is known for its unsavory reputation. Lisa once rode the bus on route 22A, passing through Crackton, and later remarked that she should have gotten off there.
A Christian Science Reading Room in Springfield is a place where religious texts are held. It was once mistakenly targeted by an angry mob who believed it was associated with natural sciences.

An arts and crafts store in Springfield, Crafty Art's is where Otto once bought airplane glue without models and later discarded the models he purchased. Homer and Bart visited to buy balsa wood for a school project, but were criticized by Principal Skinner for their choice of the Washington Monument, prompting Homer to select the more challenging Westminster Abbey model instead.
A shop in Springfield Mall, this china store specializes in selling china products, including tea sets and a Krusty teapot.

A forest in Springfield, this Christmas tree farm grows Christmas trees and is protected by a groundskeeper who uses a rifle and two hounds to deter trespassers. Homer once stole a Christmas tree from this location.

The Counter Truancy Unit (CTU) is a secretive organization located beneath Springfield Elementary School, established by Principal Seymour Skinner to combat student misbehavior. Equipped with advanced surveillance technology, the CTU employs students like Bart and Milhouse as field agents to monitor and address truancy and other issues within the school.
A child psychiatrist's office is located on Psychiatry Row in Springfield.

A district in Springfield characterized by Asian culture, it features businesses like Toys "R" Us and Bob's Big Buddha. Chinatown is known for its rivalry with the neighboring Tibet Town and has been visited by the Simpson family.
A dance club that specializes in Cuban dances, it features a sign that incorrectly translates to "Cuban Dance Palace." Tito Puente performs here in the episode "Who Shot Mr. Burns? Part Two."

A bar from the sitcom "Cheers" appears in Springfield when Homer considers drinking there after being kicked out of Moe's Tavern. He encounters characters like Sam Malone and Carla Tortelli, but is put off by their arguments.
A fine dining restaurant located in Springfield, Chez Nous is situated in the same district as The Aristocrat and Amor.

location_type: Transporting children from unsafe homes to new homes
description: A child welfare van is used to transport children from unsafe homes to new placements. In one instance, it arrived at the Simpsons' home to take Bart, Lisa, and Maggie to the Flanders' house after social workers deemed Homer and Marge unfit parents.

location_name: Chief Starving Bear Weight Loss Center
description: A weight loss camp associated with Kamp Krusty, it emphasizes difficult and painful exercises to promote weight loss. Martin Prince was sent there by his parents, which he resented.

Located near Springfield, this farm serves as the headquarters for 4-H and features cows, chickens, pigs, and extensive crop fields. Bart joined 4-H here, where he cared for animals, including his cow named Lou, and met Mary Spuckler.
The Channel 6 News Van is used by Springfield's Channel 6 to quickly respond to news events. It first appeared in the episode "Some Enchanted Evening."

The Chalmers house is the residence of Gary Chalmers and his daughter, Shauna, located across from the Springfield Zoo. Gary is a doomsday prepper who stores a large arsenal of supplies in his basement, including bulk foods, first-aid equipment, and automatic rifles.

Springfield's most popular TV channel is located next to the Springfield Box Factory and adjacent to Krustylu Studios. Kent Brockman is the main news presenter, and the channel features various shows, including the Krusty the Clown Show and children's programming.

A ballet academy for women and girls, it is owned by Chazz Busby. Marge Simpson auditioned there to fulfill her childhood dream, but after a poor performance, her daughter Lisa was offered a spot, leading to unexpected challenges and ultimately Lisa's decision to quit ballet.

location_type: Gas station, souvenir, food and bait shop
description: This general store serves as a gas station, souvenir shop, food outlet, and bait shop located along a mountain road near Catfish Lake. Homer visits the store to buy bait while Marge stretches her legs, and he learns about the legend of a giant catfish named General Sherman from a local.

A freshwater lake located in the mountains of Springfield, Catfish Lake is popular with fishermen seeking the legendary giant catfish known as General Sherman. The lake features a main cabin for couple counseling and dormitory cabins for guests, and it serves as a retreat for Homer and Marge during Reverend Lovejoy's marriage encounter weekend.

The Channel 6 helicopter is used by the news team to report on various events, with Arnie Pye covering traffic and Kent Brockman delivering news updates. It serves as a key tool for Channel 6's news coverage in Springfield.

A set of caverns in Springfield discovered by Carl's dad in 1956, the location is known for a family trip where Bart attempted to escape a nature walk. The Simpson family encountered hidden gold coins inside, leading to a confrontation with various characters, but ultimately chose to volunteer instead of pursuing greed.

A medical center in Springfield, the Center for Geriatric Medicine caters to the elderly. It gained attention during its grand opening when many seniors came to see Ben Matlock, who was unexpectedly attacked by fans.
Located in the Springfield Mall, this card shop sells greeting cards for various occasions, including birthdays.

A hotel located in Capital City, it is where Homer Simpson and Mindy Simmons stay while representing the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant at a national energy convention. The hotel features a bellhop who adds to the tension of the situation, but Homer ultimately chooses to bring Marge to the hotel instead.

An old and rundown arcade located in the Springfield Mall, Captain Blip's Zapateria features dirty and cracked game systems. Notable games include Click Clack Unipede, Monkey Kong, and a pinball game, among others.

A mental hospital in Springfield, Calmwood Mental Hospital is where Ned Flanders voluntarily commits himself after a breakdown. Homer Simpson is also admitted after being accused of imagining a character named Ray Magini, leading to a series of misunderstandings and electro-shock therapy administered by Dr. Hibbert. Notable patients include Lucille Botzcowski, John Swartzwelder, and Jay Sherman.
A small coffeehouse in Springfield, it is a popular hangout for Springfield University students, known for its poetry performances.

A candy store located near Springfield Town Square, it is owned by Mr. Dandy. The store has appeared in a few episodes, including "The Telltale Head" and "The Daughter Also Rises," and was featured in the opening sequence from seasons 2 to early 20.

A fat camp for overweight boys, Camp Flab-Away focuses on weight reduction through diet, exercise, and discipline. Notable attendees have included Mayor Quimby, Chief Wiggum, and Comic Book Guy, while Homer Simpson accidentally ended up there after falling off a cliff near a neighboring camp.
A candy shop appears in "The Serfsons," owned by an unseen character known as William Child-Eater.
A Mexican restaurant located in Springfield, Cafe de Mexico was where a young Homer worked as a member of a Mexican band.

Bus routes 22 and 22A are two of the main public transport options in Springfield. Route 22 serves key locations like the Springfield Museum and the university, while Route 22A has stops at places such as Pressboard Estates and the airport.

A casino located on an Indian reservation, it features gambling and entertainment acts. The Simpson family visits after being unable to camp at a nearby lake, where Homer takes out a second mortgage and Marge loses a significant amount of money.

Mr. Burns' mansion, located at 1000 Mammon Avenue in Springfield Heights, is a heavily fortified residence featuring a high wall, electrified fence, and a pack of attack dogs. The mansion contains 137 rooms, including a laboratory, a theater, and a wine cellar with rare artifacts, and it was once the site of the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant's annual picnic.

Owned by Charles Montgomery Burns, this drilling company was established to extract oil beneath Springfield Elementary School, leading to significant financial and structural damage to the school and surrounding areas. The operation caused the closure of Moe's Tavern due to toxic fumes, destroyed Bart's treehouse, and weakened the foundation of Springfield Retirement Castle, resulting in widespread resentment towards Burns from various Springfield residents.

A television studio produces the series "Police Cops," which features a character named Homer Simpson, leading to ridicule for the real Homer in Springfield. The studio initially considered creating a show inspired by "Titanic" and "Frasier" before settling on the cop series.

A for-profit college owned by Charles Montgomery Burns, Burns University features faculty made up of employees from the Springfield Nuclear Power Plant, including Homer Simpson, Lenny Leonard, and Carl Carson. The university's motto is "ut uberiores divites," meaning "the rich get richer," and it is known for its unconventional approach to education.
The bus depot serves as a transportation hub in Springfield where recruits of the U.S. Navy can board buses to the naval base.

A free-standing building within Springfield Cemetery, the Burns Family Mausoleum contains the graves of the Burns family, including Ebenezer Burns and the gaslight killer. It has appeared in several episodes, notably when Mr. Burns attempted to wall Homer inside it in "C.E. D'oh" and later served as a refuge for Burns in "The Great Phatsby."

A large, white, fancy home with an attached double garage and two chimneys is located across the street from the Simpsons' and Flanders' houses on Evergreen Terrace. It is currently occupied by former President Gerald Ford and has appeared in several episodes of The Simpsons, including "Two Bad Neighbors."

A fast-food restaurant, Burger Plate is where Homer and his family stop to eat while searching for Marge. Bart suggests they pretend it's his birthday to get free food, leading Homer to declare it a birthday celebration for the whole family.
A repair store specializing in chimney services, Broken-Home Chimney Repair is seen by Marge Simpson while driving.
This city bureau grants licenses and permits to Springfield's citizens, including for activities like selling lemonade. Lisa and Bart visited to obtain permission for their sidewalk lemonade stand.

A box fort built by Bart and Lisa in their backyard resembles a castle made from shipping boxes. After a confrontation with Raphael, a delivery man who wanted the boxes back, a battle ensued between Bart and Lisa's makeshift army and Raphael's team of delivery workers, ultimately leading to the fort's destruction with a garden hose.

A car wash located in Springfield, Buckingham Palace Quick Lube features a humorous design with a character dressed as a queen's guard. It is notable for an incident where Maggie mistook the guard's furry hat for Marge's hair.

The Bouvier House is where Marge Simpson grew up with her parents, Clancy and Jackie Bouvier, and her twin sisters, Patty and Selma. The current owner sells rabbit carcasses, and Marge and Homer lived there briefly before moving to an apartment.

A bookshop in Springfield, Books! Books! and Additional Books! features a variety of titles, including works on relationships and UFOs. Homer and Marge once visited to find a book to improve their marriage, while Bart and Lisa explored their own interests, leading to humorous situations involving the books they chose.
A hardware superstore in Springfield, Builders' Barn is a parody of Home Depot. It is featured in episodes such as "Don't Fear the Roofer" and "Please Homer, Don't Hammer 'Em."
An electronics store in Springfield, it sells televisions, satellite dishes, and other audiovisual equipment. The exterior resembles the Try-N-Save store, featuring satellite dishes above the sign.

A self-storage unit in Springfield, Broken Dreams Storage Lockers was once home to Sideshow Bob and Gil Gunderson. After his release from prison, Bob used the locker to plot his revenge against Bart, while Gil also sought revenge and interrupted Bob's plans.

A car dealership in Springfield, Homer Simpson briefly worked at Boris' Car Loft after being fired from the nuclear power plant, where he later purchased an antique ambulance. The name is a play on actor Boris Karloff.

A large bookstore in Springfield, Bookaccino's features at least four floors and a café on the first floor. It is known for its extensive collection of books and has appeared in several episodes of The Simpsons.

A bookstore located in the Springfield Mall, it first appeared when Homer was searching for a birthday present for Marge. The store has been depicted in various episodes, including "Homer's Phobia" and "Peeping Mom."

A large theme park made almost entirely of Blocko building blocks features three areas: Rectangle Land, Cube Country, and Squaresville. The Simpson family visited Blockoland, which parodies Legoland, a chain of amusement parks based on the Danish toy brand LEGO.
Sideshow Bob resides in a Victorian-style home in Springfield. In the "Treehouse of Horror XXVI" segment, he takes Bart's body back to this house after killing him.
A store located in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, it specializes in selling Blocko sets. Lisa once visited the shop seeking a plain Blocko set, but was informed that it was not available.

A Hawaiian restaurant in Springfield, Bob's Big Poi closed down after going out of business. Homer retrieved a discarded tiki statue from the curb and modified it to burp fire by rerouting the kitchen gas into its mouth.
A store that sells whalebone corsets, Blowhole Republic is frequented by characters like Patty, Selma, and Comic Book Guy. The name parodies Banana Republic.

An RV dealership run by Cowboy Bob, it sells various recreational vehicles, including the impressive "Ultimate Behemoth." Notable customers include Ned Flanders and Homer Simpson, with Homer often making poor purchasing decisions despite his family's concerns.
Located at Springfield Squidport, this shop is known for its jello shooters. Homer and Marge visited the shop, where Homer reassured Marge about their children at home.

location_type: Birthplace where Jebediah Springfield was born
description: The birthplace of Jebediah Springfield is the house where he was born. It was destroyed when the Springfield monorail crashed into it, and although it was rebuilt, it faced further destruction when Moe's house fell on top of it.

Matt Groening was born in 1954 in Portland, Oregon, not in a log cabin. In an episode of The Simpsons, Homer drives through a building resembling Groening's birthplace after dropping Bart off at a boot camp.

A location in Springfield where various kinds of birds can be observed, the bird sanctuary is a place Marge longs to visit. However, during a chaotic incident at Itchy & Scratchy Land, the birds at the sanctuary become aggressive, attacking visitors due to a lack of food.

A campsite for billionaires, this location is frequented by wealthy individuals like Mr. Burns and Jeff Bezos. It is adjacent to the millionaire camp, and entry requires a net worth of over one billion dollars; those who fall below this threshold risk being demoted. Activities include food fights, archery on famous paintings, and poker games, while residents live in cottages displaying their current wealth.

A house owned by the Bin Laden family is located in Springfield, where Bart befriends Bashir Bin Laden after smelling food from their garden. Homer initially misinterprets the family's activities as suspicious, believing they are involved in terrorism, but later discovers they are simply involved in a construction project.
Located in the Springfield Mall, this bikini shop sells a variety of bikinis and is situated next to Ren's Meat. It appears in the episode "Simpson and Delilah."

A hotel offering cabin accommodations for tourists, Bill & Edwina's Tour-Rest Cabins is located near Potato Rock National Park. Guests receive a complimentary souvenir booklet about Potato Rock during their stay.

An internet animation studio, betterthantv.com produced various cartoons, including Bart's comic strip "Angry Dad," which became a brief sensation after being adapted into a cartoon. The studio eventually went out of business due to financial issues, but years later, Bart collaborated with Herman Millwood to turn "Angry Dad" into a successful movie.

A theater in Springfield, Big T Theatre hosts various events, including concerts featuring artists like Ice-T and Booker T. The venue is marked by a prominent red letter "T" on its signage and was considered by Springfield residents as a potential hiding place for hidden money.
A bikini store located in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glen, it is situated near XO and Puttering Barn. The shop is named Bikini Atol, a playful reference to Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands.
A bike track in Springfield is where Bart takes Martin to teach him how to be cool. It is featured in the episode "Bart Gets an F."

A restaurant in Springfield, Big T Burgers & Fries specializes in burgers and fries, with a sign featuring a large red letter "T." It was considered by Springfield residents as a potential hiding place for hidden money, but it was not actually the location.

A traveling museum exhibition featuring historical and cultural items, including Abraham Lincoln's hat and Fonzie's jacket, visited the Springfield Convention Center. Homer Simpson accidentally damaged the Bill of Rights during the exhibition and was required to repay his debts.

An old-school drive-in burger joint, Berger's Burgers features waitresses on roller skates. Marge worked there before and briefly after her marriage to Homer to support the family when he lost his job.

An organization associated with the Springfield government, Bear Patrol was established in response to citizen concerns after a bear sighting. Despite its heavy funding and use of vans and aircraft, it has not had a significant impact, as bears are nearly nonexistent in Springfield.
A clothing store located at Springfield Squidport, it specializes in beachwear.

location_name: Baseball Announcer (Brother from the Same Planet)
