description: The baseball announcer works at Springfield War Memorial Stadium and announces a game on Tomato Day, where he delays the game due to a speech by a communist party recruiter.
A motel located in Terror Lake, it is where Sideshow Bob plotted his revenge on Bart Simpson.

A bowling alley in Springfield, Barney's Bowlarama is owned by Al Gumble, Barney Gumble's uncle. It has been destroyed and rebuilt multiple times, including after a fire and a hurricane, and served as a venue for church sermons following a court case won by Homer.
A barn shop located in Springfieldia, Barns for Nobles is a parody of Barnes & Noble. Homer and Lisa pass by it while trying to earn gold pieces for the amulet of Warmfyre.
Bart's treehouse is located in the backyard of 742 Evergreen Terrace and serves as a hangout spot for Bart and his friends, where they often read comics.

A street in Springfield, Bart Boulevard is home to Springfield Elementary School and Springfield General Hospital. It is notable for an incident involving a major car crash that occurred after Bart stole the street sign.
A mental health facility located at the waterfront, it specializes in helping individuals manage their anger and express it constructively.
An old, rundown bar located in a less affluent area of Springfield, it is featured when the Simpsons search for a cheap Christmas tree after Homer spends the family's money on an astrolabe.
An apartment complex inhabited by Barney Gumble, it is known for being dirty and in disrepair. The apartment overlooks the Springfield Penitentiary and is located above Moe's Tavern.
A surgery center and barber shop, Barber Hibbert's Surgery is located in Springfield. It is run by Dr. Hibbert, who has treated various characters, including Krusty the Clown and Jacqueline Bouvier.

An apartment complex in Springfield, Bachelor Arms is where Kirk Van Houten stayed during his divorce from Luann. The building is known for its high rate of suicides, with a sign that counts the days since the last incident.
A clothing store located in the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, it parodies the real-life store Banana Republic.
A clothing store located in Springfieldia, Banana Monarchy is featured in the episode "The Serfsons." It is a parody of the retail chain Banana Republic.

The office of Lucky Jim, a bondsman, is a rundown building with a failing neon sign. He employs tough individuals like Wolf the Bounty Hunter to track down those who skip bail, including Homer Simpson.
This bondsman office is located across the street from Sleazy Sam's Payday Loans and next to Lotto 'n' Liquor. It appears in the episode "Ned 'n Edna's Blend."

A movie theater located off the town square next to a pawn shop features atmospheric decor inspired by the Aztec civilization. It has premiered several films, including installments of the Space Mutants series and "Itchy & Scratchy: The Movie," and has a strict no refunds policy for disgruntled viewers.

A crime-ridden section of Springfield, the Badlands is known for its rampant illegal activities and features a large landfill. The area's sign even allows for high-speed chases, highlighting its lawless reputation.
A dentistry in Springfield, B. Hoffman Dentist is where Homer and Marge took Bart and Lisa after their graduation from Rommelwood Military School, instead of the promised trip to Disneyland.
An elementary school featured in the movie "Springfield of Tomorrow," where Junior studies history. In the film, Mel and his wife pick up Junior using a robot arm.
A scrap-metal junkyard, the Auto Graveyard is where Truckasaurus was stored before Bart reactivated it.
An erotic bakery is run by an Irish man named Patrick Farally, where Marge once worked after he recognized her baking talent. Notable customers include Patty, Selma, and Dr. Hibbert.
A top-secret military base, Area 51-A is where Lisa accidentally ended up after taking the wrong bus. She initially thought it was Area 51, but a guard clarified its true identity.

A fine dining restaurant where Homer and Marge have dined, it is known for its expensive menu featuring roast beef and wine, as well as a buffet table and a chocolate fountain. The restaurant also offers a signature view of Springfield.
This bus stop is located at the Army Proving Grounds in Springfield. It was mentioned when Lisa was riding a bus and listening to the names of various bus stops.
A salon owned by Homer, Are We Hair Yet? primarily catered to women and was located where Honey Me Mine once stood. The name is a pun on the phrase "Are we there yet?"
A course was held for Springfield residents when the town was divided into two area codes, 636 and 939. Homer, Lenny, and Carl attended Area Code Camp for two weeks to learn about the changes.
Apu's Taj Mahal is the residence of Apu, his wife Manjula, and their 64 grandchildren, all of whom are the offspring of their octuplets.
A store located in Springfield's gay neighborhood, it specializes in selling mopeds. Homer once walked by while searching for Julio and Grady's apartment.
A shop located at the Promenade on the Grove in Springfield Heights, it specializes in cultural artifacts.
Apu's apartment is the residence of Apu Nahasapeemapetilon, his wife Manjula, and their eight children. Apu often prioritizes his work at the Kwik-E-Mart over spending time at home with his family.
A veterinary service in Springfield, the animal hospital treated Homer Simpson after he experienced belly pain from being hit by a cannonball at Hullabalooza.

A company provides animal assistants to disabled individuals. Homer Simpson sought a helper monkey from them after seeing Apu with his, but was denied due to not being disabled; he later brought his grandfather Abe to adopt a monkey named Mojo, which was eventually returned due to its poor health.
An antiques store located at Springfield Squidport sells various vintage items.

location_name: Another Government Highway Project That Will Never End
description: A highway construction project on rural route 9, it connects to Suicidal Moron Pass. The project is humorously depicted as never-ending.

location_name: The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop
description: A comic book shop in Springfield, it is run by Jeffrey Albertson, known as Comic Book Guy. The Android's Dungeon & Baseball Card Shop offers a wide selection of comic books and collectibles, and is located on the town square next to Skip's Diner.

Springfield's most luxurious hotel features fifty-seven themed fantasy suites, including the Smokey and the Bandit suite and the Oval Office. Notable guests have included celebrity lion tamers Gunter and Ernst, as well as Mayor Quimby.
This health facility is where Homer and Marge took Santa's Little Helper for therapy. It is accessible via bus route 22.
A fine dining restaurant located in Springfield, Amoré is situated in the same district as The Aristocrat and Chez Nous.

A recurring group of Springfield townspeople, known as the angry mob, often reacts violently to minor issues, typically targeting the Simpson family or other characters. Members include various residents, such as Abe Simpson, and they are known for their mob mentality, often wielding torches and pitchforks during their pursuits.

A doll store located at the Towne Centre at Springfield Glenne, it features a Princess Café where girls can have tea parties with their dolls. Lenny visits the store after the Simpsons decline to shop with him, and the cashier offers to assist him.
A store in Springfield, America's Apparel appeared in "The Day the Earth Stood Cool" and replaced Sprawl-Mart as hipsters from Portland transformed the town.
A store located in Springfield's gay neighborhood, it specializes in selling knives. Homer once walked by while searching for Julio and Grady's apartment.

A store that sells bowling balls and accessories, Alley McBalls is where Homer purchased a blue bowling ball by selling his Apple shares during a flashback in the episode "Four Regrettings and a Funeral."

location_name: America's Most Armed and Dangerous Office
location_type: TV studioMain set for America's Most Armed and Dangerous
description: The office serves as the main filming location for the show "America's Most Armed and Dangerous."

American Shipping Services provides free shipping boxes to companies, with Raphael working as a delivery man there. Bart and Lisa once ordered numerous boxes to build a fort, leading to a conflict with Raphael, who returned with an army of delivery personnel to reclaim the boxes.

Abe and Selma's house is where Abe Simpson and Selma Bouvier lived with their adopted daughter, Ling. While Selma worked, Abe took care of Ling but caused chaos in the kitchen, leading to a series of mishaps that contributed to their eventual separation.

location_type: StoreThe Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers base
description: The abandoned store served as the first headquarters for the Ancient Mystic Society of No Homers, a breakaway group formed by former members of the Stonecutters to exclude Homer. It was originally a Baskin-Robbins ice cream store before being taken over by the society.

A Taste of Springfield is a food festival featuring booths from many of the town's restaurants, set in an outdoor venue. The event was notable for a failed assassination attempt on Homer Simpson, who was then a food critic, when a chef attempted to poison him with an éclair, leading to chaos and an explosion at Hans Moleman's gruel stand.

The abandoned aqueduct is a site for illegal drag racing in Springfield, where characters like Grampa and Jasper Beardly have participated in races. The tunnel's exit leads to a cliff near the Simpsons' house.

This feed lot for cows is located on Rural Route 9 next to the slaughterhouse in Springfield. Bart's cow, Lou, was taken here after winning at the Springfield County Fair, but Bart and Lisa later rescued him with the help of animal rights activists.

The A-Maize-Ing Maize Maze is an electrified corn maze featured at a harvest festival. The Simpson family got lost in it, with Homer eventually being rescued by Santa's Little Helper after a series of misadventures.

The Flanders family resides at 744 Evergreen Terrace, next door to the Simpsons at 742 Evergreen Terrace. The house, which features a pink-purple exterior and religious imagery inside, was destroyed by a hurricane and poorly rebuilt, leading to an emotional outburst from Ned Flanders in the episode "Hurricane Neddy."

The mansion at 743 Evergreen Terrace is located across the street from the Simpson family's home at 742 Evergreen Terrace. It features multiple rooms, including a hall, living room, study, garage, kitchen, and bedroom.

The blue detached home at 754 Evergreen Terrace belongs to Professor John Frink, located in the Pressboard Estates district of Springfield. It features a flying gorilla attached garage, solar panels, and a basement used as a lab for his experiments.
The Simpson family's house is located at 742 Evergreen Terrace in Springfield and serves as the main setting for the series. It first appeared in the short "Good Night."

This location, featured in The Simpsons Movie, is a wooden building that Homer collides with while being tossed around by a wrecking ball. It serves as a visual representation of the phrase "between a rock and a hard place."

The Brown House, located at 740 Evergreen Terrace, is a residential property next to the Simpson family's home at 742 Evergreen Terrace. It has been inhabited by various families, including the Winfields, the Powers, and a disguised Sideshow Bob, and has seen multiple occupants over the years, including Ted Flanders and his daughters.

A medical office located on Psychiatry Row, it is a parody of the 99 Cents Only Stores chain and is situated next to Quack in the Box. Marge and Homer pass by this location in the episode "The Girl Who Slept Too Little."
The residence at 725 Evergreen Terrace belongs to Reverend Lovejoy, the local pastor in Springfield.

A block of apartments located in the Pressboard Estate district, one of the units at 82 Evergreen Terrace was rented by Edna Krabappel, Bart's teacher, until she moved in with Ned Flanders. The layout of the apartments has shown inconsistencies in various episodes.

The Wiggum family resides at 732 Evergreen Terrace, where Chief Wiggum keeps a cupboard filled with police equipment and files on Springfield residents, which his son Ralph is forbidden to access. The house's design varies throughout the series, sometimes depicted as a small one-story home and other times as a larger two-story structure.
A subway station located on 3rd Street in Springfield. It appears in episodes such as "Bart Sells His Soul" and "Postcards from the Wedge."

A large suburban house, 734 Evergreen Terrace is the residence of the Hibbert family, situated between the Wiggum and Brown houses. It has been featured in various episodes, including "Bye Bye Nerdie," where Homer baby-proofed it, and "Grift of the Magi," where Bart and Lisa caroled there as part of a Christmas distraction.
A giant magnifying glass located in downtown Springfield, it is primarily known for burning down the popsicle stick skyscraper.

An abandoned factory located at 35 Industry Way was won by Bart Simpson for one dollar at a government tax seizure auction. The factory, which previously housed adding machines and a coffee vending machine, became a playground for Bart and Milhouse until it ultimately collapsed.
A rundown block of flats located in Springfield, 652 8th Avenue is home to residents Kurt Hardwick and Ethan Ballantyne, with a tramp often found outside.

A discount store sells all items for 33 cents, primarily featuring discontinued, factory second, and recalled products. The Simpsons shop there to save money for a family vacation, and Homer suffers from red tide poisoning after consuming expired plankton from the store.
Moe Szyslak lives at 57 Walnut Street, which is a residential house. It has been featured in various episodes, including "A Star is Burns" and "Days of Wine and D'oh'ses."

The Spuckler house, located at 27 Rural Route 9, is home to Cletus and Brandine Spuckler and their numerous children. Cletus is known for his rural lifestyle and is often depicted as an inbred character in the series.

The Muntz family resides at 19 Fish Smell Drive, located on the east side of Springfield. Their house features a wooden interior and is stereotypical of a hillbilly home, with Nelson's room containing a bed, a guitar, and various propaganda posters.
A subway station is located on 3rd Street in Springfield.
A street located near Springfield Harbor, 257th Street features an apartment building where Grandma Van Houten resides. It is depicted in the episode "Bart Sells His Soul."
A shop located in Springfield Mall, it specializes in selling calendars from the year 1987.
A street in Springfield, 181st Street is notable for a scene where Chief Wiggum calms a derelict and Bart intimidates Ralph for his soul while in a police car.

In 2013, a tornado struck Springfield, first noticed by Lisa. The tornado caused significant destruction, sucking up characters like Homer, Marge, and Santa's Little Helper, and destroying locations such as the National Bank of Springfield and Lard Lad Donuts.
One of the streets in Springfield, 12th Avenue features the Springfield Bridge.
An abandoned house at 123 Fake Street was mistakenly used by Marge as a fake address when she called the police. When the police arrived, they found Bart and Milhouse hiding illegal fireworks inside.
One of the streets in Springfield, 156th Street is where Bart travels in search of his soul.

The houseboat at 1 Ocean View Drive is the residence of Judge Constance Harm and her pet seal, Poncho. Homer and Marge once attempted to prank the judge by posting a banner on her boat, which led to a series of events that resulted in the boat sinking.
